orig_title: Reports: 'streamlined' UK asylum process to replace interview with questionnaire for five nationalities
text: According to reports, The United Kingdom Home Office today is to begin issuing questionnaires in place of official interviews to determine refugee status for some 12,000 asylee hopefuls from Afghanistan, Eritrea, Libya, Syria and Yemen who applied before last summer. The forms are part of Prime Minister Rishi Sunak's effort to clear the nation's 92,000 asylum claim-'legacy backlog' by year end. While standard security, criminal, and health checks will continue, officials will scrap the face-to-face interview step to "streamline" processing for five nationalities whose claim acceptance rate is already above 95%. The document, which media reports range from ten to 32 pages with 40 to 50 questions, "must be completed in English", the government recommending "online translation tools" if needed. A leaked internal letter seen by Sky News says "failure to return the questionnaire without reasonable explanation may result in an individual's asylum claim being withdrawn in line with the published policy", but the government will provide a reminder after the deadline and consider extensions. Officials tell BBC News every claim will be assessed meritocratically, with the reporting no one will be refused "based solely on the response of the questionnaire". A similar fast-track system backed by the British Red Cross in September 2021 for 3,000 Afghan refugees was reportedly rejected by Prime Minister Boris Johnson over fears it would amount to amnesty, which the Home Office today rejects, and strain the UK's welfare and housing systems. Labour's Shadow Home Secretary Yvette Cooper stated her party has supported the idea "for months", and stated it was "damning that the Home Office isn't doing this already [...] including for safe countries like Albania" after the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees "recommended it two years ago. She continued: "Labour has a common-sense plan to fast-track cases, get return agreements in place so unsuccessful claims can be quickly and safely returned, and take much stronger action against the criminal gangs driving dangerous small boat crossings. Sunak has made tackling migration one of his main priorities, with laws banning illegal migrants from claiming asylum in the UK expected next month. The Home Office letter reads "we may extend the use of the questionnaire as a means to gather additional information from other claimants awaiting an asylum decision in due course", but no current plans to expand the scheme exist. On Wednesday, Home Secretary Suella Braverman told GB News: "It's clear that we have an unsustainable situation in towns and cities around our country [...] because of the overwhelming numbers of individuals arriving here illegally and our legal duties to accommodate them". But media have stated the questionnaires attract criticism both for making it easier for some asylum seekers to obtain the right to live and work in the UK, and for presenting a burden on those who may not speak English or have access to help or legal counsel. The Guardian cited examples of complicated questions with over fifty words, including: "Were you subject to human trafficking (the recruitment, transportation, transfer, harbouring or receipt of individuals through force, fraud or deception, with the aim of exploiting them for profit) or modern slavery (severe exploitation of other individuals for personal or commercial gain) during your journey to or after you arrived in the UK? It quoted critics like immigration barrister Colin Yeo, and Joint Council for the Welfare of Immigrants campaigner Caitlin Boswell, with Boswell stating: "People fleeing desperate circumstances clearly need this government to make quicker and fairer asylum decisions, but this latest move from government is clumsy, unthinking and could put individuals's safety at risk. "No one's right to refuge should be jeopardised because they weren't able to fill in an unwieldy form in a language they don't speak. After the leak, CEO of the Refugee Council Enver Solomon told Sky News any process "must be well thought out": "Moves to reduce the backlog are welcome but the answer is not yet more bureaucratic hurdles and threats of applications being withdrawn. "After living in worry and uncertainty for months and even years without hearing anything about their claims, it cannot then be fair or reasonable to expect individuals to complete a lengthy form only in English in a matter of weeks especially for those who don't have access to legal advice and don't speak English. During Prime Minister's Questions Wednesday, Sunak defended the government's record whilst promising a "formal update" from Braverman is forthcoming: "The Home Secretary and I are working intensely and as quickly as possible to bring forward that legislation [...] in the meantime our deals with Albania and France are already yielding benefits [...] we want a system whereby if someone arrives in our country illegally they will not be able to stay. Stay tuned for more updates on this story.

orig_title: Tensions increase as US recovers downed Chinese "spy balloon" debris
text: According to reports, The United States revealed Monday a "significant" portion of the payload of a Chinese high-altitude balloon shot down over the Atlantic Ocean on February 4 had been recovered. Ryder stated the balloon was floating eastward at about 60,000 feet (18,300 meters) above the central United States and demonstrating a capability to maneuver using motors and propellers. Ryder explained it was "well above civilian air traffic [...] we do assess at this time that it does not pose a physical threat to individuals on the ground. Presidential press secretary Karine Jean-Pierre called the balloon's trajectory over the US a "clear violation of our sovereignty. US Secretary of State Antony Blinken, scheduled to leave for Beijing late February 4, canceled the trip, declaring the balloon's entrance into US airspace an "irresponsible act" during a call with Chinese diplomat Wang Yi. The meeting was to have included discussions about reinforcing communications and easing tensions between the two countries. Advisors told US President Joe Biden the military should wait until the balloon was over water before shooting it down, so the debris would not threaten civilians. Meanwhile, a second balloon flew across Latin America; on February 3, Ryder confirmed that, saying: "We now assess it is another Chinese surveillance balloon. In a February 6 statement, China admitted ownership of the second balloon as well, countering it, too, was a civilian weather balloon forced off its path by wind. orig_title: Pakistan reverses block on Wikimedia projects, including Wikipedia
text: According to reports, On Monday, Pakistan's government reversed its block on all Wikimedia Foundation projects, including the online encyclopedia Wikipedia. Marriyum Aurangzeb, Pakistani Minister for Information and Broadcasting, tweeted Sharif's decree, which stated: "The prime minister is pleased to direct that the website (Wikipedia) may be restored with immediate effect". On February 1, the PTA stated "the services of Wikipedia have been degraded [] for 48 hours" and gave the Foundation until Friday night to remove "unlawful" content from its websites. The PTA warned it might block Wikipedia if "[the] Foundation failed to comply with the takedown orders". A Wikimedia Foundation press release on Friday revealed the block; PTA released a statement confirming it: "An opportunity of hearing was additionally provided, but, the platform neither complied by removing the blasphemous content nor appeared before the Authority". The Foundation tweeted on Monday, "Wikipedia is no longer blocked in Pakistan. We are happy to say we have confirmed that traffic on @Wikipedia and other Wikimedia websites from Pakistan has resumed as before. The Pakistani government has repeatedly blocked access to certain websites for its citizens, drawing fire from free speech activists, according to . In 2010, Pakistan blocked Facebook amid the backlash to Internet users' advocacy for the creation of depictions of Muhammad; it eventually repealed the block. The government additionally blocked YouTube from 2012 to 2016 for hosting a movie about Muhammad, and asked the site in 2020 to prevent Pakistanis from accessing "objectionable" videos. Additionally, the PTA earlier banned dating applications such as Tinder and Grindr, citing "immoral" components, and has repeatedly blocked TikTok, a Chinese social media application people in Pakistan alone have acquired millions of times. orig_title: "A commonsense proposal": Wikinews interviews Michelle Tilley, Campaign Director for Yes on 820
text: According to reports, {{DISPLAYTITLE:"A commonsense proposal": Wikinews interviews Michelle Tilley, Campaign Director for Yes on 820}} On March 7, voters in the US state of Oklahoma will decide on State Question 820, the Marijuana Legalization Initiative. If the initiative passes, adults 21 and older could own up to an ounce (28.35 grams) of recreational marijuana and cultivate "not more than six (6) mature marijuana plants and six (6) seedlings" in their homes, and some convictions for marijuana possession could be expunged. The state's profits earned by taxing marijuana transactions would fund the Oklahoma Medical Marijuana Authority, while the rest would be split between: the state's fund pool (30%), programs in public schools to improve student success, extracurricular activities, and decrease drug abuse (30%), governmental and nonprofit programs to counter drug abuse (20%), courts (10%), and the local government where the transaction occurred (10%). Wikinews emailed interview questions to the Yes campaign on January 6; Michelle Tilley, their Campaign Director, responded on January 11. The following is the interview with Tilley. Interview with Michelle Tilley First, can you briefly explain what you see as the main problem(s) with Oklahoma's current marijuana laws? Oklahoma currently allows residents to apply for a medical marijuana license, with a doctor's referral, from the Oklahoma Medical Marijuana Authority. This means that marijuana is illegal for adults to consume or possess for non-medical purposes. State Question 820, which the individuals of Oklahoma will vote on this March 7, 2023, proposes to safely legalize, regulate, and tax recreational marijuana for adults over 21 years of age. Legalizing marijuana for adults over 21 would have a significant and positive economic and fiscal impact for the state. Passage of SQ 820 would lead to the collection of tens of millions in new tax revenue in the first year of implementation and hundreds of millions in the first five years. This revenue could offer a significant boost to Oklahoma's underfunded public schools, law enforcement agencies, mental health programs and other priorities. Furthermore, local economies, in every town, large and small, would benefit from good paying jobs and new sales tax dollars that will stay in local communities. Passage of SQ 820 would also represent a positive alignment of Oklahoma's public safety priorities: Law enforcement would be able to devote their limited resources away from low level marijuana offenses, focusing instead on serious crimes. Meanwhile, Oklahoma would become a more just state, because 820 allows Oklahomans with old convictions for low level marijuana crimes to remove those offenses from their criminal history, making it easier to find gainful employment and move on with their lives. Finally, SQ 820 would provide a sensible and safe regulatory framework. Under SQ 820, all marijuana products would be tested, safe, and only available to adults aged 21 and older (unless you have a medical marijuana card). Each product will be analyzed to determine potency and screened for unsafe contaminants. What would Initiative 820 do to rectify these problems? See above How would you respond to claims that legalizing marijuana would create a "slippery slope" towards total legalization of drugs, and, in fact, do you think that would be a bad thing? SQ 820 does not propose to legalize any substances other than marijuana. What or who are some businesses, organizations, or individuals supporting Initiative 820 who voters might not expect to support it, and why are they? This includes parents who want more resources for their kids' schools, patients concerned about the cost or availability of health care resources, and individuals who don't want to run over potholes on the way to work; Businesses and families who know their communities can benefit from the good jobs and investment of a multi-billion dollar industry; Members of the legal and law enforcement community who are tired of wasting their time and resources on low level marijuana offenses instead of fighting more serious criminal activity; and Adults interested in using cannabis for non-medical purposes. Lastly, why do you think Initiative 820 will succeed? SQ 820 will succeed because Oklahomans want more resources for priorities like education; we want the economic boost that comes with supporting a new, multi-billion dollar industry; and we want to reap the public safety benefits that come with refocusing law enforcement on dangerous criminal activity instead of minor marijuana offenses. This is a commonsense proposal that will help make Oklahoma a stronger, more prosperous and more just state. Stay tuned for more updates on this story.

orig_title: "Energized and excited": Chris Hipkins becomes 41st Prime Minister of New Zealand
text: According to reports, On January 25, Chris Hipkins succeeded Jacinda Ardern as prime minister of New Zealand after the latter's 'shock' resignation on January 19. At the swearing-in ceremony in Wellington, Governor-General Dame Cindy Kiro, King Charles III's representative, appointed Hipkins prime minister and Carmel Sepuloni the first Pasifika New Zealander deputy prime minister. Hipkins, 44, was elected to replace Ardern as leader of the Labour Party unopposed on January 22. He is expected to lead the party into the October elections amidst economic challenges and two years of declining Labour popularity against a stronger conservative opposition. In his first speech as prime minister, Hipkins, who under Ardern led New Zealand's response to COVID-19, said: "This is the biggest privilege and responsibility of my life [...] I'm energized and excited by the challenges that lie ahead. Hipkins said the cost of living was an "absolute priority" for the new ministry but ruled out announcing specifics "only a couple of hours into the job". Quarterly consumer spending figures published that morning showed New Zealand's inflation rate remained high at 7.2%, led by increases in housing and food costs. "New Zealanders will absolutely see in the coming weeks and months the cost of living is right at the heart of our work program [...] It is the number one priority that we are facing as a government and they will see tangible evidence of this", he told reporters, but said "I'm not going to be so hasty as to make things up on the fly". Sepuloni expressed her gratitude for the position and saluted Hipkins' victory. On Sunday, Sepuloni, of Samoan, Tongan, and New Zealand European descent, said she "want[s] to acknowledge the significance of this for our Pacific community". On Sunday, Hipkins pledged to fight what he described as a "pandemic of inflation": "COVID-19 and the global pandemic created a health crisis. Now it's created an economic one and that's where my government's focus will be". Christopher Luxon, the Leader of the Opposition, said he texted Hipkins and Sepuloni his congratulations, but declared the Ardern government "failed spectacularly", and Hipkins promised only 'more of the same'. Despite previous cabinet positions as Minister of Education and Minister of Police, Hipkins became known as the 'architect' behind New Zealand's COVID-19 policy. Nevertheless, according to the Associated Press, he and other party members were obscure compared to Ardern, a "global icon for the left". Ardern said she resigned after serving almost fifteen years as a member of parliament because she didn't "have it in the tank [to continue]. She is expected to remain an MP before resigning in April, to prevent a by-election before the October vote. In her last event as prime minister on Tuesday, Ardern said individuals were "the joy of the job". On Wednesday morning, staffers and supporters gathered to say goodbye and hug her as she walked out of the Parliament building. William and Catherine, the Prince and Princess of Wales, tweeted Ardern and her family their gratitude "for your friendship, leadership and support over the years, not least at the time of my grandmother's death. Related news Sister links Sources Stay tuned for more updates on this story.

orig_title: Actor Alan Cumming returns OBE for British Empire's 'toxicity'
text: According to reports, On Friday, Scottish theatre and film actor and producer Alan Cumming said how "the British Empire profited at the expense (and death) of indigenous peoples around the world" affected his decision to return the OBE he received in 2009. For his 58th birthday, the two-time Tony awardee revealed on Instagram "the misgivings I have being associated with the toxicity of empire" outweighed the "great good" his receiving of the order represented for the LGBT community. Cumming was bestowed the chivalric honour, which stands for 'Order of the British Empire', as part of Queen Elizabeth II's Birthday Honours for his work as an actor and activist "for equal rights for the gay and lesbian community". Made a US citizen in 2008, Cumming was an outspoken critic of the since-repealed Defense of Marriage Act that forbade federal recognition of same-sex marriage, and the 'don't ask, don't tell' policy that prevented openly LGBT individuals from serving in the US Armed Forces. At the time, he said: "I see this honour as encouragement to go on fighting for what I believe is right and for what I take for granted as a UK citizen. Thank you to the Queen and those who make up her birthday honours list for bringing attention to the inaction of the US government on this issue. It makes me very proud to be British, and galvanised as an American. However, the laws' repeal and "conversations about the role of the monarchy" and legacy of British colonialism begun after Elizabeth II's death in September convinced him "the great good the award brought to the LGBTQ+ cause back in 2009 is now less potent than the misgivings I have being associated with the toxicity of empire. In the past, other celebrities have returned OBEs in protest of social issues: in 2020, Welsh actor Michael Sheen revealed he returned his received in 2009 over the "tortured history" between Wales and the UK. Musician John Lennon returned his lesser MBE in 1969 over the UK's involvement in the Nigerian Civil War and support for the US in Vietnam. Cumming's film credits include and the trilogy. He received his Tony Awards for producing the musical (2022) and appearing in (1998). In 2019, he expressed his pride in his work on the television series where he was in the star role of the first US network drama to have a gay lead character. Posting on Instagram, he remembered the show, which was cancelled after two series, for being where "millions of individuals will have seen a same-sex marriage portrayed for the first time". orig_title: UK Treasury considering plans for digital pound, economic secretary says
text: According to reports, Andrew Griffith, Economic Secretary to HM Treasury, told members of the United Kingdom House of Commons Tuesday the government was considering a "digital pound", with public consultations on the attributes and regulation of digital assets expected in the coming weeks. Speaking before Parliament's Treasury Select Committee, Griffith reported the government was "a long way down the road [...] to establish a regime for the wholesale use, for payment purposes, of stablecoins", cryptocurrencies less susceptible to price fluctuations by being pegged to traditional assets. While affirming commitments for the UK to become a cryptocurrency hub, Griffith stated creating regulations for a digital pound would be "a long lead-time activity. Griffith told the Committee the first use of a digital pound would likely be for settling financial transactions wholesale, but suggested public policy considerations meant a private, fiat-based stablecoin could probably do the job first. Nevertheless, he stated: "We have got to get them [public policy issues] right. I would rather be right than be first". Griffith expressed the desire that a regulatory regime, Britain's first for crypto assets, would be included in the Financial Services and Markets Bill, which is being debated in the House of Lords. He stated embracing "potentially disruptive game-changing technology" could "challenge but additionally turbocharge" the UK's fintech and financial industries. The European Central Bank is due to complete its two-year investigation phase for a digital euro in July, when it will be followed by three years of implementation. Consumer protection has come under scrutiny during the 'crypto winter' precipitated by a fall in the value of Bitcoin and the collapse of major exchange FTX. The EU has previously laid out the world's first comprehensive ruleset for regulating crypto markets, which may enter effect in 2024. Griffith indicated the UK's rules could be broader to cover decentralised finance, and that the public consultation over regulating crypto assets would be part of a "research and exploration" phase with the government and the Bank of England. This includes "at least" six discussions with industry members to "expose us as regulators and decision makers" and uphold Britain's "strong financial reputation". Stay tuned for more updates on this story.

orig_title: Powerful earthquake rocks Vanuatu archipelago
text: According to reports, An earthquake with the likely magnitude of 7.0 struck the Oceanian nation of Vanuatu at 11:30 PM VUT Saturday (10:30 UTC Sunday). There were no reports of casualties. A tsunami warning for "waves reaching 0.3 to one meter [3.9 feet] above the tide level" along the coasts of Vanuatu, New Caledonia and the Solomon Islands issued by the United States Geological Survey after the quake was quickly lifted after none materialized. The French Embassy in Port Vila additionally issued a statement on its Facebook page urging residents to . 22-year-old college student Kayson Pore, who lives on Vanuatu's largest island Espiritu Santo, told Agence France-Presse: "We were right on the sea, we were looking for crab on the coast," when he experienced a "very huge" quake. "We ran for our lives and then we ran to our homes [...] individuals were moving to higher ground" to avoid a tsunami. The New Zealand National Emergency Management Agency stated they didn't expect any tsunamis to affect their coast. The Vanuatuan islands lie along the convergent boundary of the Australian and Pacific tectonic plates, part of the Ring of Fire along which seismic activity frequently occurs. In November, a magnitude 7.0 earthquake shook the Solomon Islands but didn't cause serious casualties or destruction. In 2018, 4,300 individuals died or went missing in a magnitude 7.5 earthquake on the island of Sulawesi in Indonesia. Last year's WorldRiskReport, which assesses the disaster risk of 193 countries, ranked Vanuatu 49th on its . Related news Sister links Sources Stay tuned for more updates on this story.

orig_title: Troops freed by Mali return to Ivory Coast

orig_title: Kevin McCarthy elected US House Speaker on 15th ballot
text: According to reports, In a historic vote past midnight yesterday, California Representative Kevin McCarthy was elected the 55th Speaker of the US House of Representatives on the fifteenth ballot, after making major concessions to end four days of Republican deadlock. Addressing the House for the first time as Speaker, McCarthy promised "debates will be passionate. They will never be personal" and said: "Now the hard work begins". On Tuesday, the first day of the 118th session, the House adjourned for the first time since 1923 without electing a speaker. Despite leading the Republicans, who won a slim majority in the midterm elections, about twenty conservatives steadfastly opposed McCarthy's leadership. To clear the impasse, McCarthy steadily caved on major fronts, including reducing the number of representatives needed to force a 'motion to vacate', or vote of no confidence, down to one. Ultimately, fourteen holdout Republicans either switched their votes for McCarthy or voted 'present' to abstain on the twelfth ballot, and another, Andy Harris, on the thirteenth. A chaotic scene took place after McCarthy lost on the fourteenth ballot on one vote, despite initially predicting victory, during which his ally Mike Rogers of Alabama had to be pulled away from confronting Florida's Matt Gaetz. The near-altercation, on January 6, was exactly two years after the attack on the US Capitol. Finally, on the fifteenth ballot, Gaetz changed his vote to 'present': ultimately, 216 Republicans voted for McCarthy, six 'present', and all 212 Democrats for their House leader Hakeem Jeffries. USA," while McCarthy took the oath of office. Jeffries spoke briefly before handing the gavel to McCarthy: "Freedom over fascism. Justice over judicial overreach. Knowledge over kangaroo courts. Liberty over limitation, maturity over Mar-a-Lago. Finally, McCarthy ascended to the , and the House could begin swearing in new lawmakers. orig_title: "One-in-100-year flood event" devastates Western Australia
text: According to reports, Aerial evacuations took place and food was airlifted in yesterday after a devastating flood Western Australia emergency services minister Stephen Dawson called the 'worst in a century' isolated communities in the Kimberley. Flooding began last week after heavy rain from Tropical Cyclone Ellie swelled local rivers, bolstered by La Niña. Notably, the Fitzroy River broke a 2002 record of , reaching a water level of on Wednesday, according to a Bureau of Meteorology spokesperson. The Bureau today released a statement warning while the storm has moved eastward toward the Northern Territory, "record-breaking major flooding" continues in the Kimberley. While the extent of the damage isn't yet known, parts of the Great Northern Highway have been shut, the bridge at Fitzroy Crossing closed and the airstrip inundated. According to Reuters, among the hardest-hit is the town of Fitzroy Crossing, on the Fitzroy River after flooding created a wide "inland sea", making roads there impassable. By Saturday, 233 individuals had been evacuated from settlements across the Kimberley, which has a 50% aboriginal population, and Australian Defence Force helicopters airlifted approximately 3,000 kilograms (6,600 lbs) of food and supplies as weather has improved and the airstrip reopened. Five new helicopters will begin operations by Thursday, Reuters heard. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described the flood as "devastating" and pledged federal assistance for the region. The Western Australian government has additionally announced a AU$3 million distress fund organized by Perth's Lord Mayor Basil Zempilas. Stay tuned for more updates on this story.

orig_title: 118th United States Congress convenes; House of Representatives adjourns without electing Speaker for first time in 100 years
text: According to reports, The United States Congress, convened Tuesday to begin its 118th session. Vice President and President of the Senate Kamala Harris swore in new and reelected Senators in the Senate chamber beginning shortly after noon EST (17:00 UTC). The Republican-majority House of Representatives is holding a roll call election for Speaker. In the first ballot for Speaker on Tuesday, all 212 House Democrats voted for their leader, Representative Hakeem Jeffries, 203 House Republicans voted for their leader, Representative Kevin McCarthy, while 19 Republicans voted for other candidates. Thus, as no candidate attained the 218-vote majority necessary to win, the House was forced to proceed to a second ballot for the first time since 1923. The second ballot produced the same totals for Jeffries and McCarthy, but the 19 Republicans opposed to McCarthy voted en bloc for Representative Jim Jordan, even though he had taken himself out of the race and endorsed McCarthy. A third ballot resulted in 212 votes for Jeffries again, but 202 for McCarthy and 20 for Jordan. At approximately 5:29 PM EST (22:29 UTC), the House adjourned until noon EST (17:00 UTC) on Wednesday. Meanwhile, in the Democratic-majority Senate, Harris swore in the most senior Senator, Washington State Democrat Patty Murray as President pro tempore; Murray, the first woman to serve in that role, is now third in the United States presidential line of succession. The Senate began adopting rules Tuesday afternoon. Senators serve staggered six-year terms, so federal elections, which occur every two years, see about one-third of all 100 Senate seats up for election; there are now 51 Democrats (including three independents who are members of the Democratic caucus) and 49 Republicans in the Senate. Representatives, by contrast, serve two-year terms, so all seats in the House of Representatives are up for election in every federal election; there are now 222 Republicans, 212 Democrats, and one vacancy in the House. Stay tuned for more updates on this story.

orig_title: Two helicopters collide in Gold Coast, Australia

orig_title: Pope Benedict XVI dies at age 95
text: According to reports, Emeritus Pope Benedict XVI, birth name Joseph Aloisius Ratzinger, died at the age of 95 at 9:34 CET (10:34 UTC) on Saturday in the Mater Ecclesiae monastery, located in The Vatican, where he spent his final years. The current Pope, Francis, had revealed Wednesday that Benedict was gravely ill. Benedict, born in rural Germany in 1927, served in the German Army in World War II before studying philosophy and theology at the University of Munich. In 1977, Benedict was appointed Archbishop of Munich and Freising, and became Dean of the College of Cardinals in 1998. Benedict served as pope from 2005 until his 2013 resignation, which stunned Catholics, being the first voluntary resignation since Pope Celestine V in 1294. World leaders including UK Prime Minister Rishi Sunak, King Charles III of the UK, US President Joe Biden (the second Catholic to serve in the position), French President Emmanuel Macron and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni paid their respects to the late pope. Pope Francis stated, "It is with emotion that we remember his person, so noble, so kind. And we feel in our heart such gratitude, gratitude to God for having gifted him to the church and the world. Benedict's body will lie in state from Monday, with his funeral to be held on Thursday at 9:30 CET (10:30 UTC). According to the Director of the Press Office of the Holy See, Matteo Bruni, his funeral will be simple per Benedict's wishes. Stay tuned for more updates on this story.

orig_title: "National treasure": Former Brazilian footballer Pelé dies at age 82
text: According to reports, Former Brazilian association football player Edson Arantes do Nascimento, better known as Pelé, died in São Paulo of multiple organ failure Thursday. Pelé, whose country's government declared him a "national treasure" in 1961, was 82. A post by Pelé's official Instagram account revealed the death of "The King": "Inspiration and love marked the journey of King Pele, who peacefully passed away today...[he] enchanted the world with his genius in sport, stopped a war, carried out social works all over the world and spread what he most believed to be the cure for all our problems: love. Pelé was born on October 23, 1940, in Três Corações, a town in the state of Minas Gerais, into an impoverished family. Pelé himself worked as a shoeshiner, playing informally; he acquired the nickname "Pelé" from his incorrect pronunciation of "Bilé", the name of a local association football player. When he was 15, Santos, a local association football club, recruited Pelé for its juvenile team, and eventually promoted him to the adult team. In 1956, at the age of 16, he joined the Brazilian national team. The national team brought Pelé, 17, as a reserve during the 1958 World Cup in Sweden; while the Brazilian team was playing in the final, they moved him onto the field. Pelé punted the ball over one of the opposing team's defenders, then wheeled around the other man and propelled it into the opponents' goal, scoring. This was voted among the best plays in the history of association football, and Pelé was proclaimed the winner of the Cup. Pelé suffered an injury and was largely unable to play in the 1962 World Cup in Chile, although he still won. Brazil additionally advanced to the 1966 Cup in England. England won the tournament. Pelé nevertheless played in the 1970 World Cup in Mexico, his last Cup. Brazil advanced to the final, facing Italy, with Pelé making the first goal for his team in that game and winning once again. In 1972, Pelé retired from Santos FC. European clubs invited him to play for them, but he declined. In 1975, Pelé made a comeback playing for the New York Cosmos in the new North American Soccer League. After a 1976 game between the Cosmos and Santos, his old club, of which he played half with each team, Pelé revealed he was again retiring from professional association football. Pelé wrote an autobiography in 1977, My Life and the Beautiful Game, which the Associated Press credited with the popularization of that nickname for the sport. Pelé had been hospitalized more than a month ago in Albert Einstein Hospital in São Paulo while undergoing treatment for colon cancer, which he developed in 2021; the hospital attributed the multiple organ failure that killed him Thursday afternoon to this cancer. After the announcement, current Brazilian footballer Neymar posted to Instagram, "Pelé changed everything. He transformed football into art, entertainment...Football and Brazil elevated their standing thanks to the King! He is gone, but his magic will endure. French footballer Kylian Mbappé tweeted, "The king of football has left us but his legacy will never be forgotten...RIP KING. Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, the President-elect, tweeted, "few Brazilians carried the name of our country as far as he did. Emmanuel Macron, the President of France, tweeted, "The game. Stay tuned for more updates on this story.

orig_title: Brothers Sunshine Coast to join A grade rugby union competition on Australia's Sunshine Coast
text: According to reports, Wikinews reporter Patrick Gillett interviewed President of the Brothers Rugby Union Club Sunshine Coast Mike Haines on November 25 after the team's announcement they would join the top grade of Australia's Sunshine Coast Rugby Union (SCRU) in 2023. The November 14 announcement on Instagram confirms it will raise the number of A grade teams to seven. It also means the other SCRU clubs - Caboolture, Caloundra, Maroochydore, Noosa, University of the Sunshine Coast, and Wynnum, as well as Gympie and Nambour, who do not play at the top level - approved the decision. Said Haines: "Essentially, we just had to put together a case to demonstrate that there was a larger playing group out there, that's of a higher quality player, that we could essentially tap into. "We put out some expressions of interest. We spoke to a large number of players out there on the Sunshine Coast and the broader community and we've actually had a great response from a large number of players who are looking to play at Brothers next year. In 2022, Brothers played in the newly established Sunshine Coast Cup competition. This was the clubs first season playing senior age rugby. "[So, we] had a really strong Friday night [competition.] Obviously, the Friday night Cricks, Sunshine Coast Cricks Cup that went really well for us this year," Haines summarised. "A large number of our boys will be looking to sort of advance [or] go into the reserve grade in the A grade on the back of their efforts this year. The club introduced team coaches on November 19, and began recruiting players in early December. "We're all very excited about the A grade and the reserve grade for 2023. orig_title: First deep space images from James Webb Space Telescope released
text: According to reports, Webb's First Deep Field showing thousands of stars and galaxies. On Monday, NASA Administrator Bill Nelson and US President Joe Biden presented the first image (see left) obtained by the Near-Infrared Camera (NIRCam), an instrument on the James Webb Space Telescope. The image, named , shows thousands of galaxies in the SMACS 0723 galaxy cluster, about 4.6 billion light-years away from Earth. However, the area shown by the image is only a small portion of the Southern Hemisphere sky. The blended image (at left) resulted from the stitching together of numerous smaller images obtained at multiple wavelengths with far greater depth than achieved by the Hubble Space Telescope, the predecessor to James Webb. The telescope entered its current orbit around the L2 Lagrange point from January 24, about from Earth, on the opposite side of Earth from the Sun. This followed a month-long journey that began in late December 2021, following years of delays and several cost overruns. For its expected five- to ten-year service life, it is intended to study the most distant, and therefore the earliest galaxies formed after the Big Bang. During its journey, dubbed "30 days of terror" by , the telescope successfully unfurled its wide mirror, deployed its sunshield and cooled down to below 50 degrees Kelvin as it traveled to the L2 Lagrange point. L2 is a secure location for spacecraft where the gravitational pull of the Sun and the Earth is balanced. Full scientific operations will involve thirteen teams of scientists. The primary mission is to find the most distant and earliest galaxies formed after the Big Bang to help study the origins of the Universe. The nominal mission time is five years, with a goal of ten. The location of its orbit is very different to the Hubble Space Telescope, which orbits much closer to Earth. James Webb's instruments face away from the Sun, giving a greater clarity to the images it will obtain compared to Hubble. An Ariane 5 launch vehicle carried the telescope to space on December 25 from the Guiana Space Centre in French Guiana, after arriving at the launch site in October. The launch date was delayed by a week due to unfavorable weather. The United States National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) began project development in 1996, planning for a launch in 2007 at a cost of USD550 million. After NASA contracted Northrop Grumman to build the telescope, mission managers estimated a 2010 launch would cost between one and 3.5 billion USD. Redesigns to reduce technical requirements pushed launch plans to 2013 for an estimated cost of USD4.5 billion. The US Congress ordered a project review in 2010 which delayed the launch again to 2015. Due to an estimated cost of USD6.5 billion, the United States House Appropriations Subcommittee on Commerce, Justice, Science, and Related Agencies proposed canceling the telescope altogether in 2011. After a plan was made for a 2018 launch at a cost of USD8.8 billion, technical errors found in the telescope and the subsequent COVID-19 pandemic pushed the launch date to 2021. orig_title: Conservationists capture most massive Burmese python in Florida history
text: According to reports, Media reported Wednesday that biologists from the Conservancy of Southwest Florida reported having captured a Burmese python (Python bivittatus) measuring nearly in length and 215 pounds (97 kg) in weight in the state's Everglades wetlands. It may be the largest member of its species ever found outside its natural range in Southeast Asia. Another Burmese python measuring 18 feet and 9 inches (5.7 m) was found in 2020, but it only weighed 104 pounds (47.2 kilograms). In a search documented by , the team captured the current snake in December 2021 by tagging a male "scout snake" named Dionysius with a GPS tracking device and releasing it into the western Everglades. "How do you find the needle in the haystack? You could use a magnet, and in a similar way our male scout snakes are attracted to the biggest females around," stated wildlife expert Ian Bartoszek, the team's project manager. Pythons are an invasive species in Florida. Removing female snakes from the environment before they lay their eggs is the Conservancy's preferred strategy for limiting python breeding. When the team saw that Dionysius was spending several weeks in one area, they concluded he'd found a sexually mature female and set off to retrieve him. It took twenty minutes of wrestling and three adult humans to carry the snake to a vehicle, in which it was taken to a laboratory in Naples, Florida and euthanized. Upon necropsy, it was found to contain over 122 healthy but unfertilized egg follicles. Pythons were introduced to Florida in the 1970s, probably by being sold as pets. While there is a history of individual pet owners illegally releasing exotic animals into the wild after they grow larger than expected, the destruction caused by Hurricane Andrew in 1992 also allowed animals from a serpent center to escape to the Everglades and other habitats, where they reproduced in great numbers. The state of Florida considers Burmese pythons a threat to native wildlife and sponsors an annual python hunt with USD2,500 as first prize. Stay tuned for more updates on this story.

orig_title: Canada, Denmark agree to resolve Arctic border dispute
text: According to reports, A long-standing and mainly good-natured border dispute between Canada and Denmark over the uninhabited Hans Island in the Arctic Sea is to be resolved, with the Danish Foreign Ministry confirming Tuesday the nations have agreed to divide it in two. The agreement, which awaits parliamentary approval before it can be fully ratified, sees Hans Island split almost equally between Canada and Denmark, with the border to follow a naturally occurring cleft on the island. It is mainly a symbolic agreement, and serves as a show of unity and cooperation between the two NATO countries. It follows the 2018 establishment of a working group between the two countries with the aim of resolving the dispute, termed the 'Whisky War'. The dispute arose as Hans Island is of a roughly equal distance between Canada's Ellesmere Island and Greenland, a territory of Denmark. It dates to 1971, but the name arose after Canadian troops left the Canadian flag and a bottle of Canadian whisky on the island in 1984. Denmark's Greenland affairs minister Tom Høyem responded by visiting the island, replacing the Canadian flag with Denmark's, and leaving a bottle of Danish schnapps. This developed into a tradition where officials, scientists and soldiers from both Canada and Denmark visited the island to remove the other side's flag, raise their own and leave either Canadian whisky or Danish schnapps for the other side to find. In a press release, Canadian foreign affairs minister Mélanie Joly called the Arctic region a "beacon for international cooperation, where the rule of law prevails". Joly added "as global security is being threatened, it's more important than ever for democracies like Canada and the Kingdom of Denmark to work together, alongside Indigenous peoples, to resolve our differences in accordance with international law. Her Danish counterpart, Jeppe Kofod, noted that sovereignty over the island had been in contention "for more than 50 years", and that "efforts" between the two nations "demonstrate our firm common commitment to resolve international disputes peacefully". Kofod stated that he hoped "our negotiation and the spirit of this agreement" would inspire other nations, and that it was "much needed at a time when respect for the international rules-based order is under pressure". orig_title: Scientists discover seagrass off Australia is world's largest plant
text: According to reports, Scientists at the University of Western Australia published a study Wednesday suggesting that a seagrass off the coast of Western Australia is the world's largest plant. It is located in Shark Bay, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Western Australia. The scientists discovered the plant was a single organism after taking 18,000 separate genetic markers to examine the seagrass to find samples to use in restoration projects. However, they discovered the same plant had cloned itself many times instead. Dr Martin Breed, an ecologist at Flinders University, stated "We thought 'what the hell is going on here?'... We were completely stumped. The plant is around three times the size of Manhattan, and measures at least 180 kilometres (112 miles) in length. As well as being the world's largest known plant, it is the world's largest known clone. The seagrass greatly surpasses the 43-hectare stand of quaking Aspen trees in Utah, United States, previously thought to be the world's largest plant. The seagrass grows a maximum of 35 centimetres per year, with its large size helping scientists calculate its age. Elizabeth Sinclair, another co-author of the study, stated the plant's survival was helped by it holding onto all the chromosomes from both its parents. This gave it genetic diversity, which is unusual among plants that produce asexually. The plant does not sexually reproduce; but, subtle variations in its DNA may help explain its longevity. Associate Professor Kathryn McMahon, of Edith Cowan University, was not involved in the study but is an expert on seagrass. She stated seagrass tends to live for between 2,000 and 100,000 years, meaning the plant's age of about 4,500 years fits into the normal age range of seagrass. McMahon also stated she was confident in the method used by the researchers, and that the finding it was a single plant was "amazing". Despite the plant's vast size, in the past ten years, almost a tenth of it has been destroyed by cyclones and rising ocean temperatures, which NBC News noted had been attributed to climate change. The bay has relatively high salinity and its temperatures vary from as cold as to as hot as . Stay tuned for more updates on this story.

orig_title: Ethics chief: UK PM's reforms after Partygate "highly unsatisfactory", won't "restore public trust"
text: According to reports, Chair of the Committee on Standards in Public Life Jonathan Evans criticised United Kingdom Prime Minister Boris Johnson's proposed changes to the ministerial code after the Partygate revelations on Wednesday as "highly unsatisfactory". Evans said that unless the adviser, currently Lord Geidt, is allowed to scrutinise ministerial conduct independently, "suspicion about the way in which the ministerial code is administered will linger. orig_title: New cabinet formed in Bermuda following election

orig_title: US Navy Secretary nominee Phelan outlines readiness, cost-cutting reforms in Senate hearing
text:
As the Senate Armed Services Committee weighs the nomination of John Phelan to lead the US Navy, a critical assessment of his leadership qualifications has emerged. Phelan, a businessman and financier with no prior military experience, faces a daunting task in addressing the Navy's maintenance shortfalls, shipbuilding delays, and personnel challenges.

During his Senate confirmation hearing, Phelan emphasized the need for significant reforms to improve fleet readiness, tackle cost overruns, and enhance living conditions for sailors. However, his lack of military experience has raised eyebrows among lawmakers and defense experts, with some expressing concerns that he may struggle to navigate the complexities of the Department of the Navy.

Senator Rick Scott, chair of the Armed Services Committee, used a striking image of the USS Dewey's rusting hull to highlight the Navy's maintenance woes, an issue Phelan acknowledged as part of broader systemic challenges. "The US Navy is at a crossroads," Scott warned, "with extended deployments, inadequate maintenance, huge cost overruns, delayed shipbuilding, failed audits, subpar housing, and record-high suicide rates. These are systemic failures that have gone unaddressed for far too long, and it's unacceptable."

Critics argue that Phelan's business background, while potentially valuable in addressing logistical and industrial challenges, may not be sufficient to address the Navy's more complex and nuanced issues. "It will be difficult for anyone without experience in the Pentagon to take over the leadership of a service and do a good job," noted Stacie Pettyjohn, director of the defense program at the Center for a New American Security. "Services are sprawling organizations with distinct cultures, subcultures, and bureaucratic interests, and where decisions are made through many formal processes."

Supporters, however, argue that Phelan's entrepreneurial spirit and experience in managing complex systems could be a valuable asset in revamping the Navy's shipbuilding efforts. "If we threw a zillion dollars at the Department of the Navy today, we couldn't build the ships because we don't have the industrial base," said Senator Roger Wicker, chairman of the Armed Services Committee. "We've got to fix that. And I think that's why the president looked to an entrepreneur and an experienced business person."

As the Senate Armed Services Committee deliberates Phelan's nomination, the stakes are high. A simple majority is required for confirmation, and the fate of the Navy hangs in the balance.

orig_title: Trump, Starmer talk Ukraine, tariffs, and UK visit in White House meeting

orig_title: Gunman enters Pennsylvania hospital ICU, kills officer before police fatally shoot him

orig_title: NASA revises asteroid 2024 YR4 threat, near-zero chance of Earth impact

This effort aims to bolster planetary defense preparedness and provide a robust safeguard against potential asteroid threats.

orig_title: International Asteroid Warning Network issues alert on asteroid 2024 YR4 impact risk in 2032
text:
A recent assessment by NASA and the European Space Agency has significantly increased the estimated chances of asteroid 2024 YR4 colliding with Earth on December 22, 2032, from 1.2% to a staggering 2.2%. This development has sparked renewed concerns among astronomers and scientists, who warn that time is running out to observe the asteroid.

The asteroid, estimated to be roughly the size of a football field, poses a significant threat to our planet, with an impact potentially equivalent to the force of a nuclear bomb. According to the Torino Impact Hazard Scale, which rates the likelihood of impact, 2024 YR4 has been classified as a level 3 out of 10, indicating a close encounter that warrants attention.

"It's a ticking time bomb," said Paul Chodas, director of the Center for Near-Earth Object Studies. "The likelihood of impact could fall to zero almost any day now, but we don't know that." Chodas emphasized that scientists are facing a critical deadline to study the asteroid, which is set to become unobservable again until 2028.

Despite the increased risk, the European Space Agency (ESA) remains optimistic that the asteroid will safely pass our planet without incident. However, they caution that an impact "cannot yet be entirely ruled out." The agency notes that the asteroid may fade from view before further observations can confirm the risk, placing it on their risk list until it becomes observable again.

Astronomers are drawing parallels with the 2004 case of asteroid 99942 Apophis, which was initially estimated to have a 2.7% chance of striking Earth in 2029. Further observations ruled out this possibility, highlighting the importance of continued monitoring.

The International Asteroid Warning Network (IAWN) has issued a warning, stating that if the asteroid were to impact Earth, it would most likely strike in the ocean. The IAWN's notification serves as a reminder of the urgent need for continued research and monitoring of near-Earth asteroids.

As the world watches with bated breath, the scientific community is working tirelessly to provide accurate and timely warnings. The stakes are high, and the clock is ticking – will we be able to mitigate the risks posed by asteroid 2024 YR4? Only time will tell.

orig_title: Air ambulance crashes into infrastructure in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania while transporting pediatric patient, no survivors

orig_title: Passenger plane collides with military helicopter near Washington, D.C.

orig_title: US President Trump orders government recognize male, female as only sexes

orig_title: Chilean president Gabriel Boric makes historic trip to South Pole becoming the first head of state to visit and third head of government
text:
In a groundbreaking move, Chilean President Gabriel Boric has made history by becoming the first sitting head of state to reach the South Pole, a feat that has been hailed as a major achievement by his government. Boric's expedition, part of "Operation Polar Star III," aimed to reaffirm Chile's commitment to Antarctica's preservation and scientific research, solidifying the country's claim to sovereignty over a significant portion of the continent.

As part of his visit, Boric was joined by his defense and environment ministers, as well as three military commanders, and arrived at the Amundsen-Scott South Pole Station, a U.S. research base, at 8pm GMT. The Chilean leader spent approximately two hours at the outpost, which is situated in one of the planet's most remote and inhospitable regions.

Boric's historic visit marks a significant milestone for Chile, making him the first Latin American leader to reach the planet's southernmost point. "This is a milestone for us," Boric said, adding, "It is the first time a Chilean president has come to the South Pole and talked about Chile's Antarctic mission."

The visit comes at a critical time for Chile's scientific endeavors in the region, with the country seeking to expand its research efforts to the Bellingshausen and Weddell Seas. Throughout the 20th century, countries like Chile, France, the U.S., the UK, Argentina, and Japan established research stations in Antarctica for scientific purposes and to solidify their presence in the region.

The Antarctic Treaty, established in 1961, governs activities in Antarctica, aiming to protect the continent and surrounding seas from geopolitical tensions. While the U.S. State Department states that seven countries, including Chile, maintain territorial claims in Antarctica, the country is not recognized by the international community.

Boric's journey began early in the day from Punta Arenas, in southern Chile, and he reached Chile's research station on the Union Glacier in Antarctica aboard a Hercules C-130 military transport plane. The visit emphasizes Chile's strategic interest in Antarctica, a region that has been the subject of territorial disputes over time.

"It is an honor to be the first president to visit this place," Boric said, adding, "To see the Chilean flag among the 12 representing the signatories of the Antarctic Treaty fills me with pride." The visit serves as a confirmation of Chile's claim to sovereignty, underscoring the country's commitment to science and preservation in the region.

orig_title: Luigi Mangione, suspect in killing of US healthcare CEO, charged with terrorism

orig_title: IDF missile strikes UN school

orig_title: Dutch F-16s supplied to Ukraine to be used in Russian airspace

orig_title: The Ancient Pyramids of the World, a new photo exhibition by Viktor Pinchuk took place in Crimea

Among the highlights of the exhibition was a haunting image of the Pulemelei Mound in Samoa, a pyramid-shaped structure that was once a marvel of engineering but now lies almost completely destroyed. Located deep within the dense jungle of Savai'i, this remote site is a treasure trove of history and geography, yet remains largely unknown to the general public.

According to Pinchuk, the exhibition aims to inspire visitors to explore the world's historical and geographical wonders. By sharing his photographs, he hopes to spark a sense of curiosity and wonder in those who witness his work. As a photographer who has spent years documenting the world's most remarkable sites, Pinchuk's passion for his craft is evident in every image.

The exhibition's digital format allowed for an unprecedented display of works, with over 100 images on show. This innovative approach enabled the organizers to showcase a wider range of photographs without the need for physical transportation, making it possible to reach a broader audience.

The event was a testament to the importance of cultural exchange and the value of preserving our shared history. As the Russian Geographical Society's "Night of Geography" event continues to inspire people to explore and learn about our world, Pinchuk's exhibition serves as a powerful reminder of the beauty and significance of our planet's ancient monuments.

orig_title: Severe weather affects portions of Texas
text:

orig_title: Russia warns United States against allowing cross-border strikes by Ukraine

orig_title: Former U.S. President Trump convicted in hush money trial
text:

The prosecution had alleged that Trump's then-attorney, Michael Cohen, made a US$130,000 payment to adult film actress Stormy Daniels in 2016, in an effort to silence her about an alleged affair with Trump. The payment was reportedly made to ensure Daniels did not speak publicly about the incident. Cohen had also received US$420,000 from Trump and his trust as reimbursement for various payments he had made on Trump's behalf, including the payment to Daniels.

Daniels' attorney acknowledged that the verdict had a profound impact on her client, saying that it was a "culmination of a lot of things" and that it had been a "worry" for her leading up to the trial. When asked about the verdict, Daniels stated that she believed Trump should face jail time and community service, and that he was "completely and utterly out of touch with reality." However, she also noted that she would continue to speak out about the trial, despite the verdict.

The verdict has already had an impact on Trump's public image, with a recent poll showing that 54% of registered voters approved of the conviction, while 34% disapproved. However, analysts have noted that early poll results may not be indicative of future trends, and that the situation is likely to continue evolving in the coming days and weeks.

orig_title: Tens of thousands of people join the Israeli day parade

orig_title: Levenmouth Rail Link reopens as June timetable changes reshuffle United Kingdom rail service patterns
text:

orig_title: Ukraine permitted to strike Russian territory near Kharkiv

orig_title: Hamas fires rockets at Tel Aviv

orig_title: Exhibition featuring ethnic music from around the world opens in Crimea

orig_title: Stunt performer set ablaze for cover artwork of Pink Floyd album dies aged 88
text: Ronnie Rondell Jr., the stunt performer best known for his appearance on Pink Floyd's 1975 album cover, has died at the age of 88. Rondell, who was 88, died at an assisted living facility in Missouri, according to his family. He had a long career in stunt work, including gymnastics, hang gliding, and scuba diving, and appeared in numerous films and television shows. Rondell sustained numerous injuries throughout his career, but continued to work until 2000 before retiring. He left behind a wife of 56 years and two sons, one of whom also worked as a stunt double.

orig_title: Several people hospitalized after thousands of hotdogs spill following collision on interstate in Pennsylvania
text: Thousands of hot dogs spilled onto Interstate 83 in York County, Pennsylvania after a tractor trailer crash. The incident occurred when the truck's mechanical issue caused it to brush against a concrete divider, resulting in the hot dogs spilling out. Several people were injured, but their conditions were not life-threatening. Cleanup efforts, which involved rakes and a front-end loader, took several hours to complete. The Pennsylvania State Police were investigating the incident, which resulted in over 1,000 pounds of lost hot dogs.

orig_title: Summer Streets returns with uninterrupted car-free stretch across Manhattan
text: New York City's Summer Streets program returned this weekend, with select roads closed to cars in Manhattan. The program, which runs through August, features a continuous route stretching from the Brooklyn Bridge to Inwood, with side streets also closed for socializing and activities. Programming included live music, arts and crafts, water bottle refilling stations, and sports equipment rentals. The event attracted cyclists, runners, rollerbladers, and scooter users, who enjoyed partly sunny skies and mid-70s temperatures. The program will return on August 9 and 16, and expand to Brooklyn and the Bronx on August 23.

orig_title: Nigerian abductors kill hostages despite ransom, officials report
text: Nigeria's Zamfara state officials have confirmed that abductors have killed 33-35 hostages in the Banga village, despite a ransom of tens of thousands of dollars being paid. The victims were "slaughtered like rams" and mostly consisted of young people, with the attackers seemingly unaware of the human cost of their actions. The incident occurred despite the government making ransom payments a criminal offense in 2022, intended to disrupt the lucrative kidnapping industry.

orig_title: Train derails in southwest Germany after landslide, causing deaths
text: A train derailed and crashed in southwest Germany, killing three people and injuring several more. The incident occurred in the Riedlingen area, near the cities of Ulm and Stuttgart. Authorities are investigating the cause of the derailment, with reports suggesting a landslide triggered by heavy storms and possibly an overflowing sewage shaft. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has offered support to the rescue services, describing the incident as a "shock". The investigation is ongoing, with the number of injured passengers still being clarified.

orig_title: Jury convicts Minnesota lawmaker Nicole Mitchell of burglary
text: Democratic Minnesota state senator Nicole Mitchell has been convicted on two charges, felony first-degree burglary and possession of burglary or theft tools, stemming from a 2024 incident where she allegedly broke into her "estranged" stepmother's home in Detroit Lakes. Mitchell's defense claimed she was checking on her stepmother's well-being, but prosecutors argued her recorded statements contradicted this claim. The senator faces a minimum of 180 days in jail and is expected to resign, according to Governor Tim Walz's office.

orig_title: UK voting age to be lowered to 16, among other reforms
text: The UK's Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government has unveiled plans to lower the voting age to 16, following successful reforms in Scotland and Wales. The proposal, supported by Prime Minister Keir Starmer, would give 16 and 17-year-olds the right to vote, citing their ability to pay taxes and participate in the workforce. A poll found 51% of 16-17 year olds support the change, while Reform UK leader Nigel Farage criticized the move, arguing that 16-year-olds should be able to stand for Parliament before they can vote.

orig_title: Car goes airborne twice in Indiana roundabout crash, man hospitalized
text: A man in Fort Wayne, Indiana was hospitalized in critical condition after losing control of his vehicle in a roundabout on July 11. The vehicle, which was traveling at high speeds and swerving, struck a curb and became airborne before hitting a barricade and airborne again. The man was found hundreds of feet from the road and was taken to Lutheran Hospital in life-threatening condition. The Allen County Sheriff's Department is investigating the incident, which is currently under investigation.

orig_title: 20-year-old astrophotographer captures rare solar eclipse on Saturn
text: A 20-year-old astrophotographer from Shoreline, Washington, Adam Smadi, has captured a rare solar eclipse on Saturn, an event not seen until 2038. Smadi used a telescope and specialized camera to plan and execute the image, taking advantage of the Stellarium software to pinpoint the exact moment when Saturn's moon Titan cast a shadow across the planet's surface. The resulting photo shows Titan's shadow crossing Saturn's pale surface, with three other moons visible as tiny dots near the rings.

orig_title: Russia launches record drone, missile attack on Kyiv
text: A night of intense Russian strikes on Kyiv resulted in one death and 26 injuries. The strikes, which included 539 drones and missiles, lasted for over eight hours and targeted nearly every district of the city. Air raid sirens sounded continuously during the assault, which was described as the "main target of the strikes". The attacks came hours after a call between US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin, in which Trump expressed disappointment at Putin's refusal to end the war in Ukraine.

orig_title: Ugandan military helicopter crashes in Mogadishu, Somalia
text: A Ugandan military helicopter crashed at Aden Adde International Airport in Mogadishu on Wednesday, July 2. Eight people were on board, with five passengers killed and two pilots and a flight engineer seriously injured. The crash occurred during a "routine combat escort mission" against Islamist militant group al-Shabaab. Emergency personnel quickly brought the fire under control, and an investigation into the crash is underway. Domestic flights continued operating normally, but a Turkish Airlines passenger plane was delayed in departure.

orig_title: Bangladesh beat hosts Myanmar 2–1 to qualify for 2026 AFC Women's Asian Cup
text: Bangladesh defeats Myanmar 2-1 in their Group C match of the AFC Women's Asian Cup 2026 qualifiers at Thuwunna Stadium in Yangon, Myanmar. Goals from Ritu Porna Chakma in the 19th and 72nd minutes secured the win for Bangladesh, which marked their first-ever qualification for the continental finals. The victory also secured their spot in the final tournament of the 2026 AFC Women's Asian Cup in Australia, with Bangladesh topping Group C with one match remaining against Turkmenistan.

orig_title: Third person charged in relation to Pheobe Bishop's alleged murder
text: A 30-year-old man, Kieren Daniel Mittelheuser, has been arrested in Queensland, Australia, and charged with two counts of accessory after the fact to murder in relation to the alleged murder of 17-year-old Phoebe Bishop. Mittelheuser is also facing charges of unlicensed driving, fraud, breach of bail, and drug possession. He remains in custody and is set to appear in court on August 25. Bishop's body was found on June 6, and police are continuing to appeal for information about her disappearance and a grey Hyundai IX35 vehicle. Two other housemates, James Wood and Tanika Bromley, who were also accused of Bishop's murder, are scheduled to appear in court in August.

orig_title: Beyoncé halts performance after "flying car" prop malfunctions mid-air above audience
text: Beyoncé halted a live performance at NRG Stadium in Houston, Texas, due to a prop malfunction on the first night of her tour. The Cadillac suspended in mid-air above the audience began to tilt to one side, prompting the singer to repeatedly say "stop". The car was lowered into the crowd and audience members responded with cheers and applause. No injuries were reported in relation to the incident, described as a "technical mishap" by Beyoncé's production company.

orig_title: U.S. strikes Iranian nuclear sites Fordow, Natanz, Isfahan overnight
text: The US has launched airstrikes on three Iranian nuclear sites: Fordow, Natanz, and Isfahan. The operation, designated Operation Midnight Hammer, was ordered by President Donald Trump and aimed at disabling Iran's nuclear capabilities. The strikes involved seven B-2 Spirit stealth bombers and Tomahawk missiles, dropping 14 bunker buster bombs on the sites. The US Department of Defense described the mission as a demonstration of the country's "unmatched reach, coordination and capability". Iran has condemned the US action, calling it an act of aggression and threatening to defend itself.

orig_title: Bangladeshi interim leader Muhammad Yunus returns home after four-day visit to London
text: Bangladesh's Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus returned home on Saturday after a four-day visit to London, where he discussed national asset recovery, peace and sustainability, and Rohingya refugee issues. Yunus received the King Charles III Harmony Award 2025 and met with King Charles III and other UK officials, but failed to secure a meeting with UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer. Yunus also addressed Rohingya refugee concerns and stated that a national election in 2026 would be held in February, pending progress in reforms. His visit was seen as important, with the Bangladesh government and opposition parties calling for increased cooperation and transparency.

orig_title: San Diego joins US-wide No Kings protests
text: A series of protests organized by Take Action San Diego began in Downtown San Diego on June 14, as part of the nationwide No Kings protests against President Donald Trump's administration and policies. An estimated 80,000 people gathered at Waterfront Park, marching through the city before returning to the park. Protesters cited concerns over authoritarianism, fascism, and the administration's perceived illegality, with one participant stating they had been personally affected by Trump's policies as a transgender individual. The protests remained peaceful throughout the day.

orig_title: Hot air balloon crashes in Turkey, killing pilot and injuring tourists
text: A hot air balloon crashed in central Turkey on Sunday, killing its pilot and injuring 19 tourists from Indonesia. The crash occurred near the Ihlara Valley in Aksaray Province due to shifting wind conditions. The pilot fell from the basket and became trapped, resulting in his death. The injured tourists were taken to the hospital. Another tourist balloon experienced a hard landing on the same day, but with minor injuries and no fatalities.

orig_title: Football: Japan beats Indonesia with score 6-0 for 2026 FIFA World Cup
text: Japan secured a 6-0 victory over Indonesia in the AFC qualifiers final Group C match, with Daichi Kamada and Takefusa Kubo among the scorers. The win marked Japan's spot in the 2026 FIFA World Cup, while Indonesia took fourth place and still have a chance to qualify through their next matches. Japan has scored 30 goals in ten games, and the country now heads to the 2026 World Cup after securing a 2-0 win over Bahrain in March.

orig_title: Boeing 787 crashes into Indian medical school, killing hundreds
text: An Air India Boeing 787-8 crashed into a residential building in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India shortly after takeoff on Thursday, killing 241 people, with one survivor. The plane struck the city's Meghani Nagar neighborhood at 1:38 p.m. local time, crushing a nearby medical school building. The sole survivor, a British-Indian man, described the plane making a loud noise and catching fire. The incident is the first reported crash of any 787 version, with the 787-8 designed for long, nonstop routes. Multiple agencies, including Boeing, the US NTSB, and the FAA, have announced cooperation in investigating the crash, which has left a trail of destruction and death.

orig_title: Scottish Labour win Scottish Parliament by-election
text: A by-election was held in Scotland on June 5, 2025, following the death of incumbent MSP Christina McKelvie. Davy Russell from the Scottish Labour won the election with 31.6% of the vote. The Scottish National Party came in second with 29.4%, while Reform UK took third place with 26.1%. The Scottish Conservatives, Scottish Greens, and Scottish Liberal Democrats also had significant shares of the vote. Russell's victory speech criticized the SNP and Reform UK, saying the latter's divisive tactics were unwelcome in Scotland. The outcome is seen as significant ahead of the 2026 Scottish Parliament election.

orig_title: Ukrainian drone strikes target four airfields in Russia
text: Ukraine claims to have carried out drone strikes on four Russian military airfields, damaging over 40 aircraft and causing an estimated $7 billion in damages. The SBU said the operation targeted A-50 surveillance aircraft, strategic bombers, and strategic missile carriers. The Russian Ministry of Defense stated that the attacks were repelled, but there were no casualties among military personnel or civilians. The operation, which allegedly involved 117 quadcopter drones, was reportedly planned for over a year and a half.

orig_title: Activists claim sexual abuse and torture at the hands of Tanzanian authorities
text: Activists from Kenya and Uganda have accused Tanzanian security officers of torturing and sexually assaulting them while they were in detention from May 19 to 23. Photojournalist Boniface Mwangi and journalist Agather Atuhaire claim they were blindfolded, beaten, and subjected to humiliating treatments, including lubricant and objects being inserted into their bodies. Tanzanian authorities have dismissed the allegations as "hearsay", but human rights groups have condemned the mistreatment and called for accountability. The incident is part of a broader crackdown on opposition leader Tundu Lissu, who faces treason charges.

orig_title: NSW DCCEEW researchers discover critically endangered Leadbeater's possum in Kosciuszko National Park, Australia
text: A team of researchers from the NSW Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water has discovered seven photographs of the critically endangered Leadbeater's possum near Yarrangobilly Caves in Kosciuszko National Park, NSW. The discovery was made while reviewing footage from trail cameras set up to monitor the smoky mouse. The find is significant as Leadbeater's possum was previously thought to be extinct in NSW, but the discovery in Victoria in 1961 and subsequent findings in 1986 and 1990s suggested the possibility of a remnant population. The NSW Government has started the process of applying for an expedited conservation listing of the species. The discovery has raised hopes for the future of the species and could lead to the establishment of a new breeding program to improve genetic diversity in the wild.

orig_title: Man starts car collision at Liverpool FC trophy parade
text: A 53-year-old man, Paul Desmond Sanders Doyle, has been charged with dangerous driving and multiple counts of intending to cause grievous bodily harm after allegedly driving a Ford Galaxy into a crowd of pedestrians at a Liverpool FC trophy parade in Liverpool, England. The incident occurred on Monday, May 26, resulting in 27 people being taken to hospital, with seven still receiving treatment. Twenty people were treated for minor injuries. The alleged driver was arrested shortly after the incident and has been charged with the crimes.

orig_title: Baseball: Detroit Tigers sweep San Francisco Giants, making their fourth win in a row
text: The Detroit Tigers swept the San Francisco Giants 4-3, taking their fourth consecutive win and improving to the best record in Major League Baseball with 37 wins and 20 losses. Pitcher Brenan Hanifee earned a win-loss record of 3-2, while Tommy Kahnle secured his seventh save with a perfect ninth inning. The Tigers' victory propels them to the top of the league standings.

orig_title: Australian Coalition reunite after one week
text: The Liberal-National Coalition of Australia has reunited after a week-long split, with leaders Sussan Ley and David Littleproud announcing the parties' reintegration. The Nationals have agreed on four policy demands with the Liberals, including nuclear power and remote mobile data coverage. The reunification has led to a shadow cabinet reshuffle, with Ley stating she looks forward to the parties working together in the future. The Coalition's policy on nuclear power has changed, shifting from building new plants to pushing against the existing moratorium.

orig_title: Australian Nationals leave Coalition with Liberal Party
text: The leader of the National Party, David Littleproud, has announced that the party is ending its century-long partnership with the Liberal Party following the Coalition's historic defeat at the 2025 Federal Election. The decision is attributed to growing policy differences, including budgeting and nuclear power, as well as the party's poor performance at the election. The Nationals will no longer be part of a coalition agreement and are unlikely to form a government independently with the Liberals. This marks a significant shift in Australian politics, with the Nationals now sitting apart from the Liberals.

orig_title: Professional baseball is back in Tucson, Arizona, thanks to relocation of Mexican team
text: The Mayos de Navojoa, a Mexican Pacific Winter League team, have announced plans to relocate to Tucson, Arizona, starting the 2025-26 season. The team plans to rename themselves with fan input, and officials hope the relocation will lead to a multi-year arrangement. The move comes after Sonora Governor Alfonso Durazo Montaño announced plans to convert the team's former stadium into a school for young baseball players.

orig_title: Three UK neo-Nazis convicted of multiple terrorism offences
text: Three UK extremists, Christopher Ringrose, Marco Pitzettu, and Brogan Stewart, have been convicted of planning an act of terrorism and other related charges after a nine-week trial. The court heard the men communicated online, including through Telegram, and planned to use crossbows, machetes, and swords in their attack. Sentencing is scheduled for July 17 and is expected to be substantial.

orig_title: Texas police arrest mother and her son on terrorism charges
text: A 33-year-old woman and her  teenager son were arrested by the San Antonio Police Department on terrorism charges. The son, who was a student at Jeremiah Rhodes Middle School, was found to have purchased equipment and was spotted hammering a live bullet in his bedroom. The mother, Ashley Rosalinda Pardo, had taken him to military surplus stores to buy tactical gear and had shown support for his violent drawings.
