orig_title: "Too Easy LoL": messages written on cell wall as ten inmates escape from Orleans Parish Prison in Louisiana, United States
text: Ten inmates broke out of the Parish Justice Center Orleans in New Orleans, Louisiana, on Friday, May 16, 2025. The escapees, who included three facing second-degree murder charges, managed to break open a cell door and exit the jail around 1:01 a.m. Louisiana time. Authorities quickly apprehended several inmates, including Robert Moody and Corey Boyd, but seven remain at large. The inmates were armed and considered dangerous, prompting a massive search operation involving local, state, and federal agencies. The jail was understaffed, with only 36 staff and 4 supervisors present, and officials are reviewing security procedures and staff actions amid the investigation.

orig_title: Trainmen and engineers go on statewide strike in New Jersey, first time in 42 years
text: Members of the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen (BLET) union in New Jersey went on strike at midnight on Friday, May 16, due to a lack of agreement on contract terms with NJ Transit officials. The strike, which is expected to last until Sunday, has brought commuter trains, including NJ Transit and MTA Metro-North West of Hudson service, to a halt. Union members are protesting what they claim is excessive spending on a new headquarters and lack of pay raises, citing that NJ Transit engineers make at least $10 less per hour than Amtrak and Long Island Railroad employees.

orig_title: Thai officials seize 238 tons of illegal e-waste at Bangkok port
text: Thai authorities have seized 238 tons of electronic waste hidden in storage containers falsely declared as metal scrap at the port of Bangkok. The shipment, allegedly imported from the United States, was inspected during a routine search and found to contain electronic circuit boards. Officials plan to bring charges for the false declaration and refusal to accept the containers, with the aim of returning them to their sender. The incident is one of the largest e-waste imports uncovered by Thai authorities this year, highlighting the growing problem of e-waste globally, with 62 million tons generated in 2022 and only 22% properly collected and recycled.

orig_title: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese reshuffles cabinet following re-election
text: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has reshuffled his cabinet following the 2025 federal election, with many top jobs staying the same. However, former Attorney-General Mark Dreyfus and Minister for Industry and Science Ed Husic have been removed from their positions. New ministers include Anne Aly, who has been appointed to small business, international development, and multicultural affairs, and Michelle Rowland, who is the new attorney-general. Albanese's reshuffle comes after the Labor government won a second term in office, with a landslide election victory on May 3.

orig_title: United National Congress party wins elections, new government cabinet meets in Trinidad and Tobago
text: The new cabinet of Trinidad and Tobago, led by Prime Minister Kamla Persad-Bissessar, met at the Red House in Port of Spain on May 8. The UNC party won the 2025 general election, defeating the incumbent People's National Movement (PNM) after 10 years in government. The new cabinet discussed establishing an e-Cabinet platform, changes to gun laws, and modifications to the Children's Fund Act. Persad-Bissessar broke with tradition by taking her oath on the constitution instead of a holy text. The new cabinet includes both new and old members, with Persad-Bissessar serving for the second time as Prime Minister.

orig_title: 2025 Khelo India Youth Games begins, first time in Bihar
text: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the 2025 Khelo India Youth Games in Bihar, marking the event's first appearance in the state. The 28-sport competition, set to conclude on May 15, aims to improve India's youth sports development and global influence. Modi highlighted the importance of investing in sports for India's future. The event features indigenous sports, including kho kho, and demonstrates eSports, showcasing video games such as Street Fighter 6 and eFootball.

orig_title: Texas authorities announce manhunt after alleged murderer's ankle monitor found in fire
text: The Kaufman County Sheriff's Office in Texas is searching for Trevor McEuen, 32, who is accused of murder. McEuen removed his court-ordered ankle monitor and fled from Van Zandt County on Monday. Authorities believe he set a barn fire on his property to make it appear abandoned. McEuen had been released on a $2 million bond and was awaiting trial. His neighbor, Aaron Martinez, 35, was found dead of multiple gunshot wounds in May 2023. The sheriff's office has offered a $10,000 reward for information leading to McEuen's capture, and US Marshals are assisting in his apprehension.

orig_title: Robert Francis Prevost elected as Pope Leo XIV
text: White smoke signalled the selection of Pope Leo XIV at 18:07 CEST on May 8, 2025, at the Sistine Chapel. The 267th Pope, born Robert Francis Cardinal Prevost, is from North America, specifically Peru, and holds dual citizenship. Prevost, who previously served as Bishop of Chiclayo and Prefect of the Dicastery for Bishops, was appointed cardinal in 2024 by Pope Francis. He is the second Pope from the Americas and the first from North America, and has sparked interest among peers for his openness on social justice issues.

orig_title: Official White House social media accounts repost AI image of US President Donald Trump dressed like Pope
text: US President Donald Trump's social media accounts reposted an AI-generated image of him wearing the Pope's attire, sparking criticism from the Catholic Church. The image was shared just days after Trump joked about wanting to be Pope, and 11 days after Pope Francis' death. A spokesperson for the New York State Catholic Conference called the post "mocking" and "not funny," while former Italian Prime Minister Matteo Renzi described it as "offending believers" and "showing the leader of the right-wing world enjoys clowning around." The White House denied the post was intended to affront the Catholic Church.

orig_title: President of Serbia Aleksandar Vučić gets sick, flies home early from US visit
text: Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić was hospitalized in Belgrade on Saturday after suddenly experiencing severe chest pain during a trip to the US. He was discharged from the hospital on Sunday, with a doctor stating that his condition remains the same. Vučić had been in the US for a brief visit, which was cut short due to his health issues. The president has faced criticism for his stance on Russia sanctions and a deadly roof collapse in Serbia, which sparked anti-corruption protests.

orig_title: Peruvian police locate bodies of security guards allegedly abducted by illegal goldminers
text: Police in Peru's Pataz province have found the bodies of 13 security guards who were kidnapped by individuals involved in illegal mining on April 26. The security guards were employed by a private security firm that serves La Poderosa, a gold mining company. The discovery was made after a video of the victims being murdered circulated on social media, prompting authorities to impose a curfew and suspend gold mining in the area for 30 days. President Boluarte has vowed to take full control of the area, but critics argue that shutting down formal mining will only fuel the illegal mining industry.

orig_title: People's Action Party wins Singaporean election in landslide victory
text: The ruling People's Action Party (PAP) secured a landslide victory in the 2025 Singaporean general election, claiming 65.57% of the national vote and 87 seats in the 97-seat Parliament. The opposition Workers' Party (WP) took 14.99% of the vote and 12 seats, with the PAP winning 65 seats without contesting the Marine Parade-Braddell Heights GRC. The election marks the PAP's 16th successive election triumph since 1959, cementing its status as Singapore's longest uninterrupted governing party. The vote was held just nine days after the campaign began, and Prime Minister Lawrence Wong took office following a brief transition period.

orig_title: Grand Theft Auto VI release date pushed back until May 2026
text: Rockstar Games has announced that the release date of Grand Theft Auto VI has been pushed back to May 26, 2026, from its previously scheduled fall 2025 release. The company cited a desire to deliver a game that meets its high standards, stating that it aims to "exceed your expectations" and apologizes for the delay. The game is expected to be a major entertainment launch and follows the success of its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V, which remains popular eleven years after its launch.

orig_title: Former guitarist of pioneering death metal band Possessed dies in shootout with San Francisco police
text: A 60-year-old former guitarist of the death metal band Possessed, Brian Montana, was shot and killed by police during an armed shootout in San Francisco. The incident began over a dispute with a neighbor over tree clippings, with Montana reportedly pulling a gun on his neighbor and firing rounds at their house. The police engaged Montana in a 25-minute shootout, during which he used landscaping scenery and vehicles to shield himself. Montana was pronounced dead at the scene, and one resident in the house sustained a graze wound. The district attorney attributed the incident to alcohol involvement.

orig_title: Competitive local elections held in England
text: Local elections held in England on May 1, 2025, saw Reform UK, led by Nigel Farage, make significant gains. The party won 677 out of 1,600 council seats, taking control of 15 councils and winning the first female MP for the party. Labour Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Conservative opposition leader Kemi Badenoch lost ground, while the Liberal Democrats made strong gains. The Conservatives suffered their worst results in history, losing over 600 councillors and all 15 of their controlled councils. The Green Party also had mixed results, while the Labour Party's leader described the result as "disappointing".

orig_title: CSIRO releases 15 captive bred endemic spotted handfish into wild in Tasmania
text: CSIRO researchers have released 15 juvenile spotted handfish, a critically endangered species, into the wild near Hobart, Tasmania. The handfish, which have adapted pectoral fins resembling hands, were bred in captivity and provided with "handfish hotels" to aid adaptation. The researchers plan to monitor the fish closely for two weeks before removing the hotels, with the ultimate goal of ensuring their survival in the wild. The breeding program, supported by the Derwent Estuary Program, aims to boost the captive population and support the critically endangered species, which was first listed as endangered in 1996.

orig_title: Ukraine, US reach minerals deal
text: The US and Ukraine have reached a deal allowing the US to gain preferential access to new Ukrainian rare earth mineral deals, as well as creating a new fund to support Ukraine's rebuilding efforts. The agreement, signed in Washington, will prioritize US access to 55 minerals, including lithium and titanium, in exchange for monetary and military aid. Ukraine will deposit 50% of its future profits from government-owned resources into the new fund, which will be maintained for ten years. The deal was seen as a significant step towards strengthening cooperation between the two countries.

orig_title: Massive power outage hits Spain, Portugal

The shutdown led to widespread disruptions, including hospital power failures, cancelled flights, and evacuations. Authorities declared a state of emergency, and power was gradually restored by Tuesday morning, with Spain recovering over 92% of its power.

orig_title: Local South Carolinian police places male suspect of three injuries into custody after manhunt
text: A large-scale manhunt search took place in Sullivan's Island, South Carolina, after a driver struck two children and an adult outside Sunrise Presbyterian Church on May 1, 2025. orig_title: Stunt pilot Rob Holland dies after crashing experimental aircraft
text: Aerobatic pilot Rob Holland, 50, died in a plane crash at Langley Air Force Base in Virginia on Thursday. The cause of the crash is currently under investigation by the FAA, NTSB, and DOD. According to the National Transportation Safety Board, there were no acrobatic maneuvers involved and Holland was attempting a normal landing. The incident occurred just days before Holland was set to appear at the Air Power Over Hampton Roads airshow.

orig_title: Streaming platform Twitch bans rapper Kanye West seven minutes into first stream for performing "Nazi salute"

text: Black Sabbath has announced a final show with the original lineup, scheduled for July 5, 2025, at Villa Park in Birmingham, England. The performance, dubbed "The Back to the Beginning" show, will feature the band's original lineup of Ozzy Osbourne, Tony Iommi, Geezer Butler, and Bill Ward, who has rejoined the group after a 20-year absence. The show will also feature a supergroup of heavy metal acts and will be accompanied by a charity event, with all proceeds going to Cure Parkinson's, Birmingham Children's Hospital, and Acorns Children's Hospice.

orig_title: Shark fatally bites 17-year-old off Bribie Island
text: A 17-year-old girl, Charlize Zmuda, was bitten by a shark while swimming off Woorim Beach in Bribie Island, Queensland, on Monday. She was rescued by Surf Life Saving Queensland officers and paramedics, but died shortly after at 5:00 p.m. local time. The attack is the third shark incident in Queensland in less than three months, with the previous two fatal. Zmuda's father has spoken out, urging people not to stop visiting the beach, which is a big part of their lives. Flowers and green balloons have been placed at the beach to commemorate her death.

orig_title: Quran-burning refugee Salwan Momika fatally shot in Sweden apartment
text: A 38-year-old Iraqi refugee, Salwan Momika, was shot to death in his apartment in Södertälje, Stockholm, Sweden, on January 30. Authorities have apprehended five people in connection to the shooting, with Sweden's security services providing support due to potential links to foreign powers. Momika had been involved in a high-profile court case over burning a Quran in 2023, sparking tensions, and was scheduled to receive the verdict just hours before the shooting. Local media reported Momika was live-streaming on TikTok at the time of the incident.

orig_title: Air ambulance crashes into infrastructure in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania while transporting pediatric patient, no survivors
text: A small air ambulance crashed into a residential and commercial area in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, killing everyone on board, including six passengers and at least one person on the ground. The Learjet 55 was transporting a Mexican pediatric patient and her mother, as well as medical personnel, before losing altitude and crashing. The cause of the crash is unknown, and officials warn that the death toll could rise as they investigate the incident. Debris from the plane has been scattered across the area, and residents are advised to avoid the accident zone due to safety concerns.

orig_title: Addu City Council opens Hankede Bridge in Maldives
text: The Addu City Council has officially opened the 1.4 km long Hankede Bridge in the Maldives to the public, after delays in its completion. The bridge, which was initially announced to open in July but was postponed several times, was finally inaugurated on February 1, 2024, during a ceremony attended by India's Minister of External Affairs. The construction of the bridge faced controversy, including a dispute over seized sand intended for the project. The bridge connects Maradhoo and Gaukedi and is part of a larger development project in the region.

orig_title: Passenger plane collides with military helicopter near Washington, D.C.
text: A mid-air collision occurred on January 29 near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, involving a Bombardier CRJ700 operated by PSA for American Airlines and a US Army Black Hawk helicopter. Both aircraft crashed into the Potomac River, killing all 64 on board the plane and two crew members on the helicopter. The FAA and NTSB have launched an investigation, while airport officials have reported the airport will remain closed until January 30. US President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance have issued statements, and American Airlines CEO Robert Isom has offered condolences.

orig_title: Larry Rhoden replaces outgoing Kristi Noem as Governor of South Dakota
text: Larry Rhoden was sworn in as the 34th Governor of South Dakota on Monday, succeeding Kristi Noem after she resigned to serve as Secretary of the Department of Homeland Security. A private ceremony took place in Pierre, followed by a public ceremony on February 8 at the State Capitol Rotunda. Rhoden, who previously served as Lieutenant Governor under Noem, is the third governor in South Dakota's history to be appointed without winning an election. He took the oath on two Bibles, one belonging to his mother and another carried by his father during World War II.

orig_title: US President Trump orders government recognize male, female as only sexes
text: US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order revoking recognition of non-binary gender identities, declaring that only male and female are valid sexes. The order removes government diversity, equity, and inclusion programs and revokes the option for individuals to select "X" as their gender on government identification documents, including passports. The move has sparked criticism from LGBTQ groups, who say it targets and hurts their communities, with the Human Rights Campaign calling it a "harmful provision" that aims to "divide our communities".

orig_title: Times Square marks New Year's Eve 2025 in New York City
text: People gathered in Times Square, New York, to celebrate the New Year's Eve ball drop, despite stormy weather. Crowds braved rain and wind to see the iconic ball descend, with many people writing messages on confetti before it dropped. The event was part of Dick Clark's New Year's Rockin' Eve, which featured performances and crowd control measures. The ball was retired and replaced after the countdown, with preparations beginning weeks in advance. The event also included a "Good Riddance Day" event, where people wrote things they wanted to leave behind in 2024 and shared their messages with scientists working on cancer treatments.

orig_title: Chilean president Gabriel Boric makes historic trip to South Pole becoming the first head of state to visit and third head of government
text: Chilean President Gabriel Boric has made a historic trip to the South Pole, becoming the first sitting head of state to reach the continent's southernmost point. Boric's visit, part of "Operation Polar Star III," aimed to reaffirm Chile's sovereignty claim over its part of Antarctica and emphasize the country's strategic interest in the region. Accompanied by his defense and environment ministers, Boric spent approximately two hours at the US research base, stating that the trip was a "confirmation of our claim to sovereignty."

orig_title: Luigi Mangione, suspect in killing of US healthcare CEO, charged with terrorism
text: New York District Attorney Alvin Bragg has charged Luigi Mangione, 26, with first-degree murder in connection with the killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson in Manhattan. Mangione is accused of carrying out the attack with the intent to "sow terror" and faces life in prison with no parole. Mangione was arrested in Pennsylvania on December 9 and found to be in possession of a "ghost gun" and fake IDs. He was originally from Maryland and had been missing for several days before his mother reported him missing. A court hearing is scheduled for December 19 to determine Mangione's extradition to New York.

orig_title: South Korean president impeached by nation's parliament
text: South Korea's National Assembly voted 204 to 85 to impeach President Yoon Suk Yeol, following his declaration of martial law amid months of political turmoil. The vote was approved by the ruling People Power Party, with 12 members supporting impeachment and 85 opposing. Yoon has been suspended from office, and Prime Minister Han Duck-soo is acting president. The decision is subject to ratification by the Constitutional Court, which has 180 days to make a decision. The court has vowed to hold a speedy and fair trial, and an election to replace Yoon must be held within 60 days if the court votes to remove him from office.

orig_title: FBI Director Christopher Wray to resign
text: US FBI Director Christopher A. Wray has announced his resignation prior to Donald Trump's inauguration, citing a desire to avoid further conflict and protect the FBI's values. Trump had previously threatened to fire Wray, who was nominated by him in 2017 to replace James Comey. Wray's resignation will take effect at the end of the current administration, January next year. Trump has welcomed the move, calling it a "great day for America". Kash Patel, a former Trump aide, has been nominated as the new head of the FBI.

orig_title: Indian chess grandmaster Gukesh Dommaraju, 18, becomes youngest world chess champion of all time
text: Gukesh Dommaraju, an 18-year-old Indian chess grandmaster, has become the youngest world chess champion in history, defeating Ding Liren of China in the World Chess Championship in Singapore. The match was described as tight and on the verge of a tie, but Dommaraju's victory was attributed to a fatal error made by Liren late in the game. Dommaraju, hailed as a "chess prodigy", surpasses Russian grandmaster Garry Kasparov's record of being the world's youngest champion, set in 1985 at 22 years old.

orig_title: Ruby slippers worn by American actress Judy Garland in 1939 film The Wizard of Oz break sales record, sold for US$28 million at auction
text: A pair of ruby slippers worn by Judy Garland in the 1939 film The Wizard of Oz sold at Heritage Auctions in the US for $28 million to an anonymous buyer, setting an all-time record for highest selling price on an entertainment memorabilia item. The shoes, which have been called the "Holy Grail of Hollywood memorabilia", exceeded estimations by $25 million, with a buyer's premium adding $4.5 million. Only four pairs of ruby slippers from the film have survived, and the shoes were previously stolen from a museum in 2005 before being recovered in 2018. Over 800 people bid on the shoes, with the Judy Garland Museum among them.

orig_title: World leaders attend grand reopening of Notre Dame Cathedral in Paris five years after damaging fire
text: Notre-Dame de Paris has reopened in Paris after five years of closure following a devastating fire in 2019. Approximately 50 world leaders attended a grand reopening event over the weekend, which highlighted the cathedral's art, culture, and history. The ceremony was moved indoors due to bad weather and was attended by French President Emmanuel Macron, who described the cathedral as a "happy metaphor of what nation is and what the world should be". The rebuilding process, which began in 1345, required the work of 1,200 artisans and is complete. The cathedral is set to hold its first mass on Sunday.

orig_title: President of South Korea declares and lifts martial law
text: South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol declared martial law late Tuesday night, citing local unrest caused by "anti-state forces" as the motivation. The military law was lifted just hours later, but the National Assembly filed an impeachment motion, citing President Yoon's actions as a threat to democracy. Lawmakers and demonstrators clashed with soldiers outside the National Assembly building, but the Assembly voted 190-0 to lift martial law. President Yoon has accused the Assembly of "reckless actions" and requested them to stop their impeachment efforts, but the cabinet ultimately voted to lift martial law.

orig_title: Impeachment of South Korean president Yoon Suk Yeol fails
text: South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol's motion to impeach him failed as most members of his ruling party abstained from voting in the National Assembly session. The move came after President Yoon declared and lifted martial law on Tuesday, sparking widespread concern and calls for his resignation. Yoon apologized to his constituents, citing recent political adversity, including a scandal involving his alleged misuse of influence. The declaration was met with backlash from lawmakers, who voted 190-0 to annul the decision, sparking fears of nationwide protests.

orig_title: Suspect in shooting death of UnitedHealthcare CEO fled New York City by bus, police say
text: New York authorities believe the suspect in the murder of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson has fled the city and is no longer in New York. The suspect, who was wearing a mask during the attack, was seen on video fleeing on bicycle before taking a taxi to the Port Authority bus terminal. Police have recovered a backpack believed to have belonged to the shooter and released photos showing the suspect unmasked at a hostel. The suspect's face was concealed during the attack, but the locations accessible from the bus terminal suggest they may have traveled to various destinations, including New Jersey, Philadelphia, and Washington, D.C.

orig_title: Manslaughter charges against Daniel Penny dismissed following jury deadlock
text: A Manhattan judge has dismissed a manslaughter charge against Daniel Penny, an ex-Marine accused of choking a homeless man to death in 2023. The jury became deadlocked, prompting the judge to dismiss the charge and order a new trial on a lesser charge of criminally negligent homicide. The maximum penalty for the new charge is four years in prison. Penny's defense team argued that he acted in self-defense, while the prosecution claimed he used excessive force. The case will now proceed with the jury deciding on the new charge.

orig_title: Court ruling upholds TikTok ban unless ByteDance sells stake
text: The US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit has upheld a ban on TikTok if its China-based parent firm, ByteDance, refuses to sell its stake in the company. The ruling, which was made unanimously, argued that the ban is necessary to secure national security due to TikTok's "expansive reach." The US Justice Department commended the decision, while TikTok's spokesperson plans to appeal to the Supreme Court, claiming the ruling was based on "inaccurate" information. The ruling is seen as a victory for US national security officials who have expressed concerns about the app's association with the Chinese Communist Party.

orig_title: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire faces several violations
text: Israel launched a wave of airstrikes across Lebanon on Monday, killing 11 civilians, in response to a Hezbollah attack on Israeli forces. The ceasefire agreement, proposed by the US, was meant to be in effect since November 28, but has been repeatedly violated by both sides. Hezbollah claims Israel breached the ceasefire and launched the attack as a warning shot, while Israel says Hezbollah repeatedly violated the agreement. Strikes continue, with both sides accusing each other of ceasefire violations.

orig_title: United States President-elect and Canadian Prime Minister have dinner in Palm Beach, Florida
text: Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau met with US President-elect Donald Trump at Mar-a-Lago on November 29 to discuss Trump's plan to impose significant tariffs on Canadian goods. The meeting follows a phone call between the two on November 2, during which Trudeau criticized the plan, citing its potential harm to Canadians and American businesses. Despite Trudeau's previous criticism, the two leaders appeared to have had a positive discussion, with Trudeau stating that their conversation was "excellent" and Trump describing it as "very productive".

orig_title: World AIDS Day 2024 is marked around the world
text: World AIDS Day 2024 marked its 37th commemoration on December 1, with governments and NGOs around the world raising awareness about acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS) and human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). The UN's theme, "Take the rights path" to end AIDS, emphasizes a human rights-focused approach. Various countries, including the US, Latin America, and South Africa, held events and announced initiatives to address the issue, such as expanding HIV treatment and prevention programs. The 95-95-95 target, aimed at treating 95% of people living with HIV, is set to be fulfilled in 2025.

orig_title: International Criminal Court issues arrest warrants for Netanyahu, Gallant, and Deif over alleged war crimes in Israel-Hamas war
text: The International Criminal Court (ICC) has issued arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, former Defense Minister Yoav Gallant, and senior Hamas military leader Mohammed Deif, accusing them of war crimes and crimes against humanity during the 2023-2024 Israel-Hamas war. The ICC's decision has sparked differing opinions from countries and organizations, with some, like the European Union, supporting the court's involvement. The warrants make Netanyahu and others internationally wanted suspects, exposing them to potential arrest during foreign travel.

orig_title: Princess Yuriko of Mikasa, Japan's oldest royal family member, dies at 101
text: Japan's Princess Mikasa, Yuriko, passed away on November 14 at the age of 101, becoming the last member of the Imperial house born in the Taishō era and the oldest since the Meiji era. Her health declined in recent days, with a final examination revealing overall body function issues. A grand funeral is set for November 26, with Princess Akiko as chief mourner, and the Imperial Household agency has invited people to sign a condolences book at the estate. The Emperor Emeritus and Empress Emerita also sent their condolences.

orig_title: Trump wins 2024 U.S. presidential election, securing 312 electoral votes and all swing states
text: Donald Trump secured 312 electoral votes, surpassing the 270 required to win the US presidential election, after winning key swing states like Wisconsin, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Georgia, North Carolina, and Nevada. Trump received approximately 50.5% of the popular vote, totaling around 74 million votes, compared to Kamala Harris's 48.0%. Trump will be inaugurated as the 47th president of the United States on January 20. The Republican Party retained control of the Senate, while the outcome of the House of Representatives election remains uncertain.

orig_title: Smithsonian National Zoo euthanizes elderly Asian elephant
text: Kamala, a 50-year-old Asian elephant at the Smithsonian National Zoo in Washington, D.C., was euthanized on November 2 due to irreversible osteoarthritis. The condition, which affects joint and bone health, was managed with monthly injections, but her condition declined rapidly. Born in Sri Lanka in 1975, Kamala was raised at a sanctuary and later had two calves at the Calgary Zoo before being transferred to the Smithsonian National Zoo in 2014. She served as an ambassador for her species and contributed to the birth of at least a dozen elephant calves worldwide.

orig_title: Lancet release yearly Countdown report raising alarm of increase in heat caused deaths
text: The Lancet Countdown report for 2024 highlights worsening environmental issues, including increased exposure to extreme temperatures, with an average person facing 50 more days of dangerous heat this year compared to 2023. The report found that only a quarter of countries can assess early symptoms of heat-related health issues and less than 10% for mental health concerns. The authors also note a concerning trend of new fossil fuel mining sites despite the need for renewable energy. The report warns of a 1.45°C warmer planet by 2023 and a projected 2.7°C heating by 2100, calling for urgent action to reverse climate change and pollution impacts.

orig_title: Russian court fines Google more money than the world's entire GDP
text: A Russian court has fined Google $20 trillion, making it an amount beyond the world's GDP, for blocking Russian state media channels on YouTube. The fine was handed down after a 2020 lawsuit by 17 Russian TV channels and media outlets. Google's Russian YouTube subsidiary had paused commercial operations following US sanctions on Russia in response to its 2022 invasion of Ukraine. The court ordered Google to restore the accounts within nine months, with a daily fine of $1,000 after that.

orig_title: Indian and Spanish leaders inaugurate India's first private military aircraft facility
text: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez have jointly inaugurated India's first private-sector Final Assembly Line for manufacturing military aircraft, located in Vadodara, Gujarat. The facility, a joint venture between Airbus SE and Tata Advanced Systems Limited, will manufacture 56 aircraft, with 16 assembled in Spain and 40 made in India. The deal, worth US$2.5 billion, aims to replace ageing Hawker Siddeley planes used by the Indian Air Force. The facility marks a significant milestone in India's military aviation capabilities and strengthens bilateral ties between India and Spain.

orig_title: Grateful Dead bassist Phil Lesh dies, aged 84
text: Phil Lesh, the former bassist and vocalist of the Grateful Dead, has died at the age of 84, surrounded by loved ones. Born in 1940, Lesh was a key member of the iconic rock band, playing bass guitar and singing on many of their songs, including the hit "Box of Rain". After the band's breakup in 1995, Lesh continued to collaborate with fellow Dead members and maintained a successful solo career. He is survived by his widow Jill and their sons, Brian and Grahame. No cause of death was given.

orig_title: Qantas Australian airline employees strike for better wages
text: Hundreds of unionized Qantas workers went on strike on Wednesday, affecting Melbourne and Brisbane airports. The strike, which included 24 hours of no work by engineers, was in response to a five percent yearly wages increase and a one-off 15 percent increase. Qantas management deemed the demands "unsustainable." The workers, who have had their wages frozen for three-and-a-half years, chanted slogans such as "Who keeps the planes flying? We do!" during the strike. The Qantas Engineers Alliance, comprising the Australian Manufacturing Workers' Union and others, began bargaining in April.

orig_title: New Zealand defeats South Africa to win 2024 women's T20 cricket world cup
text: New Zealand wins 2024 ICC Women's T20 World Cup title, defeating South Africa by 32 runs in the tournament final. The Black Caps posted 158/5 in their innings, with Amelia Kerr scoring 43 runs and taking three wickets. South Africa struggled to chase the target, managing 126/9, with Laura Wolvaardt scoring 33 runs. Amelia Kerr was named Player of the Match and Tournament for her all-round performance. New Zealand's victory marks their first Women's T20 World Cup title, with Kerr hailing it as a "dream come true" after the team's journey.

orig_title: Bruce Lehrmann judge said to have no links to published book of judgement
text: A book titled "He Went Back for His Hat" about Judge Michael Lee's judgement in the Bruce Lehrmann defamation trial will be published by Melbourne University Publishing. The book's title refers to a quote by Lee describing Lehrmann's actions as "going back for his hat" after escaping legal consequences. The judge had previously presided over the trial, which concluded with him finding Lehrmann guilty of raping complainant Brittany Higgins. The book's publication has sparked no issue with Judge Lee, who was approached by the publisher in advance.

orig_title: TV host Willie Revillame files certificate of candidacy for upcoming Philippine elections
text: Filipino TV host Willie Revillame has filed his Certificate of Candidacy with the Commission on Elections to run for senator in the 2025 midterm elections. Revillame, known for hosting variety shows, made the announcement at a prayer rally in Davao City on January 28, stating he had previously been offered a chance to join the senatorial slate of former President Rodrigo Duterte and Senator Bong Go. Revillame declined at the time due to contractual obligations with his show, Wowowin.

orig_title: Massachusetts Institute of Technology engineers tap access to battery-less desalination of more groundwater than ever before
text: Researchers at Massachusetts Institute of Technology have developed a new battery-less solar desalination plant technology that can desalinate water without connecting to the power grid. The system adjusts desalination rates in real-time to account for changes in solar irradiance, allowing it to handle variations in electric current caused by weather. The prototype, tested in New Mexico, demonstrated the ability to desalinate an average of 5,000 liters of water per day, making it suitable for processing brackish groundwater in drought-affected regions. This innovation could provide access to clean water in areas previously inaccessible due to technological limitations.

orig_title: Former leader of the Scottish National Party Alex Salmond dies at 69
text: Former Scottish National Party leader Alex Salmond has died on October 12, 2024, at the age of an unknown age. He collapsed at a conference in North Macedonia, apparently due to a heart attack, shortly after making a speech. Salmond was a key figure in Scotland's independence movement and served as the country's first minister to do so. His death has been met with tributes from UK politicians, including Prime Minister Keir Starmer, who described Salmond as someone who "cared deeply about Scotland and communities he represented".

orig_title: Data breach and DDOS attacks bring down Wayback Machine
text: The Internet Archive suffered a data breach of 31 million user passwords and screen names, followed by a wave of distributed denial-of-service (DDOS) attacks, making the Wayback Machine inaccessible. The breach is believed to have occurred on September 28 and was attributed to a hacker group operating from Russia, claiming political motivation. The hackers accused the US government of supporting Israel, sparking the cyberattack. The Archive's staff is working to upgrade security and is expected to restore access to the Wayback Machine within the next several days.

orig_title: New Zealand Navy ship HMNZS Manawanui capsizes one nautical mile from shore
text: A New Zealand Navy ship, HMNZS Manawanui, ran aground off the coast of Samoa on Saturday evening while conducting an aquatic terrain survey. The ship caught fire and partially sank, but all 72 crew members were safely evacuated and taken ashore. Rescue efforts were assisted by the Royal New Zealand Air Force and a local air force unit, with medical and welfare support provided on site. Three crew members were left stranded in Samoa and were later transported back to New Zealand on commercial flights.

orig_title: Hololive VTuber Watson Amelia holds last livestream
text: Watson Amelia, a member of Hololive Production's English-speaking branch, has ended her streaming activities on October 1, after previously announcing her decision on September 21. She debuted in 2020 and became the fourth most popular English VTuber, earning significant revenue from Superchat donations and ad revenue. Her YouTube channel has 1.8 million subscribers. Watson's departure is not considered a "graduation" as she will remain affiliated with the agency and work with it occasionally. Hololive Production has announced they will continue to sell her merchandise and provide updates on her and the agency through their official social media channels.

orig_title: Prosecutors charge man with attempted assassination of former US President Donald Trump
text: A 58-year-old man, Ryan Wesley Routh, has been charged with attempting to assassinate former US President Donald Trump at Trump International Golf Club in Florida on September 15. Routh faces three additional charges, including attempting to assassinate a presidential candidate and assaulting a federal officer. If convicted, he could face life in prison. Prosecutors have revealed details of their investigation, including a note written by Routh about his plans to kill Trump, and a 12-hour stakeout at the golf course.

orig_title: Prime Minister of Canada Justin Trudeau survives a no confidence vote
text: Canada's prime minister Justin Trudeau has survived a vote of no confidence in his minority Liberal government, with 211 MPs voting against a motion of no confidence and 120 in favor. The Conservative Party, led by Pierre Poilievre, had urged MPs to vote in favor of the motion, but ultimately failed to secure a majority. The vote comes after the New Democratic Party backed out of a deal to keep Trudeau in power until an election in October 2025, leaving him with reduced support. Trudeau's approval rating has been in decline, with 28% of Canadians expressing support for him.

orig_title: Thousands of pagers explode in Lebanon killing twelve people and injuring thousands
text: A series of coordinated pager explosions in southern Beirut and the Bekaa Valley, Lebanon, on Tuesday and Wednesday killed 32 people and injured over 3,200. The blasts targeted Hezbollah, a Lebanese Shia Islamist group, and were suspected to be caused by explosives or faulty batteries. Investigations suggested the pagers had been tampered with, possibly with added metal balls to increase the impact of an explosion. The incident was reportedly timed to coincide with Hezbollah's investigation into inconsistent battery life of the pagers.

orig_title: Around 8,000 Rohingya Muslims have fled to Bangladesh
text: Bangladesh has reported a surge of 8,000 Rohingya Muslim refugees from Myanmar over the past two months, amid intensifying conflict in Rakhine state. With the country already overwhelmed, officials are calling for international aid to address a humanitarian crisis. Myanmar's military junta and the Arakan Army's attacks on Rohingya have made it impossible for them to return home. Bangladesh is urging India and other countries to allow refugees to enter and pressure the Arakan Army to cease its attacks. A cabinet meeting is scheduled to discuss the refugee situation this week.

orig_title: Four killed in Apalachee High School shooting in Georgia, United States
text: Two 14-year-old students and two teachers were killed in a mass shooting at Apalachee High School in Winder, Georgia, on Wednesday. Nine people, including eight students and one teacher, were hospitalized but are expected to survive. The suspect, a 14-year-old student named Colt Gray, was taken into custody after a brief confrontation with school resource officers. Authorities are investigating how Gray obtained the AR-15 style rifle used in the shooting. This is the 45th school shooting in the US this year, the deadliest so far.

orig_title: SpaceX will return stranded astronauts in February 2025, NASA announces
text: NASA has announced that astronauts Sunita Williams and Barry Wilmore will return home from the International Space Station on a SpaceX Crew Dragon spacecraft in February 2025, after a Boeing Starliner spacecraft was grounded due to issues. The Boeing Starliner was expected to transport the crew but experienced helium leaks and thruster malfunctions, rendering it unsuitable for a crewed mission. The Crew Dragon will carry two astronauts instead of the planned four, allowing Williams and Wilmore to return to Earth safely. The astronauts will remain on the ISS for several months as part of Expedition 71/72.

orig_title: India wins T20 men's cricket world cup against South Africa
text: India wins seventh T20 World Cup match against South Africa at Kensington Oval Stadium in Barbados, emerging victorious by seven runs. India scored 176 runs for seven wickets, with Virat Kohli top-scoring with 76. South Africa scored 169 runs for eight wickets, falling short. Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli announced their retirement from T20 international cricket after the match. Jasprit Bumrah was awarded Player of the Tournament for his 15 wickets. The win marks India's second victory in the tournament, held from June 2-29.

orig_title: Azov Brigade to be allowed to use US weapons
text: The US State Department has lifted a 10-year-old ban on the Azov Brigade, a Ukrainian unit accused of being far-right and neo-Nazi, after determining it had not committed human rights violations. The brigade, designated as a 12th Special Forces Brigade in the Ukrainian National Guard, was previously barred from using American weapons and attending US-led military exercises. The decision comes after the US found no evidence of gross human rights abuses by the brigade, which has been accused by Russia of being a terrorist organization since 2022.

orig_title: Israel Defense Forces rescue four hostages in Gaza
text: The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) announced the successful rescue of four hostages held by Hamas in Gaza, bringing an end to an eight-month ordeal. The hostages, aged 26-41, were freed in a daring operation involving two helicopters. The IDF reported that the hostages were in good medical condition and being treated at a hospital. One Israeli police officer was killed in the operation, while Hamas has reportedly suffered fewer casualties. The release comes after a complex and violent conflict that has resulted in significant loss of life on both sides, with estimates ranging from 1,139 Israelis killed to 35,000 Palestinians killed by Hamas.

orig_title: Israel Defense Forces discover tunnel in child's bedroom in Rafah
text: The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) reported discovering a tunnel in a child's bedroom in Rafah belonging to Hamas, along with a butcher's knife and explosives. The same day, six militants were "eliminated" by UAV and tank fire near a school. The discovery comes amid escalating tensions following the October 7, 2023 attack, which killed 1,139 Israelis and injured many others. The attack, which saw over 3,000 Hamas gunmen cross the border and fire thousands of rockets, sparked a declaration of war on Hamas. The conflict has resulted in thousands of deaths and numerous reports of war crimes.

orig_title: Vladimir Putin threatens to give allies weapons to attack West
text: Russian President Vladimir Putin has warned that Russia could provide weapons to other countries to strike Western nations, in response to the US and Germany allowing Ukraine to use Western-supplied weapons on Russian territory. Putin described this as a "dangerous step" that harms Russo-German relations and Russia's sovereignty. He also warned that Russia reserves the right to act in self-defense, stating that the response can be asymmetric and that Russia would consider using all means at its disposal if its territorial integrity is threatened. The warning comes amid tensions over the use of nuclear weapons in the conflict.

orig_title: IDF missile strikes UN school
text: Israeli forces launched a missile attack on a UN-operated school in the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza, killing 35-45 people, including civilians. The attack targeted Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad militants hiding in the school. The Israel Defense Forces claim the attack was planned to minimize civilian casualties, but witnesses describe chaotic scenes with shattered glass, debris, and smoke filling the air. The death toll in Gaza now stands at over 36,000, with UNRWA reporting that 186 of their installations have been affected.

orig_title: Dutch F-16s supplied to Ukraine to be used in Russian airspace
text: The Netherlands plans to donate 24 American-made F-16 fighter jets to Ukraine, allowing them to strike within Russian airspace, with the condition that Ukraine complies with international law and UN Charter. The move is part of a four-nation effort, including Belgium, Denmark, and the US, to supply F-16s to Ukraine. NATO's influence over the US allows the Netherlands to proceed without permission. The jets will replace lost aircraft and provide improved capabilities, including stronger radar and air-to-air combat capabilities.

orig_title: The Ancient Pyramids of the World, a new photo exhibition by Viktor Pinchuk took place in Crimea
text: Russian photographer Viktor Pinchuk's exhibition of works at the Genoese Fortress Museum-Reserve in Sudak, Crimea, coincided with the annual "Night of Geography" event of the Russian Geographical Society. The exhibition showcased Pinchuk's photographs of archaeological monuments from around the world, including the Pulemelei Mound in Samoa, which is almost completely destroyed. The exhibition, now in its digital format, aims to encourage visitors to explore and study historical and geographical objects, highlighting the importance of understanding the planet's cultural heritage. The exhibition is part of Pinchuk's extensive travels to Africa, Asia, Oceania, and Latin America.

orig_title: Severe weather affects portions of Texas
text: A powerful storm swept across eastern Texas, including Tyler, on Monday evening, causing widespread damage and power outages. Heavy rain and high winds hit the area, knocking out electricity to 68,000 homes in Smith County by Tuesday morning. Randwick includes the areas of Clovelly, Coogee, Maroubra, Malabar, Little Bay (Malabar Beach), La Perouse (Frenchmans Bay), and Yarra Bay. The proposal suggests that new signs and parking meters will be introduced at the end of 2026 and 2027 if the proposal is approved.

orig_title: Green Party wins major by-election in northern England city of Manchester
text:
The Green Party of England and Wales has announced its candidate, Hannah Spencer, as the winner of the recent by-election in Gorton and Denton, a parliamentary constituency in Manchester. The election was triggered by the resignation of the previous Labour MP, Andrew Gwynne. This marks the first time a Green Party candidate has won in a parliamentary election and the first time the Green Party has won in North England. Spencer will become the fifth current Green Party MP, with only 41% of the vote share, a margin of 12% over the second-placed candidate, Matt Goodwin of Reform UK, who received around 29% of the vote.

The election was highly anticipated as it was a test of the stability of the current Labour government, which has faced numerous high-profile scandals in recent months. The Labour candidate received around 25% of the vote, which is 25% below the 50% of the vote they received in 2024 in the general election. The seat was previously considered the sixth safest Labour seat in Britain and had not been lost by a Labour candidate since 1931.

The Mayor of Greater Manchester, Andy Burnham, had sought to become the party's candidate but was excluded by the National Executive Committee due to concerns that the Labour Party would lose the next mayoral election and that Burnham would start a leadership campaign against Prime Minister Keir Starmer. Former Deputy Labour Party leader and former Deputy Prime Minister Angela Rayner said that this result was a "wake-up call" and added that it would put further pressure on Keir Starmer within the party to leave. Starmer stated in a statement that he was not planning to resign after the elections.

The Reform candidate Matt Goodwin received 29% of the vote, which is 15% more than the party's share in the previous general election. He cited BBC staff and said that the Green Party had won because of a "coalition of Islamists and growing progressive forces" coming together to dominate the election, and said that "many people in this country will see Gorton and Denton as being disgusted by what they see". The Conservative and Liberal Democratic Party local representative also received less than 2% of the vote, with the Conservative Party losing 6% of their previous vote share and the Liberal Democratic Party losing 2%. This is the second time that the Conservative Party has lost their seat, since 1962, and the worst result for the party in a campaign.

orig_title: Strong earthquakes in Indian and Pacific Oceans
text: A 6.2-magnitude earthquake occurred in the Banda Sea in Indonesia yesterday, and two similar earthquakes occurred in the Pacific Ring of Fire. There are currently no reported damages from 9am today. These are the strongest earthquakes since Monday. The Indonesian earthquake occurred in the thin archipelago of Maluku, northwest of Australia, at 5:46am UTC on Thursday (9:46am Friday, Darwin time). The Maluku Islands are located in the earthquake-prone Pacific Ring of Fire between New Guinea and Sulawesi. The Indonesian earthquake was felt 600 km south of the epicenter in Darwin, northern Australia.

orig_title: United States capture Venezuelan president, Nicolás Maduro
text:
The BBC reports on air raids in Caracas, which targeted the military bases La Carlota and Fort Tiuna, suspected of being involved with the US in Maduro. Additionally, other locations are also reportedly targeted. According to local authorities, civilians have been killed and injured, but the exact numbers are unknown. It was also reported that the operation was led by a CIA infiltration of the Venezuelan government. France 24 reported that the CIA has been tracking Maduro since August, despite his efforts to change his position multiple times. The operation reportedly involved over 150 military aircraft, including a helicopter intended to capture Maduro.

According to US authorities, the Delta-Force special unit reached Maduro's home at 2:01 local time and captured him before taking him on a ship, after crossing the coast of Venezuela at 3:29 am. Trump later revealed that Maduro's wife, Cilia Flores, was also taken into custody, and both were taken on the USS Iwo Jima (LHD-7) en route to South East NY to be tried. General Prosecutor Pam Bondi said that he would experience the full wrath of the American legal system on American soil in American courts. After CNN, it was announced that a conviction for leading "state-controlled gangs" and supporting drug trafficking was expected.

The Venezuelan government also reported other air raids, intended to secure oil and mineral resources, and issued a national invitation. Along with Cuba, Colombia, Iran, and Russia, they condemned the action as a "serious military aggression". The President of Argentina, Javier Milei, supported the action. The Vice President of Venezuela, Delcy Rodríguez, demanded the release of Maduro and his wife, as the operation had violated the country's sovereignty. The BBC reported that these air raids followed over 30 attacks on Venezuelan ships, and a "port area" in Maracaibo that resulted in over 110 deaths. The Trump administration stated that it was a "non-international armed conflict" with "suspicious drug traffickers". After the capture, the US Department of Justice made a detention request against Maduro, accusing him and others of being part of a "coalition to reach terrorists" and "coalition to import cocaine". Maduro denied the allegations, stating that Trump's true goal was to gain access to Venezuela's oil reserves, as seen in the US decision to seize multiple oil tankers.

orig_title: Wikinews attends Veterans Day event in Texas, United States
text: On Tuesday, Wikinews visited a Veterans Day event in New Chapel Hill, Texas. 21 military veterans and an active National Guard member were interviewed on stage, while seated on stage. As each military branch was named, the corresponding members stood up to the audience's enthusiasm. Around 480 people attended the celebration. The event was held to honor veterans and current US military personnel. In the US, the holiday is a time to honor men and women who served in the United States, marking the end of World War I as an armistice. The US holiday recognizes veterans from all branches and eras, thanking them for their sacrifices, bravery, and dedication. Texas communities held ceremonies, parades, and moments of silence to express their recognition. It's also a day to reflect on the freedoms protected by their service and support those who bear the weight of their duties.

orig_title: Turkish military transport plane crashes near Georgia border, 20 dead
text: A Turkish air transport plane, a C-130 Hercules, crashed near the border between Georgia and Azerbaijan on November 11, 2025, killing all 20 soldiers on board. The plane took off from the Ganja International Airport in Azerbaijan at 14:19 and was lost in the monitoring by the Georgian authorities 27 minutes later, while flying over the Georgian airspace. The Georgian authorities confirmed that the wreckage was found near the border region. Turkish Defense Minister Yaşar Güler announced that all soldiers were killed. The cause of the crash is still under investigation, with Turkish and Georgian officials working together.

orig_title: 2025 Queens World Film Festival features filmmakers breakfast and ceremony honoring Warrington Hudlin
text:
The Queens World Film Festival took place in the Astoria neighborhood of Queens, New York City, from November 6 to 9. Screenings were held at the Museum of the Moving Image, and organizers invited filmmakers to events, including a breakfast screening on November 8 and an awards ceremony. A more extensive program is planned, which will run until November 16.

On November 8, a morning meeting for filmmakers took place at Sac's Place in Astoria. Festival organizer Katha Cato introduced Brian F. Lee from City National Bank, who described the institution as "the bank of stars." Cato stated that the goal of the breakfast was to give filmmakers and financial advisors the opportunity to discuss ideas.

After the breakfast, the film "The Caravan" was screened, which tells the story of a man traveling from New York City to Canada to buy cheap insulin. The film team consisted of Doug Harris, Kathiamarice Lopez, and Sharina Martin, who also produced the film production company. The film was directed by Jefferson White and shot by Adam Volerich. The audience laughed at jokes, cheered at the end, and applauded during the credits.

Before the festival began, a press event took place on October 15. The award, known as the "2025 Spirit of Queens" prize, was awarded to Warrington Hudlin. Harriet Tugsmen spoke first and joked that Beyoncé was supposed to introduce the event. She added: "I am a local drag performer here in Astoria, Manhattan, Brooklyn, and sometimes internationally, because I travel to Jersey... Thank you for telling stories, your vision, your eyes, your dialogues, to give a picture of someone who is not heard, and please understand that I do not say "unheard" versus "silent," because we have our voice, and many people do not hear." The audience applauded.

Katha Cato took the speaker again and discussed the freedom of expression: "This is not the time to stop filming," before introducing Queens Borough President Donovan Richards Jr., who spoke about the diversity of Queens: "190 countries, 360 languages and dialects are spoken in this district." He added: "We will not be afraid, we will be proud to tell our story in Queens County."

Cato then introduced Sandra Schulberg and Donald Preston Cato. Schulberg described Hudlin as her idol and mentioned several films, including , , and . She discussed Hudlin's engagement in film conservation and archiving and mentioned that she had found the lost original version of the film by Gordon Parks in 2013, which Avery Brooks starred in. The film team was reunited.

Hudlin spoke then, first his mentors Melvin Van Peebles, who won the prize in 2016, Harry Belafonte, Ossie Davis, and Ruby Dee, and said: "It's not about me, it's about us." He named several people he had worked with in the audience, who he had worked with in the past. He explained that the new generation of filmmakers was "blessed" to tell these stories and closed with "We will not give up" and "Peace out."

There were two more short speeches after Hudlin's thank-you speech. The first was by Ralph Calle-Schulz from Rise Flix, who described his company as a platform that supports the "next big film director" and the "next big voice" for the next generation. The second was by the Slovenian artist and filmmaker Nataša Prosenc Stearns, who described herself as "things that are hard to categorize."

orig_title: Mamdani wins New York City mayoral election
text:
New Yorkers prefer democratic socialist Zohran Mamdani over Andrew Cuomo in mayoral election. Mamdani led the polls for weeks. In the Hamilton Heights section of Manhattan, voters discussed what matters to them. In a limited survey, all of them said they voted for Mamdani.

"A man listens to people and sees what people want and why they choose other people," said a German-American woman who recently received citizenship but didn't want to reveal her name.

Her husband, who also voted for Mamdani, said he wanted a change in politicians. "I chose a new growth rate. The city needs that," he added, and also mentioned that he voted for Mark Levine. Through an interpreter, Maria Nuñez said she would vote for the first time. Mamdani's campaign motivated her to vote. "Council members say things that are different from other politicians."

Another woman, who didn't want to reveal her name, added hints on why she voted for Mamdani: "I sometimes feel like change is not always easy, but sometimes it's necessary."

She pointed to "home accessibility and education accessibility" as the changes she wanted. "ABC: Not Cuomo," she said.

During the visit, Bürgermeisterkandidat Edafe Okporo was also found in New York City's district 7.

"I love apartments for New Yorkers at a fair price. But people in the community say that people working on the adjacent housing project don't have a connection to the community," Okporo explained to Wikimedia New York City. "That's just an example of what's happening all over West Harlem and Hamilton Heights."

"I thought politics was a way to fight for these changes in our community, but I quickly learned that politics is not only the place for ideas, but also where the highest buyer wields his influence," said Okporo. "No reputation should be a monopoly."

orig_title: India wins 2025 Women's Cricket World Cup, defeating South Africa by 52 runs
text:
India won the 2025 ICC Women's Cricket World Cup, defeating South Africa by 52 runs in the final at the DY Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai. The tournament was held in India, marking India's first Women's World Cup title. South Africa won the toss and chose to bowl first. India scored 298 for 7 in 50 overs, led by Shafali Verma's 87 and Deepti Sharma's 58. Smriti Mandhana supported her partner with a century of 100 runs with Verma for the first over. For South Africa, Ayabonga Khaka took three wickets, while Nonkululeko Mlaba, Nadine de Klerk and Chloe Tryon each took one wicket. India's total was the second-highest in a Women's World Cup final.

In a thrilling chase, South Africa started steadily, scoring 52 for 1 in the Powerplay. Laura Wolvaardt topped with a well-pasced century (101 for 98 balls), while Annerie Dercksen and Sune Luus each contributed 35 and 25 runs respectively. India's bowlers performed well in the middle overs. Deepti Sharma took five wickets and Shafali Verma two, so South Africa was bowled out for 246 runs.

Shafali Verma was chosen as the Man of the Match for her all-round performance. Deepti Sharma was awarded the Man of the Tournament prize.

After the game, Shafali Verma said, "I said from the beginning that God had sent me here to do something good, and it reflected today. Very happy that we won and can't speak about it. It was tough, but I had faith in myself - if I stay calm, I can do anything. My parents, my friends, my brother, everyone of them supported me and helped me understand how to play." South Africa captain Laura Wolvaardt congratulated India, saying, "I couldn't be prouder of this team. Unfortunately, we lost today - India played incredible cricket. We hoped for a bit of swing at the beginning and were in the chase for a long time, but we lost too many wickets... [In the field] I checked the scoreboard and they [India] were on 350. Our tail end was incredible."

orig_title: The Voluptuous Horror of Karen Black performs as part of Vaginal Davis' exhibit at MoMA PS1
text:
The Museum of Modern Art PS1 in Long Island City, Queens, New York, is opening on October 9, 2025, with the exhibition "Magnificent Product" by Vaginal Davis. The exhibition will showcase a significant portion of Davis's work from the last 50 years, as well as photographs by Berlin-based photographer Annette Frick. As part of the exhibition, Kembra Pfahler's "The Voluptuous Horror of Karen Black" will be performed in the museum's courtyard on October 11.

On the morning of the performance, the museum sent an email to a group of Eventbrite attendees warning them that they should be ready to arrive by 3 PM to ensure they could experience the entire program, due to expected high attendance. Although rain was forecasted beforehand, the weather eventually cleared.

Davis introduced the band, which performed a mix of old and new songs. The courtyard was nearly full, with spectators even climbing up the stairs to reach the stage area. During the performance of "Underwear Drawer," Pfahler and Alice Moy threw underwear onto the stage from a box. After the performance, Pfahler invited the audience and artists to come and say hello. The audience and artists mingled and took photos together until the museum closed.

orig_title: Crowds gather for 35th Tompkins Square Halloween Dog Parade amid car incident
text:
The 35th annual Tompkins Square Halloween Dog Parade took place from October 1-4. The event started at 5:00 PM UTC and ended at 8:00 PM UTC. Participants had to pre-register and pick up their tickets at the event.

At 7:00 PM, a car, decorated with taxi and limousine license plates, began driving between Avenues B and A on 10th Street, heading east through the crowd. The car honked and tried to navigate the crowded street filled with pedestrians, dogs, strollers, and wagons with children. The spectators were angry and confronted the driver, who, however, seemed unfazed and refused to intervene as his car was stopped by a police patrol car blocking the exit on Avenue A.

Several streets in the area, including 13th Street between Avenues A and B, 10th Street between Avenues A and B, and 6th Street between Avenues A and C, had dogs. Even in the park, dogs were present. The streets were closed for the parade, with spectators on both sides. On the 6th Street, there were several prepared stands for dog activities - a dog-friendly red carpet for dogs to pose on, a photographer who wanted to take pictures of dogs in the occasion. One of the dogs, a female dog named Izzy, was quite suspicious and ran away from the photo studio. Another dog, Tofu, a female dog who claimed to be running for president, was also present.

orig_title: Taskforce launched as search for Gus Lamont expands in South Australia's north
text:
A taskforce to search for a 4-year-old boy named August "Gus" Lamont has been set up at his family's home in the middle of South Australia, according to South Australian Police Commissioner Grant Stevens. The taskforce, which was announced on October 14 and named Taskforce Horizon, is made up of specialists who will take over the investigation.

Lamont is a 4-year-old boy who went missing on September 27 and was described by police as white with wavy blonde hair and wearing a grey hat, a blue Minions shirt, light grey pants, and boots. The investigation into his disappearance involved both the police and the Australian Defence Force (ADF). The surrounding area was searched in the evening of his disappearance, but no signs of him were found. Further searches, which covered an area of 120 and 480 meters around his home, were also unsuccessful. News.com.au reported that Lamont had played in the sand in his garden before he went missing. Yorke Mid North Superintendent Mark Syrus said that he believes Lamont may have moved further away from his home before he became lost and described him as "silent" but "adventurous". Syrus also said that the grandfather of the boy searched the neighbors in the evening but did not find him, and that other family members searched the area before contacting the authorities.

Commissioner Stevens assured that no signs of violence had been found and that the family is cooperating with the police. South Australian Premier Peter Malinauskas said that he had been informed about the situation and that no additional resources had been requested from the government. "It's a new attempt. I'm convinced that the police will handle the situation with all seriousness and care."

orig_title: New York judge rules terrorism charges legally insufficient in Mangione case
text:
Judge Gregory Carro in New York on Tuesday dismissed two of the charges against Luigi Mangione, the main suspect in the murder of Brian Thompson. Carro stated that the prosecution had not provided enough evidence to support the terrorism charges. He decided that the second-degree murder charge could be pursued.

Carro also determined that the two murder charges could not be considered terrorism because Mangione had not made any demands on the government or sought a specific policy change. Specifically, Carro dismissed the first-degree murder charge and the second-degree murder charge, while pursuing the other second-degree murder charge. In a written judgment released during the brief hearing, he wrote: "The charges against the defendant of first-degree murder (because he committed a terrorist act) and of second-degree murder as a terrorist crime are dismissed because the prosecution has presented sufficient evidence for all the other charges, including second-degree murder (premeditated act)."

The Manhattan district attorney's office released a statement: "We respect the court's decision and will continue to pursue the remaining nine charges, including second-degree murder."

Mangione is also facing federal murder charges, which could carry a death sentence, as reported by The Guardian and the BBC. Mangione was present in his prison uniform and handcuffs, as reported by The Guardian.

Mangione is allegedly responsible for Thompson's murder in December 2024 in Manhattan. Thompson was CEO of United Healthcare.

orig_title: German unemployment tops three million for first time since 2015
text:
The national unemployment rate in August reached 6.4% (or 3.025 million people), a 0.1% increase from the previous month. This milestone marks the first time since February 2015 that the 3-billion mark has been reached, according to Deutsche Welle.

According to RTÉ, the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate remained at 6.3% (2.96 million people), decreasing by 9,000 from July and increasing by 153,000 from the previous year, 0.3%. BA's broader unemployment rate, which includes both joblessness and short-term disability, reached 3.634 million, an increase of 25,000 from August 2024.

The inflation rate rose to 2.1% in August, exceeding the 2.0% forecast by analysts, according to CNBC.

Job applications in the primary sector have declined, with 631,000 job openings reported in August, 68,000 fewer than in the same month last year. The monthly Federal Employment Agency Job Index (BA-X), a labor market demand indicator, remained unchanged at 98 points.

In a press statement, BA Director Andrea Nahles said that the labor market has borne the consequences of three years of economic contraction, but now shows first signs of stabilization. She also noted that the numbers reflect the challenges faced by the manufacturing industry, citing a report by EY that the automotive industry lost 110,000 jobs last year. Nahles said she expected the typical seasonal reduction in September to improve the situation, but was waiting for the number of unemployed to rise above 3 million during the winter.

orig_title: Russian Justice Ministry designates former Putin advisor Sergey Markov as "foreign agent"
text:
The Russian Justice Ministry has again expanded its list of "Foreign Agents." What is unusual is the inclusion of a well-known Russian propagandist on the list. 

Sergey Markov, a former member of the Russian parliament and a longtime spokesperson for Vladimir Putin, was labeled a "Foreign Agent." He was responsible for the position of Russian authorities during the Russian invasion of Ukraine and was invited to write for the New York Times and Bloomberg. 

After his inclusion on the list, Markov wrote:

"I am not a Foreign Agent and it is clear to everyone. I have been supporting Putin's policy for 25 years and continue to do so. I am also under Canadian sanctions. This accusation is done by enemies of Russia and enemies of Putin's policy. These people will reveal themselves as traitors or be removed from office as corrupt officials."

He described the "error" and justified his position.

In June, Markov met with Mihail Gusman, the Vice-Director of the Russian state television, at a media forum in Azerbaijan. The relations between Azerbaijan and Russia deteriorated in the course of this year. Markov and Gusman supported the Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev, whom Markov called "brilliant thinker." Gusman was, however, dismissed after participating in the forum, after he had been in the position since 1999. Markov's statements caused discontent among Russian bloggers, such as Alexander Koc, who criticized Markow's "Azerbaijani story." The support for Azerbaijan is likely the reason for Markov's inclusion on the "Foreign Agent" list.

Markov also appeared in live streams with journalists who were labeled "Foreign Agents," such as Alexey Venediktov. Ironically, Markov supported measures against "Foreign Agents" and criticized them as well as famous Russian cultural figures who left Russia after its illegal invasion of Ukraine.

The laws regulating "Foreign Agents" were approved in Russia in 2012. These rules allow non-commercial organizations that are financed from outside and engage in political activities to be labeled "Foreign Agents." The criteria for such activities are not strictly defined, which allows organizations in areas such as education, healthcare, culture, ecology, and human rights to be pursued. These laws serve as a tool for repression in Russia and have been attributed to many critics of Putin. The Russian authorities used the "Foreign Agent" regulation as a justification to shut down groups like the human rights network Memorial and the Nobel Prize winner.

orig_title: American rapper Lil Nas X pleads not guilty of alleged assault of police officer in Los Angeles
text:
Lil Nas X wurde am 25. August 2025 nicht schuldig gesprochen wegen Angriff auf einen Polizisten. In Los Angeles County wurden ihm am selben Tag vier neue strafbare Anschuldigungen gemacht, darunter drei wegen Körperverletzung und eine wegen Widerstand gegen die Störung der öffentlichen Ordnung.

Hill wurde am 21. August 2025 in Los Angeles festgenommen. Der Vorfall begann, als die Polizei zu einem Bericht auf Ventura Boulevard in Studio City kam, wo ein Mann laufend nackt in der Straße gesehen wurde. Die Polizei stellte fest, dass Hill sich den Beamten gegenüber auflehnte und einer von ihnen zweimal ins Gesicht schlug. Er wurde daraufhin verhaftet, wegen Körperverletzung eines Polizisten. Er wurde kurzfristig in ein Krankenhaus gebracht, weil er möglicherweise einen Überdosis erlebt hatte, bevor er in eine Gefängnisverwaltung gebracht wurde. Er verbrachte den Wochenende im Gefängnis, bevor er am Montag vor Gericht erschien, um die Anschuldigungen anzuerkennen.

Lil Nas X wurde angesichts möglicherweise einer psychischen Krise oder unter Einfluss des Alkohols gesehen, die Details dazu sind jedoch nicht bestätigt. Monate vor dem Vorfall hatte er auf sozialen Medien bekannt gegeben, dass die letzten Jahre besonders "schwer" für ihn gewesen seien. Er hatte gesagt: "Ich komme gerade, so wie, in dieses Gefühl des Selbstvertrauens, das ich mir erlaube und was ich mache. Und ich versuche, mir Bewusstsein für mein Musik und meine Vision und die Kreativität hinter allem zu geben."

Seine Haftpfand wurde auf 75.000 Dollar gesetzt. Bei seiner Freilassung müsste er in die Anonymen, die sich Narcotics Anonymous nennen, gehen.

orig_title: Stunt performer set ablaze for cover artwork of Pink Floyd album dies aged 88
text:
Ronnie Rondell Jr., the stuntman featured on the cover of Pink Floyd's 1975 album, has died at the age of 88 in an Osage Beach, Missouri, nursing home in August 2023. His death was announced by his family on a funeral home website on August 17. The cause of his death was not disclosed.

Rondell was born in 1937 and attended North Hollywood High School before serving in the US Navy, where he excelled at scuba diving and rock climbing. He later began working as a double for films and TV shows, performing stunts that included gymnastics and hanging. 

In 1975, he appeared in flames on the album cover of Pink Floyd, alongside another stuntman. The photo shoot was conducted at the Warner Bros. Lot in Burbank, and a total of 15 photos were taken. Despite the use of fire extinguishers under his business suit, Rondell's mustache burned completely in the final photo, and his skin burned from the wind. He said: "That's it! I'm done!" The photographer Aubrey Powell remembered in 2020 that Rondell had said: "I knew I had a special picture. It took a long time for Ronnie to be ready, but in the end, he was very brave, and it was perfect. We made 15 other stunts and it's still one of the best in my life."

Rondell suffered numerous injuries throughout his career, including skull fractures and broken ribs. He once said: "You never tell anyone you're hurt because they always had someone else to wear the clothes." He retired in 2000.

Rondell is survived by his 56-year-old wife and a son. Another son of Rondell, who also worked as a stuntman, died in a plane crash in 1985 at the age of 22 during an air show.

orig_title: Several people hospitalized after thousands of hotdogs spill following collision on interstate in Pennsylvania
text:
Thousands of hot dogs invaded Interstate 83 in York County, Pennsylvania, just after 9:00 am EST (1300 UTC) on Thursday morning, after a collision involving a tractor-trailer and two other vehicles. During the collision, several people were injured, but were treated at the York Hospital and sustained no life-threatening injuries.

The tractor-trailer sprang into the air due to a mechanical problem, causing the cargo of frozen hot dogs to explode and scatter across the road. According to the owner of a business near the accident site, they heard a loud bang, followed by three more loud bangs. They immediately knew it was a tire blowout on the highway, but then realized it was another accident, as it took longer to happen.

The hot dogs were scattered across the road and were later cleaned up by the Shrewsbury Volunteer Fire Company. A photo released by the fire department showed a damaged concrete median at the accident site. The accidents slowed down traffic in both directions, and the journey was delayed by at least half an hour, as reported by The Independent.
