The cleanup efforts continued into the late morning hours and required a front-end loader to pick up the meat and load it into a trash truck.

Brad Dauberman, the president of the Shrewsbury, Pennsylvania, Fire Department, described the cleanup efforts as follows: "As soon as the hot dogs leave the truck and hit the road, it's all trash, and it's still hot." He added that hot dogs are very slippery and "I didn't know that." Dauberman also stated that a front-end loader was needed to pick up the meat and load it into a trash truck to complete the job. In total, over 1,000 pounds of hot dogs were lost in the accident. The Pennsylvania State Police are investigating the incident.

orig_title: Summer Streets returns with uninterrupted car-free stretch across Manhattan
text:
Several streets in Manhattan were closed to car and truck traffic on Saturday to accommodate participants in the annual Summer Streets program of the New York City Department of Transportation. Starting on July 26th and ending in August, every Saturday from 7:00 AM to 3:00 PM (11:00 AM to 7:00 PM UTC) the annual Summer Streets event, which spans from the Brooklyn Bridge to Inwood, was closed to vehicles, according to NBC New York.

Summer Streets will also return along the same route on August 9th and 16th, and on August 23rd, two smaller routes in Brooklyn and the Bronx, according to the source.

Many people gathered along the route throughout the day at the installation locations. There were also no cars on the side streets, where residents could meet and rest. Some had stages with live music and performances, and many others had art and craft stalls. There were also water bottle refill stations.

On 144th Street in Hamilton Heights, a local event hall installed a softball batting box for participants. In Mitchel Square Park on 167th Street, a game and deal hall offered a Settlers of Catan board game. At the northern end of the route in the Anne Loftus Playground, part of the Fort Tryon Parks, a Wading Pool played host to bands with HONK NYC performing.

In New York City, New Yorkers used bicycles, running, cycling, and scooters along the route. The temperature was in the mid-70s, with a light breeze and clear sunshine.

orig_title: Nigerian abductors kill hostages despite ransom, officials report
text:
On Monday, the authorities in Zamfara, Nigeria, said that the kidnappers have killed over 30 hostages. Thousands of dollars were paid for the release of the hostages. Reports say that the victims died despite the payment amount. The number of deaths is between 33 and 35.

The hostages were "slaughtered like sheep", said Manniru Haidara Kaura, Chairman of the local government committee. He added that the majority of the killed were young. He said: "Only they [the kidnappers] know why they killed them. They are senseless and heartless. They forget that they kill their own brothers and we all stand before God."
According to the BBC, between February and different reports, between 51 and 56 hostages were kidnapped. Kaura said that 18 hostages were released again.
The BBC reports that the government made it a crime to pay ransom in 2022, aimed at disrupting the " spiraling and lucrative hostage industry". The BBC reported that no arrests have been made in connection with these allegations until 2025.

orig_title: Train derails in southwest Germany after landslide, causing deaths
text:
Three people died after a train, carrying over 100 passengers, derailed and crashed in a wooded area in southwestern Germany on Sunday evening. Several others were injured in the accident. The cause of the accident is still under investigation and the number of injured passengers is still being confirmed by local authorities.

The accident occurred in Riedlingen, Baden-Württemberg, near the cities of Ulm and Biberach, close to Stuttgart. Authorities are investigating the cause of the accident. Several reports suggested that a landslide occurred after severe storms in the area. A source reported that local authorities believed that a sewage pipe overflow may have triggered the landslide, which dumped debris onto the train tracks. Two of the train cars derailed after striking the debris, climbed a 16-foot embankment, and crashed into trees after a collision.

orig_title: Jury convicts Minnesota lawmaker Nicole Mitchell of burglary
text:
Democratic Senator Nicola Mitchell from Minnesota was convicted on Friday of two crimes, particularly first-degree burglary and possession of burglary or theft tools, for a 2024 incident where she was arrested at her "distant" half-sister's house in Detroit Lakes. According to police, she was taken into custody after a incident in which she searched the half-sister's house to find her father's ashes and other memorials, despite not using this as an excuse in court. Mitchell's lawyer claimed that she had entered the half-sister's property to check her health and that her actions did not constitute burglary. The Associated Press reported on this.

Prosecutors, reported by CBS News and the Associated Press, presented a video of Mitchell, who told police "I know I've done something wrong", contradicting her explanation in court. In her final statements, Becker County Attorney Brian McDonald told the jury, "She said she wanted to take objects, and that shows her intention to commit theft." The Associated Press said that Senator Mitchell showed little reaction during her sentencing. She will have to spend at least 180 days in prison after the trial. As of Saturday, no sentencing file has been set.
The governor's office said they expect the senator to file an apology.

orig_title: UK voting age to be lowered to 16, among other reforms
text:
The British Minister for Housing, Communities and Local Government announced plans to lower the voting age from 18 to 16, after successful reforms in Scotland and Wales have been implemented.

According to official data cited by Reuters, there are 1.6 million people in the UK aged 16-17 who are eligible to vote, compared to 48 million who were able to vote in the 2024 election.

Prime Minister Keir Starmer said that he supports the changes for 16- and 17-year-olds, "because they are old enough to go to work, they are old enough to pay taxes", and added, "I think if you're paid, you should have the chance to say how you want to spend your money." The lowering of the voting age was a party promise for the 2024 election.

A survey by Merlin Strategy for ITV News found that 51% of 16- and 17-year-olds supported lowering the voting age to 16, and that 33% of 16- and 17-year-olds would vote for the Labour Party. The survey also found that former Labour Party leader Jeremy Corbyn was the most popular politician among those in the age group.

The reform plans were part of a broader range of voting rights reforms announced by the Ministry, including the classification of bank cards as a valid form of ID, the introduction of automatic voter registration, and the restriction of political donations.

orig_title: Car goes airborne twice in Indiana roundabout crash, man hospitalized
text:
A man in Fort Wayne, Indiana, lost control of his vehicle in a roundabout and crashed into a curb early on July 11th. The vehicle was reportedly airborne at two different times, and the man was in a life-threatening situation.

The police received calls about the accident and converged on the roundabout at Adams Center Road and Wayne Trace at 7:30am local time (11:30 UTC). They found the man's vehicle hundreds of feet away from the road.

According to police reports, the man was driving at high speed, speeding, and overtaking other cars. The vehicle crashed into the curb of the roundabout, then hit a closed road with a "Road Closed" sign, and crashed again before landing in a field.

The man was taken to the Lutheran Hospital in a life-threatening condition. The Allen County Sheriff's Department is investigating the incident.

orig_title: 20-year-old astrophotographer captures rare solar eclipse on Saturn
text:
A 20-year-old astrophotographer from Shoreline, Washington, captured a rare Saturn sunset from his hometown. An event that won't be seen again until 2038. The photographer, Adam Smadi, had planned the image several days in advance and used the Stellarium software to determine when the Saturn's largest moon, Titan, would cast a shadow over the planet's surface.

Smadi set his 9.25-inch telescope around 1 am PDT (08:00 UTC) to cool the optics to match the outside temperature, a step that helps prevent air currents within the telescope's tube from blurring the images. By 3:30 am PDT (10:30 UTC), Saturn was high enough over the horizon to capture photos.

He used a ZWO ASI662MC astrophotography camera with an infrared filter. He made continuous video clips, then used software to combine thousands of sharp images into one single image.

The result shows the small dark shadow of Titan, which falls over the bright surface of Saturn. In the same view, three other moons, Dione, Tethys, and Enceladus, appear as tiny points in the rings.

orig_title: Russia launches record drone, missile attack on Kyiv
text: A person died and 26 others were injured in an overnight wave of intense Russian attacks on nearly every district of Kyiv, according to official reports. The attacks continued until around 4:30 am (0130 GMT) the following morning. The Ukrainian Air Force said that Russia fired 539 drones and rockets during the attack, which was the highest number since the invasion began. Sirens for air raids rang out for over eight hours as multiple strikes hit Kyiv, with the Air Force describing it as the "main target of the attacks". The attacks came hours after a phone call between US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin, in which Trump said he was "disappointed" that Putin was not willing to end the war in Ukraine. According to the BBC, the Russian government said it would continue the war until it reached the "roots of the war in Ukraine".

orig_title: Ugandan military helicopter crashes in Mogadishu, Somalia
text:
On Wednesday, July 2, an Ugandan military helicopter crashed at the Aden Adde International Airport in Mogadishu, the Somali capital. According to Ugandan military spokesman Major General Felix Kulayigye, eight people were on board the plane. In the accident, five passengers died. The two helicopter pilots and an engineer survived the accident with severe injuries and burns, as reported by the BBC.

The helicopter caught fire, but was quickly brought under control by emergency services, as reported by the Somali State Television. Kulayigye announced that the accident would be investigated. According to the BBC, Ugandan forces are part of the African Union Mission in Somalia, fighting against the Islamist militant group al-Shabaab, an affiliate of al-Qaida. The helicopter crashed during a "routine combination flight", as Kulayigye described. The accident delayed the departure of a Turkish Airlines passenger flight, while domestic flights continued as usual, as reported by the BBC.

orig_title: Bangladesh beat hosts Myanmar 2–1 to qualify for 2026 AFC Women's Asian Cup
text: Bangladesh won Myanmar 2-1 in their second group stage match of the AFC Women's Asian Cup 2026 qualifications at the Thuwunna Stadium in Yangon, Myanmar. Ritu Porna Chakma scored both goals for Bangladesh, scoring the first goal in the 19th minute after a replay from a free kick and adding a second goal in the 72nd minute from a solo attack from the sideline. Myanmar equalized in the 89th minute, but Bangladesh kept the score closed, which was described as a historic victory by the Dhaka Tribune and other media outlets. The loss marked Bangladesh's second consecutive win in the qualification, following a 7-0 victory over Bahrain earlier, which secured their spot in the final tournament of the 2026 AFC Women's Asian Cup in Australia. It was Bangladesh's first win in the continental finals. The starting lineup of the team consisted of Rupna Chakma, Sheuli Azim, Afeeda Khandaker, Shamsunnahar, Kohati Kisku, Sapna Rani, Maria Manda, Monika Chakma, Shamsunnahar Jr., Ritu Porna Chakma, and Tohura Khatun. The team was coached by trainer Peter Butler. The win secured Bangladesh's first place in Group C with one game left before July 5th against Turkmenistan. Myanmar had earlier defeated Turkmenistan 8-0 in their qualifying match.

orig_title: Third person charged in relation to Pheobe Bishop's alleged murder
text:
Kieren Daniel Mittelheuser, a 30-year-old man, is the third person to be charged with the alleged murder of 17-year-old Phoebe Bishop. On Wednesday, at 7:00 PM Australian Eastern Standard Time (09:00 UTC), he was arrested in Bundaberg West in the Australian state of Queensland and charged with two counts of aiding and abetting murder. It is alleged that he used Bishop's phone to disrupt the investigation. Mittelheuser is also charged with invalid driver's licenses, fraud, breach of liability, and drug possession.

Although the case involving Mittelheuser was mentioned in the Bundaberg Magistrates Court, he did not appear in court. He remains currently in custody and has not made a request for bail. Nonetheless, Mittelheuser is scheduled to appear in court on August 25. A procedure to add evidence for aiding and abetting murder and fraud has been ordered by Magistrate John McInnes. James Wood, 34, and Tanika Bromley, 33, who lived with Bishop at the time of the incident, were previously charged with murder and twice with disrupting the body. According to sources, they are scheduled to appear in court in August.

On May 15, 17-year-old Phoebe Bishop, who lived in Gin Gin in the Bundaberg region of the Australian state of Queensland, died after she flew out of the country to visit her boyfriend in Perth. After several police searches, human remains were found on June 6, which were later identified as Bishop's. The police are still seeking information about Bishop or the route of a grey Hyundai IX35 from May 15 to May 18 in the Gin Gin area.

orig_title: Beyoncé halts performance after "flying car" prop malfunctions mid-air above audience
text: On Saturday, a day of performance, American pop music act Beyoncé interrupted a live performance at the NRG Stadium in Houston, Texas, due to a defect with a prop in the first show of her tour. During the performance of her song "16 Carriages," the Cadillac, suspended in the air over the audience, began to swing as it started to swing to one side. She repeated "Hold" several times during the swinging of the car, and after the performance, the audience erupted into loud noises and screams. The car was lowered into the crowd in response to the defect, which was met with enthusiasm and applause. Beyoncé returned to the stage and ended the concert by joking: "If I ever fall, I know you'll catch me." According to Beyoncé's production and management company Parkwood Entertainment, there were no injuries related to the incident. The company investigated the incident in an Instagram Story and called it a "technical malfunction."

orig_title: U.S. strikes Iranian nuclear sites Fordow, Natanz, Isfahan overnight
text:
The United States carried out overnight air strikes on three Iranian nuclear sites: Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan, in an effort to prevent Iran's nuclear capabilities. The operation, known as Operation Midnight Hammer, was ordered by President Donald Trump and announced on Saturday evening in Washington. According to the US military, the first bomb attack on the Fordow area was carried out at 20:40 local time (22:40 UTC) on Saturday as part of a coordinated attack involving seven B-2 Spirit bombers.
Tomahawk missiles were fired from a US Navy submarine, and B-2 bombers that had flown 18 hours from the US with the support of fighter jets and refueling planes dropped a total of 14 30,000-pound GBU-57/B Massive Ordnance Penetrator (MOP) bunker-busting bombs. According to Air Force General Dan Caine, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, this attack marked the first operational use of the GBU-57. During a press conference, General Caine said he agreed with President Donald Trump's assessment that "no other military in the world could have carried out this attack", and praised the mission as a demonstration of the US's "surrounding reach, coordination, and ability".
The US military said the attack included deception tactics with decoy aircraft flying west of the main attack package over the Pacific Ocean to obscure the true direction and intention of the main attack. Defense Minister Pete Hegseth said the attack should not be seen as a bid to overthrow the government, but rather a precision operation to neutralize threats to US national interests posed by Iran's nuclear program and, under the cover of, collective self-defense of US troops and allies Israel.
Hours after the attack, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi condemned the US action, saying the time for diplomacy was over and that Iran had the right to defend itself. "War intimidation, a wild regime in Washington is alone and fully responsible for the dangerous consequences and far-reaching effects of its aggressive act", Araghchi said during a press conference in Turkey, according to the Associated Press.

orig_title: Bangladeshi interim leader Muhammad Yunus returns home after four-day visit to London
text:
Muhammad Yunus, Bangladesh's chief advisor, returned home on Saturday, June 14, after spending four days in London from June 10 to 13. 

The Press Secretary Shafiqul Alam announced on Thursday the main focus of the visit, which was to drain around $24.7 billion (approximately $174 billion) of national wealth, which the Bangladeshi government claimed was accumulated during Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's tenure. On Thursday, Professor Yunus received the King Charles III Harmony Award 2025 at St. James's Palace, sponsored by the King's Foundation, for his work promoting "peace, sustainability, and harmony between people and the environment". 

Earlier, he was received by King Charles III in a private audience at Buckingham Palace. 

Yunus offered to meet with British Prime Minister Keir Starmer, but no meeting was planned. According to the BBC, Yunus said he hadn't received any explanation, and suggested that Starmer might be busy. Political and diplomatic commentators like former Ambassador M Humayun Kabir and Analyst Altaf Parvez criticized the handling and communication of the planned meeting, which was announced on June 4 by diplomat Siddique. The President of the Bangladesh Enterprise Institute M. Humayun Kabir emphasized that the announcement had led to high expectations, and the lack of a conclusion could negatively impact public perception.

Yunus delivered a speech at Chatham House on Wednesday before Director Bronwen Maddox, where he addressed the problems of the transitional period, his anti-corruption measures, and his foreign policy, as well as the situation of the Rohingya, many of whom live in Cox's Bazar's largest refugee camp. "We are working very hard to ensure that we can bring these people back to their homeland. In the meantime, we have problems. The US government has withdrawn all the funds, the US-AID money has vanished suddenly, and the $12 monthly allowance per person for food, which was previously $12, has disappeared."

Yunus declined a meeting with Labour Party Leader Tulip Siddiq, whose sister is former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who is under investigation by the government's anti-corruption commission for allegedly receiving illegal land from her aunt's old regime. He said it was a "judicial matter", but expressed full confidence in the commission. Siddiq, who left her position in the Treasury in January, expressed disappointment with Yunus' decision and denied all allegations.

On the last day of the visit, a delegation, including the South Asia Director of the Regional Department Lesley Craig and Commodore Whalley, took Professor Yunus on a tour of the HMS Enterprise, a ship that will be used by the Bengali Navy for oceanographic and hydrographic purposes. Yunus confirmed the importance of a joint effort between the two countries to utilize such a ship for research and data-sharing, which would lead to a better understanding of Bangladesh's own resources and oceans.

When asked about the chances of a national election campaign in 2026 before Ramadan, Yunus said it would take place in February, provided there are political and legal reforms in advance. He had previously suggested that the elections could take place in April 2026.

orig_title: San Diego joins US-wide No Kings protests
text:
A series of planned protests, organized by Take Action San Diego, began in Downtown San Diego, California, at around 10:15 AM PDT (1715 UTC) on June 14. The protests were part of the larger No Kings protests taking place in California and other parts of the United States to protest against the government and politics of President Donald Trump, as they suspected his authoritarian stance.

According to CBS8, cited by the San Diego Police Department, approximately 80,000 people gathered in front of the San Diego County Administration Center in the Waterfront Park. The protesters then began marching south on Harbor Drive and continued marching until they turned left onto the Pacific Highway and marched north.

Wikinews spoke with several protesters.

"We don't like what Trump is doing, and the fascism he's found, and the authoritarian atmosphere. You know, so when they said 'No Kings,' that's what America's all about," said an older couple who participated in the demonstration.

"I'm protesting the government and all their illegal actions, all their illegal dealings and what the President and his associates are doing to this country is absolutely illegal, and they're not Americans," said a protester when asked why he was there.

One of the protesters who was interviewed said that he was personally affected by President Donald Trump's policies: "I'm trans and I need my rights. It was one of the first things Trump did with his decrees, when he tried to say that the Department of Health does not acknowledge transsexual identity."

The protests remained peaceful in San Diego throughout the day, according to Police Chief Scott Wahl. By 1:30 PM PDT (2030 UTC), most of the demonstrators had left.

orig_title: Hot air balloon crashes in Turkey, killing pilot and injuring tourists
text: A hot-air balloon crashed in central Turkey on Sunday, killing the pilot and injuring 19 tourists from Indonesia, according to Turkish media. The governor's office stated that changing wind conditions put the balloon at risk. The accident occurred near the Ihlara Waterfall Cleft in Aksaray Province, where a video by İhlas News Agency, cited by the Associated Press, showed the balloon basket on the ground while rescue teams helped the injured. Aksaray Governor's President Mehmet Ali Kumbuzoglu said the pilot attempted to make a rough landing, falling out of the basket and getting his feet caught in a rope. He was trapped under the basket and died. The injured were taken to the hospital. The Associated Press reported that another tourist balloon group made a rough landing the same day, with only light injuries but no fatalities. Hot-air balloon rides are a popular tourist program in central Turkey due to the region's extensive landscape, particularly the "magical rock formations" of the Cappadocian Mountains, which are listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, according to the Associated Press.

orig_title: Football: Japan beats Indonesia with score 6-0 for 2026 FIFA World Cup
text:
Japan defeated Indonesia 6-0 in the last group match of the AFC qualification in the Panasonic Stadium Suita in Suita, Osaka, Japan on June 10. 

Daichi Kamada scored twice, while Takefusa Kubo, Ryoya Morishita, Shuto Machino, and reserve player Mao Hosoya each scored one goal. Due to injuries, Indonesia lost two defenders, Kevin Diks and his substitute Yakob Sayuri, during the game.

According to the Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA), Japan secured a spot in the 2026 FIFA World Cup with a 2-0 win over Bahrain in a game in Saitama on March 20.

Indonesia finished fourth in the round and still has a chance to qualify for the 2026 FIFA World Cup, depending on its performance in the upcoming qualification matches.

Japan scored 30 goals in ten games at the event.

orig_title: Boeing 787 crashes into Indian medical school, killing hundreds
text:
An Air India Boeing 787-8, which was destined for London's Gatwick Airport, crashed shortly after takeoff from a nearby airport in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, northwest India, into the city. It was 13:38 local time (08:08 UTC). Of the 242 people on board, only one person survived. Dozens more were killed on the ground.

The plane struck a residential area, hitting a neighborhood that belonged to a nearby medical institute. Firefighters and other emergency teams arrived at the scene and began loading the injured onto stretchers.
Air India announced that 169 Indians, 53 British citizens, seven Portuguese citizens, and one Canadian were on the flight. The parent company of Air India, the Tata Group, promised to pay for the medical care of the injured and support the restoration of the medical curriculum. They also offered $1.1 million to remember the dead. The US government, the National Transportation Safety Board, and the Federal Aviation Administration announced their cooperation with Indian authorities to investigate the crash.
According to The Guardian, which was quoted by the Hindustan Times, the only survivor, a British-Indian man named Vishwash Kumar Ramesh, who was sitting in seat 11A, said that the plane made a loud noise directly after takeoff: "When I stood up, there were bodies around me. I was shocked. I stood up and ran. There were pieces of the plane all around me. One of them hit me and threw me into an ambulance and took me to the hospital." His brother Ajay, who was also on board, did not survive. Vishwash was on his way to Britain from Leicester, England, where he had visited his family in India. The Guardian also quoted Agence France-Presse, which reported that a local resident said: "We saw people jumping out of the building to save themselves. The plane was on fire. We helped people out of the building and took the injured to the hospital."
According to the Aviation Safety Network, this is the first accident involving a 787 model. The 787-8 subseries is designed to handle long, non-stretched routes. The 787 fleet, known as the Dreamliners, reached its billionth passenger in May 2025, 14 years after its introduction into commercial air travel.

orig_title: Scottish Labour win Scottish Parliament by-election
text:
A Scottish constituency election was held on June 5, 2025, for Hamilton, Larkhall, and Stonehouse. The election was held after the death of the former MSP Christina McKelvie in March. The election was won by Davy Russell of the Scottish Labour. Ten candidates competed in the election.

Former First Minister Nicola Sturgeon accompanied the SNP candidate, Katy Loudon. Reform UK was accused of racism by Anas Sarwar, former leader of the party, over repeated attacks. In the election campaign, topics included living costs, healthcare, small businesses, and revitalizing the city center.

Labour candidate Davy Russell was elected with 31.6% of the votes. The Scottish National Party came in second with 29.4%, Reform UK came in third with 26.1%. The Scottish Conservative Party won 6.0%, the Scottish Green Party 2.6%, and the Scottish Liberal-Democratic Party 2.0%.

Russell said in his victory speech: "Like the people of Hamilton, Larkhall, and Stonehouse, and all of Scotland, we feel that we've been disappointed by the SNP. After nearly two decades, they don't deserve another chance... The mix of Reform is not for Scotland, and we don't want that here." 

According to BBC News, the election outcome is significant for the upcoming 2026 Scottish Parliament elections.

orig_title: Ukrainian drone strikes target four airfields in Russia
text:
Ukraine carries out drone attack on Russian military bases, causing over 40 aircraft to be damaged. The targets of the drone attack were the Olenya Airfield near Murmansk and the Belaya Airfield near Irkutsk. The Russian Defense Ministry stated that a "terror attack using First-person view (FPV) drones against military bases in the regions of Murmansk, Irkutsk, Ivanovo, Ryazan, and Amur" was carried out. The government added that "the fire was extinguished and there were no casualties among military personnel or civilians." According to the Russian Defense Ministry, the attacks on the bases in Ivanovo, Ryazan, and Amur were repelled.

SBU Chief Vasyl Malyuk stated: "According to the laws and customs of war, we have completely legitimate targets - military bases and aircraft that attack our peaceful cities." The attack targeted A-50 surveillance aircraft, strategic bombers such as the Tu-22M3, Tu-95, and Tu-160. The SBU estimates that over one-third of Russia's strategic missile carriers were hit, causing $7 billion in damages. The cost of the operation on the Ukrainian side was not publicly disclosed, but it included 117 quadcopter drones, along with relevant equipment, and all personnel involved were removed from the Russian territory. A source familiar with the operation told CNN that the attack was carried out using Russian communication networks, and that a small device such as a mobile phone was required to function as a communication center to connect the drones and remote controllers. The drones were hidden in the "isolation" of the "mobile houses" roofs, which were then loaded onto trucks.

The governor of Irkutsk stated that a truck from the hinterland brought the drones. The Russian aircraft were also on fire at the Dyagilevo and Ivanovo airports in central parts of Ryazan and Ivanovo. A source from the SBU stated that the operation was planned for over a year and a half. A Trump Administration official in the United States said that they were not informed of the attack.

orig_title: Activists claim sexual abuse and torture at the hands of Tanzanian authorities
text:
Activist and photographer Boniface Mwangi from Kenya claimed on Monday that Tanzanian security officials mistreated and sexually harassed him and Ugandan journalist Agather Atuhaire during their stay in Dar es Salaam between May 19 and 23. 

Both had been summoned to the first trial of arrested opposition leader Tundu Lissu on May 19 in Dar es Salaam. The two activists were taken to the police stations in Dar es Salaam without warning, without removing their eyes. After several interrogations and threats, they were taken to the Unkenrüttelungsbunker, where the mistreatment took place. Mwangi was left outside the border between Tanzania and Kenya on May 22, while Atuhaire was released near the border with Uganda on the day after. 

On Monday, Mwangi discussed his experiences in a joint press conference with the BBC and The Eastleigh Voice. He told about his time in the Unkenrüttelungsbunker, where he was beaten and whipped, and about the exposure of his personal space. He burst into tears when describing the details of the mistreatment: "They smeared his behind with liquid and stuck sticks in his back." He claimed that the authorities forced him to say the Tanzanian President's slogan "asante" while being mistreated, and that they threatened to publish the video of the mistreatment if he spoke about it. He claimed that he had pain and broken bones in different parts of his body. 

The Police Chief of Dar es Salaam, Jumanne Muliro, doubted Mwangi's claims and described them as "stories told by activists". At a Reuters interview on June 2, the Tanzanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Police did not respond immediately to the allegations. 

Atuhaire had made similar claims when she told the BBC in late May that Tanzanian security officials had beaten her and sexually harassed her and had removed her naked. Mwangi said it was difficult to contact Atuhaire due to threats of beatings and foot strikes by their pursuers. On Monday, Atuhaire said she had never thought it would be worse than her own "very authoritarian" nation, and added that she had filed a complaint against the authorities involved in the mistreatment. 

Local and international human rights organizations reacted to the mistreatment with concern. The Kenyan branch of Amnesty International issued a statement condemning the mistreatment and calling for those responsible to be held accountable. The US Department of State's Office for African Affairs highlighted that Atuhaire had won the International Women of Courage Award in 2024. 

On the day Mwangi and Atuhaire were released, President Samia Suluhu Hassan said that foreign activists were disrupting Tanzanian internal affairs and "spreading chaos" if they were arrested in the country. "Don't let them come here to meddle in our affairs. Don't give them a place here." Hassan later said she was committed to upholding human rights. 

Opposition leader Tundu Lissu called for drastic changes in policy after being arrested on April 9 on suspicion of trying to block elections. He was accused of spreading false information on the internet, which could lead to a possible death sentence. He denied both charges and his party was subsequently excluded from the elections after they were asked to sign a code of conduct by the National Electoral Commission's Unity Committee. 

At the trial on May 19, hundreds of his supporters shouted his campaign slogan "No reforms, no election" and clung to the courthouse. Lissus' lawyers complained about the excessive presence of police officers around the courthouse, which the judge acknowledged and led to a recess. Lissus' trial was postponed to June 2.

orig_title: NSW DCCEEW researchers discover critically endangered Leadbeater's possum in Kosciuszko National Park, Australia
text:
A team from the Australian Department of Climate Change, Energy, Environment and Water (DCCEEW) in New South Wales (NSW) discovered seven Leadbeater's possum images in the Yarrangobilly Caves during a survey in October in the Kosciuszko National Park, NSW, while conducting a survey on Smoky mice. Both species are critically endangered in Australia, with the Leadbeater's possum previously considered extinct in NSW, with the only known current populations in Victoria, where the species has been the state's mammal emblem since 1971. The NSW government has begun the process of listing the Leadbeater's possum on the NSW Threatened Species Scientific Committee's accelerated listing list. The discovery was confirmed by the Healesville Sanctuary and the Australian National University (ANU).

Professor David Lindenmayer, a member of the Biodiversity Council, had searched for the Leadbeater's possum in the Yarrangobilly Caves 35 years ago while pursuing his PhD, as a climate model had predicted the species might be found there, but "never saw one" in the park. In his own words, he said, "With so little high-quality habitat in Australia, we should focus all our efforts on protecting the remaining areas; hopefully, we'll have many wonderful discoveries soon." He added that large parks like the iconic Kosciuszko National Park and other large reserves in Australia are crucial for the preservation of species criticism, as they are essential for biodiversity.

Dr. Dan Harley, senior ecologist at the Healesville Sanctuary, noted that the discovery in NSW "in no way" changes the critical endangerment of the Leadbeater's possum at the moment. However, he considers it "a promising step" for the future of the species, which was very close to extinction. He recalled previous discoveries, such as the 1961 rediscovery and the discovery of lower- and subalpine populations in 1986 and 1990s, which gave hope that the last surviving form of the species might not be completely destroyed, when the terrible Black-Summer bushfires devastated the Victoria North region.

The discovery of the species in NSW was "completely unexpected" and a "surprising turning point". In Victoria, there are strong genetic differences between the highland and lowland Leadbeater's possums over short distances. Considering the large distance between the Victorian populations in the central high mountains and the discovery site in NSW, it is very likely that the NSW population will be genetically different from the populations in Victoria. Once the genetic results are available, we expect to find NSW Northern Leadbeater's possums and Victoria Southern Leadbeater's possums with different management requirements.

The adult Leadbeater's possum, also known as the feral possum, is about 40cm long and weighs 125g. There are two varieties of them in Victoria, as described above, and there are fewer than 40 lowland Leadbeater's possums left. The Healesville Sanctuary has a breeding program with another variety of Leadbeater's possum, the Highland possum, which has been successfully established. Narvi, a female Highland possum, was successfully raised and later released into the predator-free Coranderrk Bushland Nature reserve, along with a lowland possum named Mercury, with the goal of establishing a new colony. Healesville Sanctuary staff Arabella Eyre said, "The lowland population is so small, with fewer than 40 individuals in the wild, where there are only 9 pairs that can continue, and that cannot last long. Without the possibility of bringing genetic diversity to the wild populations, we expect them to disappear within 15 years." What makes these first attempts at mixing a pair so important is that Healesville Sanctuary staff Amie Hindson said, "There was an immediate connection between them, and it's a really special love story for us."

orig_title: Man starts car collision at Liverpool FC trophy parade
text:
On Monday, May 26, at 6am local time, in Liverpool, England, a motorist, allegedly a 53-year-old man from the area, drove his Ford Galaxy car into pedestrians on the Liverpool FC Trophy Parade, where hundreds of thousands of people were celebrating Liverpool FC's English football championship. Dave Kitchin from the Northwest Ambulance Service said that three adults and one child were trapped under the car, and many others were injured: In total, 20 people were treated for light injuries, and 27 were taken to the local hospital, with some more patients going to the hospital on their own. The alleged driver of the car, a white British man, was arrested shortly after the accident. On Thursday, May 29, Paul Desmond Sanders Doyle, 53 years old, from Burghill Road, West Derby, was arrested for dangerous driving and multiple charges of intending to cause harm or injury, or intending to cause harm or injury. 

"We were contacted at 6am today, Monday, May 26, after reports of a car driving into several pedestrians on Water Street," said Merseyside Police on Monday. "The car stopped at the scene, and a man was arrested. The emergency services are currently on the scene." The deputy police chief, Jenny Sims, explained on Tuesday "It is assumed that the driver of the Ford Galaxy car, who was involved in the accident, could follow the ambulance on Water Street after the lane was temporarily cleared, so that the paramedic team could treat a member of the public who was suspected of having a heart attack. 

On Thursday, the deputy police chief, Jenny Sims, provided an update on the scene "In total, 79 people were injured, and they are still in contact with our officers and staff, and seven people remain in the hospital to receive expert care from our colleagues in the NHS. ... I would like to offer all who haven't met the police yet, the relevant information, please come forward, and contact us. Information, including video footage, can be sent to us through the Major Incident Police Portal. As always, I think of the victims and all those affected by this incident." The British government's spokesperson, Keir Starmer, described the accident as "horrific". Liverpool FC is helping the police with the investigation, which occurred near the end of the parade.

orig_title: Baseball: Detroit Tigers sweep San Francisco Giants, making their fourth win in a row
text:
On Wednesday, May 28, at Comerica Park in Detroit, Michigan, USA, during the 2025 season of Major League Baseball, the Detroit Tigers defeated the San Francisco Giants with a four-game winning streak. The Detroit Tigers won 4-3 and now held the best Major League Baseball record with 37 wins and 20 losses. A rough right-handed pitcher, Jackson Jobe, started for the Tigers.

In the fifth inning, Justyn-Henry Malloy led the Tigers' attack with a single that swung the game in their favor. The Tigers scored the entire hitting in the fifth inning with the help of Colts' double home run for two runs and Malloy's second single for two runs.

Colt Keith connected with the right-handed starting pitcher Landen Roupp, and Justyn-Henry Malloy connected with the right-handed reliever Randy Rodríguez. Pitcher Brenan Hanifee made a three-strikeout relief pitcher and hit a batter in a year. Pitcher Tommy Kahnle made his seventh save after a perfect eighth inning and made a perfect ninth inning.

orig_title: Australian Coalition reunite after one week
text:
The Liberal Party of Australia, a decade-long dominant centre-right party, has reunited after the party split for a week. On Wednesday, a joint press conference of party leaders Sussan Ley and David Littleproud, where it was announced that the parties have reunited; with the opposition, also announced the new shadow cabinet of the same Wednesday, the conference.

The two parties had recently split in the wake of the 2025 federal elections, where both the Liberals and the Nationals were defeated by their rivals, leading to disagreements between the two parties over political differences, despite Peter Dutton, the leader of the Liberals and the coalition, losing his seat in the parliament and necessitating a change in the coalition leadership. On May 20, Nationals leader David Littleproud announced that the party must end its connection to the Liberal Party, denied that the Nationals would give up their political demands, while Sussan Ley, the new leader of the Liberals, was thrilled with an in-depth review of the party's positions following the significant defeat in the federal elections.

The reunification of the parties saw the Liberals agree on four political demands of the Nationals, which concern nuclear power plants, a Regional Australia Future Fund, remote mobile phone coverage, and changes in the retail sector. The split has led to internal conflicts within the party, but Littleproud stressed that he would stick to his demanded positions. The party also underwent a shadow cabinet review process after the reunification.

Together, the Liberals' leader Sussan Ley announced that she looked forward to cooperation between the two parties in the future.

In the early stages of the split, there were doubts about whether either party could ever achieve a majority to challenge the existing Labor government. There have been other splits in the past, the last one being 1987, but neither party could form a government without the other.

It should be noted that in the context of nuclear power plants, the coalition position has changed: They will give up their previous position, which they had taken to build seven power plants, and continue to fight against the existing national moratorium on nuclear power plants.

orig_title: Australian Nationals leave Coalition with Liberal Party
text:
On Tuesday, May 20, National Party leader David Littleproud announced that the party would be ending its 100-year partnership with the Liberal Party. The two parties have formed the dominant centre-right and right-wing party in Australian politics and opposed the Centre-Left Party. However, after the historic defeat of the Coalition in the 2025 Australian federal election, the Nationals have decided to end the coalition, after years of alliance.

In his announcement, Littleproud cited growing differences in policy, including budget planning and nuclear energy, and the poor performance of the party in the recent federal election. The election itself was historic, with Liberal leader Peter Dutton losing seats to a Labor MP (the first opposition leader to do so in Australian history, after leading the party to one of the country's most decisive election victories).

The two parties had discussed reforming the coalition, but the Nationals have decided to separate from the Liberals and is no longer part of a coalition agreement. According to ABC election analyst Antony Green, the Liberals and National parties are unlikely to form a government independently.

orig_title: Professional baseball is back in Tucson, Arizona, thanks to relocation of Mexican team
text:
The Mayos de Navojoa, a team in the Mexican Pacific Winter League (MPL), have announced they are moving to Tucson, Arizona, where they will become the first professional baseball team to represent the city in over a decade. They will begin playing at the Kino Sports Complex in the 2025/26 season, making Tucson the first American city to participate in the league.

The Mayos are relocating from their base in Sonora, Mexico, and the MPL president stated that the team overcame financial and logistical challenges caused by the COVID-19 pandemic, which made it difficult for them to stay in Mexico.

The team has signed a one-year contract, but officials in Tucson hope this will lead to a multi-year agreement. According to Victor Cuevas, president of the Mayos, the team's name may be changed with the support of fans.

According to All Sports, reports of a possible move had surfaced several months earlier. The Sonora governor, Alfonso Durazo Montaño, has announced plans to convert the team's former home into a school for young baseball players, similar to the Estadio Héctor Espino in Hermosillo.

The last professional franchise in Tucson was the Tucson Sidewinders, with the Tucson Saguaros, considered semi-pros by the Arizona Daily Star, currently representing the city.

orig_title: Three UK neo-Nazis convicted of multiple terrorism offences
text:
On Wednesday, May 14, at the Sheffield Crown Court in Sheffield, South Yorkshire, England, three British extremists were found guilty of planning terrorism and other related charges. In February 2024, Christopher Ringrose, 34 years old, and Marco Pitzettu and Brogan Stewart, both 25 years old, were arrested. The trial began in March and lasted for nine weeks, with the presentation of evidence, including over 200 weapons, including bows, knives, and swords, found in raids on the defendants' homes in Derbyshire, Staffordshire, and Yorkshire.

"Some of their defense in court was that it was just fantasy or harmless small talk, but all three took real-world steps to plan and prepare an attack on innocent civilians," said Detective Chief Superintendent James Dunkerley, Head of Counter Terrorism Policing North East. "They believed that a racial war between whites and other races would soon erupt."

The three men communicated only online, such as in the Telegram channel "Einsatz 14," where an undercover officer was able to infiltrate the group led by Stewart. In addition to planning terrorism, each of them was also charged with two charges related to collecting information that could be useful for someone planning to attack innocent civilians. Ringrose was also charged with manufacturing a prohibited weapon, as he had 3D-printed components for a FGC9 semi-automatic pistol and was almost complete. Pitzettu had previously been convicted of illegally obtaining a "Stun Gun."

Judge Mrs Justice Cutts stated that the defendants "all expect a significant sentence." The prosecution was set for July 17.

orig_title: Texas police arrest mother and her son on terrorism charges
text: A 33-year-old woman and her 13-year-old son were arrested by the San Antonio Police Department for terrorism charges. The woman had bought equipment such as ammunition and tactical clothing for her son to help him with a violent attack on his school. On Sunday, May 11, the boy's grandmother found him in his bedroom, working on a live round with a hammer and also discovered a homemade bomb that had the name of Brenton Tarrant, the perpetrator of the mosque shooting in Christchurch, New Zealand in March 2019, as well as a list of names of mass shooters and their victim numbers. The boy confessed to his grandmother that his mother, Ashley Rosalinda Pardo, had bought him military surplus goods to buy a tactical vest and a helmet, as well as books on firearms and guns, in order to take care of his younger siblings. The grandmother reported the discovery to the police on Monday. On Monday, the boy wore military clothing to school, but left soon after. The SAPD officers apprehended him and his mother at the school exit. The boy said he wanted to become famous before going to school. Ashley Pardo was released on a $75,000 bail and was given a detention sentence and will appear in court on July 17. The school principal, Felismina Martinez, said that the parents "must take all potential threats seriously and take immediate action to protect everyone they are responsible for." The police had been monitoring the boy since January, when the school administration learned about his activities, including violent drawings, a plan of the school grounds with the label "Suicide Route" and his fascination with mass shooters and their manifestos. In April, he was suspended after searching for information on previous mass shootings on one of the school's computers; on the same day, he tried to take his own life and was severely injured. He returned to school on May 8. According to sources, Pardo was not particularly concerned about her son's behavior and even supported his drawings.

orig_title: "Too Easy LoL": messages written on cell wall as ten inmates escape from Orleans Parish Prison in Louisiana, United States
text:
Ten inmates broke out of the Parish Justice Center Orleans in New Orleans, Louisiana, on Friday, May 16, 2025. The staff of the jail discovered the escape during a count of inmates at 8:30 AM Louisiana Time (13:30 UTC).

The authorities quickly apprehended Kendell Myles, 20 years old, who was sentenced to second degree murder - and was also accused of attempted second degree murder - in the French Quarter. According to the Orleans Parish Sheriff's Office Police, seven inmates were still on the run on Sunday evening, three more were taken into custody on Friday evening, including Robert Moody and Dkenan Dennis. The LA State Police reported that a fourth fugitive was arrested on Monday - Gary C. Price, 21 years old. On Tuesday, Corey Boyd, 19 years old, who was accused of a preliminary second degree murder, was also taken into custody.

Police Chief Hutson reported that the inmates "escaped" from the cell at 12:30 PM Louisiana Time (05:30 UTC) - "They managed to open a door," she explained. They left the cell at 1:01 AM Louisiana Time (06:01 UTC) by breaking through a wall behind a toilet room. The surveillance footage showed the fugitives climbing through a jailhouse door, a wall, and then running over the interstate. The police photos showed a large hole behind the toilet room with graffiti that read "We are innocent" and "Lol, too easy".

Three of the escaped inmates - Jermaine Donald, Derrick Groves, and Lenton Vanburen - were charged with second degree murder. The police were also searching for fugitives who were wanted for assaulting, armed robbery, fraud, bodily harm, and several drug-related crimes.

The authorities warned that the fugitives were armed and dangerous. Local, state, and federal agencies launched a large-scale search operation. Due to the danger, the victims were connected with the fugitives to ensure safety. At the time, the prison guards were in a state of crisis as only 36 wardens and 4 superiors were present. Police Chief Susan Hutson emphasized the need for $5.2 million in prison repair and increased staff.

The authorities reviewed the security procedures, the actions of the staff, and the possibility of internal help. They said they would hold accountable anyone who facilitated the escape. The authorities called on the residents to be cautious and report suspicious activities immediately, and they advised them not to approach the fugitives.

orig_title: Trainmen and engineers go on statewide strike in New Jersey, first time in 42 years
text:
Members of the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen (BLET) went on strike on Friday, May 16th at 12:01 AM (0401 UTC). The members found that there was no agreement with the NJ Transit management over the conditions and procedures of the new contract. The NJ Transit trains and the MTA Metro-North West Hudson service will not be in operation during the duration of the strike.

The union announced that the strike would continue until Sunday, to which NJ Transit CEO Kris Kolluri said that the two sides would meet with federal mediators, the National Mediation Board, in Washington, D.C.

Locomotive engineers on strike demonstrated outside the Hoboken Terminal and the NJ Transit headquarters in Newark, carrying flags with the text "Locomotive Engineers on Strike" and "NJ Transit: Millions for Penthouse Views, Nothing for the Train Personnel". The Penthouse Views reference is on the new NJ Transit headquarters, as described in a statement by National President Mark Wallace, highlighting the excessive expenses for the new building complex, while the funds for the train personnel's salaries could be used to increase wages. He said: "NJ Transit has spent half a billion dollars on a luxurious new headquarters and 53 million dollars on the interior design of an unnecessary building. They gave 20 million dollars in revenue during an annual free-load event. They have money for penthouse views and project ideas, but not for their frontline personnel. Enough is enough. We will continue to strike until our members receive the fair pay they deserve."

On Friday, Governor Murphy and Kolluri held a press conference, saying that there was "no panic situation" among the NJ Transit employees and they were "ready" to prepare for a strike. NJ Transit employees estimated that the strike would affect the lives of over 350,000 commuters and "very limited capacity for existing New York commuter buses near the train stations and in agreements with private drivers who operate the bus service as a substitute for the trains". At the same time, NJ Transit suspended both bus and train services for Shakira's concerts on Thursday and Friday at the MetLife Stadium.

orig_title: Thai officials seize 238 tons of illegal e-waste at Bangkok port
text:
Thailand's customs agency said in a press conference on Wednesday that local authorities had mistakenly protected 238 tons of electronic waste in ten containers labeled as metal waste. According to Theeraj Athanavanich, director of the customs agency, the containers were inspected at Bangkok's port yesterday as part of a routine check, with one source describing the exchange as routine and another as accidental. He said the shipment was therefore imported illegally from the US. Devdiscourse reported it as one of the largest electronic waste imports discovered by Thai authorities this year.

The contents of the containers were labeled as "mixed metal waste" by customs officials, but also contained electronic circuit boards, Athanavanich said. He said that Thai officials plan to file charges against those who made false declarations of imports and against the illegal disposal of electronic waste in the country. The authorities plan to reject the containers and send them back to their sender.

According to AP News, cited in a UN report from 2024, electronic waste is accumulating worldwide, with 62 million tons in 2022 and only 22% properly collected and recycled.

orig_title: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese reshuffles cabinet following re-election
text:
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced on Monday that he had reshuffled his cabinet following the 2025 federal election. Most of the top officials remained in their positions, with Richard Marles, Jim Chalmers, Penny Wong, Don Farrell, Katy Gallagher, and Jason Clare all staying put. Former Justice Minister Mark Dreyfus and former Industry and Science Minister Ed Husic were both removed from their positions, both being linked to the Left faction of the party. Albanese downplayed the demotions by saying on Thursday: "No one is bigger than the collective and that includes myself."

New ministers include Anne Aly, who took on the portfolios of small businesses, international development, and multicultural affairs, and Michelle Rowland, who was appointed as the new Justice Minister.

The Labor government won a second term in office after a crushing election victory on May 3. In his victory speech, Albanese said: "We have seen a temptation to play American-style politics, division and pitting Australians against each other and I believe that is not the Australian way."

Peter Dutton, the leader of the Liberal Party, lost his own seat to Labor candidate Ali France. The leader of the Australian Greens, Adam Bandt, also lost his seat.

orig_title: United National Congress party wins elections, new government cabinet meets in Trinidad and Tobago
text:
On Thursday, May 8, the new cabinet of Trinidad and Tobago met at the Red House in Port of Spain, the capital. The new government system of Kamla Persad-Bissessar was installed after the UNC party's system won the general elections of 2025 on April 28, which is the second time Persad-Bissessar has held the premiership of Trinidad and Tobago, having previously held it from 2010 to 2015.

According to the media statement released in the afternoon, the cabinet discussed during the meeting the introduction of an e-Cabinet platform, the TT Revenue Authority Act, the establishment of a commission to review the "Stand your ground" laws, and changes to the Children's Funds Act, which would allow more people to enroll for support.

The Prime Minister broke with tradition by taking her oath with her hand on the constitution, instead of a holy book, as customary. The new cabinet includes both new and old members.

In the elections, the existing party People's National Movement (PNM) lost after ten years in power and conceded defeat to Keith Rowley, the former Prime Minister. After the results were announced, Persad-Bissessar declared, "If UNC wins, the whole world wins."

orig_title: 2025 Khelo India Youth Games begins, first time in Bihar
text: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the 2025 Khelo India Youth Games (KIYG) on Sunday, praising India's progress in sports. This was the first time the annual event, known as "Play India!" in Hindi, was held in the state of Bihar, where sports for 28 disciplines were spread across five districts and concluded on May 15. Modi emphasized the importance of investments in sports to improve India's future and global influence. It was under his government that the event was first launched in 2018. India's commitment to its indigenous sports was visible during the KIYG, where kho-kho competitions were watched by hundreds of students. The addition of eSports as a demonstration sport added a unique touch to the event, with competitions for video games like Street Fighter 6 and eFootball.

orig_title: Texas authorities announce manhunt after alleged murderer's ankle monitor found in fire
text:
Trevor McEuen, 32, is wanted by the Kaufmann County Sheriff's Office in Texas for murder. Authorities say he removed his ankle monitor, which was part of his bail conditions, and fled from his home on Van Zandt County at 5:33 AM CDT (10:33 UTC) on Monday. The start of McEuen's trial was scheduled for early in the week, although sources disagree on whether it was Monday or Tuesday.

Firefighters discovered McEuen as missing when they put out a fire at his home. Kaufmann County Sheriff Bryan Beavers said he believed McEuen started the fire: "He did that, I think he thought it would burn, but then it didn't." When the fire department arrived and put out the fire, they found McEuen's ankle monitor, his phones, and other belongings, but he was nowhere to be found. Beavers later said he believed McEuen had left the area.

US Marshals are working with Texas authorities to apprehend McEuen, who was released on a $2 million bond. The Kaufmann County Sheriff's Office has a $10,000 reward for information leading to McEuen's arrest. McEuen is accused of killing his neighbor, Aaron Martinez, 35, who was shot multiple times and found dead in his truck in May 2023. The Kaufmann County Sheriff's Office initially said they would not consider the murder a hate crime. Martinez's family and Representative Joaquin Castro are asking prosecutors to bring hate crime charges against McEuen. Castro said at the time: "Three weeks ago, Aaron Martinez was killed by a man who wanted to drive Hispanics out of Kaufman County." McEuen was released from custody but was later arrested in September 2024 after threatening Martinez's uncle on Instagram.

orig_title: Robert Francis Prevost elected as Pope Leo XIV
text:
On May 8, 2025 at 6:07 PM CEST (4:07 PM UTC), white smoke emerged from the chimney of the Sibyllinenkapelle in the Holy See, signaling the emergence of a new pope. He was announced by Cardinal Protodeacon Dominique Mamberti as the 267th pope and has taken the name of Pope Leo XIV. Prevost was previously one of the "front-runners" named as a papal candidate. His openness and engagement for social justice issues of the previous pope Francis, particularly his efforts for social justice, have made him an interesting candidate among his colleagues.

Pope Leo XIV is the second pope from American countries and the first pope from North America, in particular. He is also the first pope from Peru and the first pope with double citizenship. He was born on September 14, 1955 in Chicago, Illinois. He served as bishop of Chiclayo, Peru from 2015 to 2023. Since 2023 he has been the head of the Dicastery for Bishops at the Holy See, which means he is responsible for the selection of priests and the examination of nominations of bishops around the world. He was appointed cardinal by the previous pope Francis in 2024. On February 6, 2025, the previous pope Francis appointed him as archbishop, which gave him the title of the suburbicarian church of Albano.

orig_title: Official White House social media accounts repost AI image of US President Donald Trump dressed like Pope
text: US President Trump posts AI-generated image of himself in bishop's attire that bears resemblance to Pope's clothing, sparking criticism. Trump had posted the image on his Truth-Social account before sharing it on the White House's social media accounts during a period of mourning for the late Pope Francis, who passed away on April 21. The White House denied that the post was intended to offend the Catholic Church.

orig_title: President of Serbia Aleksandar Vučić gets sick, flies home early from US visit
text:
On May 3, Serbian President Aleksandar Vučić attempted to push forward a short visit to the US before he had to return to Serbia and fell ill. He had a short stay in the hospital in Belgrade on Saturday. A doctor explained that his illness was "reliable and unchanged".

Serbian Finance Minister Sinisa Mali told RTS that President Vučić was discharged from the Belgrade Military Medical Center (VMA) at 17:00 (1500 GMT) and told that he felt better.
During his trip to the United States, Vučić suddenly experienced unexpected chest pains. After seeking medical help and undergoing an examination, he decided to cut short his trip and return to Serbia.
Vučić has criticized the western countries for refusing to join sanctions against Russia because of the 2022 invasion of Ukraine, as well as being under pressure due to a fatal accident involving a train's luggage cart at a Novi Sad station in November 2024, which triggered a wave of protests against corruption.

orig_title: Peruvian police locate bodies of security guards allegedly abducted by illegal goldminers
text:
On Sunday, May 4, the police in Peru's Pataz province in the northern region of La Libertad, near one of the largest gold mines in Peru, found the bodies of 13 security personnel who were attacked and killed on Saturday, April 26. The security personnel had worked for R&R Staff, a security company that contracts with Libmar, a craftsman, and Poderosa, the mining firm.

On Friday, May 2, the mining firm La Poderosa ("Powerful" in Spanish) announced that it was disappointed that the police had not taken sufficient action to prevent the illegal mining operation. On Saturday, a video was published on social media that claimed to have been taken by the perpetrators, showing the victims being killed. Videos of the victims were also sent to the families of the victims as part of the extortion. Authorities believe that the perpetrators were connected to the illegal mining operation. The victims were originally enclosed to confront a gang that had taken over the mine and the control. The effort to regain control of the mine was unsuccessful, and the victims were eventually caught and arrested, as reported by BBC.

orig_title: People's Action Party wins Singaporean election in landslide victory
text:
The ruling party People's Action Party (PAP) won a landslide in the 2025 general election in Singapore, taking 65.57% of the national vote and 87 seats in the 97-seat parliament. This marks the 16th consecutive election win for the PAP since 1959.

The main opposition party, the Workers' Party (WP), received 14.99% of the vote — 50.04% in the constituencies it contested — and 12 seats, with 10 directly elected seats supplemented by two additional seats for the "losers," which brought the total to 99 seats.

The election was Singapore's first significant voter-tested test for Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, who took over the position from Lee Hsien Loong on May 15, 2024. The campaign was just nine days long, making it one of the shortest election campaigns in the world, followed by a "cooling-off" period when no campaigning was allowed.

Originally, 97 seats were allocated, but it was reduced to 93 over 18 group representation constituencies (GRCs) and 15 single-member constituencies (SMCs). However, the WP surprised by not winning the Marine Parade-Braddell Heights GRC, which it had won in the last two elections, resulting in the PAP's first majority since 2011.

The PAP has held a majority government since 1959, the longest uninterrupted single-party rule in a modern multi-party system in democracies. In the current parliament, the PAP holds a majority of 83 of the 93 directly elected seats, with 11 additional seats allocated to the "losers" and the PAP nominees.

The last election, held in 2020 under the circumstances of the COVID-19 pandemic, saw the opposition, the WP, enter the parliament for the first time, with the WP winning the new Sengkang GRC.

The election took place under the circumstances of Singapore's 60th Independence Day and global economic difficulties. Singapore's Republic was not spared the impact of the Trump tariffs, which set a minimum quote of 10% for all U.S. purchases.

Singapore is classified as a "democracy failure" by The Economist's Democracy Index.

orig_title: Grand Theft Auto VI release date pushed back until May 2026
text:
Rockstar Games has announced that the release date of Grand Theft Auto VI, the sixth main installment in the Grand Theft Auto series and the sequel to Grand Theft Auto V, has been postponed until May 26, 2026. The original release date was set for Fall 2025.

Rockstar cited that the delay was necessary to deliver a quality that meets the player's expectations. The company apologized for the delay and stated that their goal has always been to exceed player expectations with each new game, and that Grand Theft Auto VI is no exception. The company hopes that players will understand that additional time is needed to deliver a quality that meets their expectations.

Grand Theft Auto VI is expected to be one of the biggest entertainment releases of all time. Despite its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V, being still popular among fans of the series, 11 years after its release.

orig_title: Former guitarist of pioneering death metal band Possessed dies in shootout with San Francisco police
text:
Brian Montana, a former guitarist of the pioneering death metal band Possessed, was shot to death by police in San Francisco on April 28. Montana joined the band in 1983, left in 1984, and was 60 years old when he died.

The shooting lasted about 25 minutes. The claim that the incident started from a dispute with a neighbor over a fallen tree on Arroyo 300 street is not verified. According to reports, Montana fired at the neighbor, and the rounds were aimed at the neighbor's house. Police arrived at the scene after receiving reports of a shooting and found Montana armed with a shotgun and a rifle, shooting at police. Montana used landscape settings and vehicles on the sidewalk to shield himself from the fire, while police took cover behind their cars.

Police eventually managed to subdue Montana, striking him with a bullet. Life-saving measures were taken, and Montana was pronounced dead at the scene. The police confirmed that a resident of the house Montana shot at received a "shotgun wound" and was taken to the hospital. There were no other fatalities or injuries.

Prosecutor Steve Wagstaffe confirmed that alcohol played a role in the incident. He stated: "The victim of Montana's death is a tragedy, but it's fortunate that no one else was injured."

Possessed's lead singer, Jeff Becerra, commented on the band's Instagram: "The Brian I knew came from the time when we were still bachelors, early on Possessed. He was nothing compared to what I read now. In fact, I think that's one of the reasons he left the band. He wasn't ready to be as dark as we were at that time. We wanted a picture of Evil, and Brian was just too easy, and a little bit silly in a good way."

orig_title: Competitive local elections held in England
text:
Local elections were held in England on May 1, 2025, with results showing both Labour Prime Minister Keir Starmer and Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch losing ground, with the Reform UK Party led by Nigel Farage making significant gains. The elections focused mainly on rural areas in England and parliamentary borough elections.

The night began with the election of Reform UK candidate Sarah Pochin to the parliamentary mayor of Runcorn and Helsby in North West England, making her the party's first successful elected female MP. The party also won two new mayors in Lincolnshire and Hull and East Yorkshire.

Later, the results were as follows: Reform UK won strongholds such as Kent and Staffordshire from the Conservatives and County Durham and Doncaster from the Labour Party. Other areas were controlled by the party, with Derbyshire, Lancashire, Lincolnshire, Nottinghamshire and Staffordshire. In total, the party won 677 of over 1,600 council seats in England. Nigel Farage described the results as "unexpected" and said it marked "the end of two-party politics".

It was also a good night for the Liberal Democrats, who came second with 370 seats and took control of three counties: Cambridgeshire, Oxfordshire and Shropshire. They also made significant gains in Devon, Cornwall and Wiltshire.

The Greens had mixed results, with new seats in Gloucestershire and Worcestershire, but finished third in the West-England mayoral election behind Labour and Reform UK.

The Conservatives lost over 600 council seats and all 15 of their controlled councils, with ITV News reporting it as one of the worst results in the party's history. They lost many seats in their heartland areas such as Cambridgeshire, Hertfordshire and Northamptonshire.

Labour leader Keir Starmer described the result as "disappointing", telling ITV News: "I understand it".

orig_title: CSIRO releases 15 captive bred endemic spotted handfish into wild in Tasmania
text:
Scientists from the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO) released 15 juvenile Spotted-Handfish, originally bred at Seahorse World in Tasmania, into the wild in the River Derwent near Hobart. To prepare the critically endangered fish for its new habitat, the researchers provided it with "Hotel" facilities. The researchers had planned to remove the "Hotels" in about two weeks, during which time the researchers would closely monitor the fish, using unique points to identify each individual. The breeding program, supported by the Derwent Estuary Program, began in 2017 and included the establishment of two satellite populations: at Seahorse World and the Melbourne Aquarium.

CSIRO Research Assistant and Project Leader Carlie Devine said: "Today is our first release of juvenile Spotted-Handfish, so we are very excited to set them free. ... It was a long way to figure out how to breed them in captivity. ... It's still a very rare event when they are bred in captivity."

Senior Biologist Rachelle Hawkins stated that the 15 released fish are part of a population of 35, which has been rescued from the aquarium, with the remaining population staying in the aquarium to strengthen the captive population. Hawkins noted that one of the challenges of breeding was determining the sex of the Handfish, which was solved in 2023 when the aquarium used ultrasound waves to determine the sex.

Tasmanian artist Jane Bamford created the artificial incubation structures to which the Handfish laid their eggs. She has since created 7,500 hand-painted ceramic sticks.

Devine said about the "Hotel" facilities: "We will conduct an intensive monitoring program ... We will check the fish and their hotel visits every few days to ensure they are doing well. The fish don't move much, making it easy to find them in the hotels for about two weeks. ... When we remove the hotels, we hope they will venture out and integrate into the wild. We want to make sure they can survive in the wild, as they are very resistant to changes. It's a long process, and this is just one step in our captive breeding program."

orig_title: Ukraine, US reach minerals deal
text:
The US and Ukraine signed a deal on April 30 to provide preferential treatment for US citizens in new Ukrainian trade agreements for rare earth minerals and to create a new fund to attract investors and support Ukraine's reconstruction after the war. The agreement was signed in Washington by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent for the US and Ukraine's First Deputy Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko for Ukraine.

US President Donald Trump proposed the agreement and announced that he expected something in return if he provided military aid to Ukraine. It would give US citizens a preferential treatment in new Ukrainian investments to mine 55 minerals, including Lithium, Titan, Lanthan, Uran, and Cerium, as well as other rare earth and valuable minerals.

The agreement did not include any debt obligations for Ukraine, which was originally proposed but rejected, and the Ukrainian government would still decide which mineral and where to drill. It also did not offer US citizens access to the profits earned by the Ukrainian side.

The Ukrainian side would give up 50% of its future profits from the state assets listed above, while the US citizens would benefit from monetary and military support. The current version, the US-Ukraine Reinvestment Fund, was reached after intense negotiations; an earlier version, which was later rejected by Ukraine, was almost signed before a now-famous dispute between Trump and his Ukrainian counterpart, Volodymyr Zelensky, turned into a conflict between Trump and Zelensky.

The signing of the agreement was publicly praised by both sides - "It clearly shows the commitment of the Trump Administration to a free and sovereign, prosperous Ukraine" - said the White House. "What's important is that the agreement sends a signal to global partners that long-term cooperation with Ukraine - over decades - is not only possible but also reliable", posted Svyrydenko on X.

Svyrydenko hoped that the agreement would bring new support for Ukraine, although the American side did not directly respond to this statement.

The former President and Prime Minister under Vladimir Putin, Dmitry Medvedev, who is currently the Deputy Chairman of the Security Council of the Russian Federation, said: "Trump has forced the Kyiv regime to pay for American help with rare earth minerals. Now they will have to pay for it with the national wealth of a disappearing country, military supplies."

orig_title: Massive power outage hits Spain, Portugal
text:
On Monday, April 28th at 12:33 PM CET (1033 AM UTC), Spain's power grid lost 15 GW, equivalent to about 60% of the country's national demand, within just five seconds. Due to the overload, the power transmission between Spain and France was shut off. As a result, Spain, Portugal, and the French Basque-Länder disconnected from the rest of the European power grid. The cause of the power outage remained unknown.

The system operations manager of Spain's power company REE, Eduardo Prieto, stated in a press conference that "Following this disconnection and the severe energy loss in our power system, our power system collapsed." After the outage, the authorities declared a state of emergency.

Hospitals switched to backup generators, streetlights went out, and the police had to manually control traffic at major intersections. Trains stopped running, between 200 and 500 flights were canceled due to the need for backup generators at airports, and over 50 million people were ordered to stay home, with long lines forming at bus stops and no metro or train service. According to the leader of the regional government, the emergency services in Madrid received 286 calls to help people stuck in elevators. Marina Sierra, a young woman in a Madrid surprise area, said, "Our building suddenly started smoking, and they had to rush in quickly." After the school was closed, ABC News reported that in Australia.

Joanly Perez, a doctor in Madrid, said, "I went to work and the power went out suddenly, and people started buying things... People are not sure what's happening, and they're buying basics just in case." With the payment systems not functioning, shops that were still open switched to cash transactions, and many stores closed due to the lack of electricity.

The French power operator RTE restored electricity in the French Basque-Länder within a few hours after the outage and helped restore Spain's power grid. Spain had regained over 92% of its power supply by Tuesday morning, after the Spanish power company Red Eléctrica reported, and Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez promised that every light in Spain would be restored by Wednesday.

The Minister for Housing, Transportation, and Infrastructure in Madrid, Jorge Rodrigo Dominguez, announced that the majority of the metro lines, except for Line 7A, would resume operation by 8:00 AM CET (0600 AM UTC) on Tuesday morning. "This is thanks to the hard work of underground workers who made everything in their power to restore the main infrastructure for the people of Madrid as quickly as possible." He expressed his "deepest gratitude" for the dedication shown by the workers once again in an extraordinary and unpredictable situation.
