orig_title: Local South Carolinian police places male suspect of three injuries into custody after manhunt
text:
A comprehensive search operation was conducted in Sullivans Island, South Carolina, after a driver struck two children and an adult while walking past Sunrise Presbyterian Church at approximately 13:00 EDT (17:00 UTC) on May 1, 2025. After hours of searching, the police found the perpetrator, Justin Collin Adams, on a boat in a nearby coastal town and took him into custody. The authorities accused him of running over the victims in the church parking lot before fleeing on foot, reportedly with a knife, and attacking the victims in the church's swing set while on the boat en route to the beach.

Many police agencies, including the FBI, U.S. Marshals, and local police departments, worked together in an intense search operation. Their efforts included checking for quadruplets, searching homes, lifting drones, and setting up checkpoints at the main access points of the island. Residents were ordered to seek shelter in their homes while the search was underway.

The authorities found Adams, described as a heavy, medieval-looking white man with a bald head and beard, wearing a red sweater and shorts, and took him into custody later that day on a boat. The authorities sealed off the crime scene and later confirmed that the area was safe.

The adult and one of the children were taken to the hospital and were in stable condition, while the other child received treatment on the scene and was returned to their family. The investigators were still working to determine if the incident was intentional, although initial reports suggested that it was an intentional act.

orig_title: Man drives into group of seven schoolchildren in Osaka, Japan
text:
Police arrested a 28-year-old man from Tokyo, Japan, and took him into custody after allegedly intentionally driving his car into a group of seven young students from a elementary school on Thursday. The traffic crime occurred at 13:35 local time in Osakas Nishinari-Ward.

Of the seven injured children, a 7-year-old girl suffered a broken jaw and was severely injured, while the other six boys sustained light injuries. A witness reported that the car seemed to swing as it hit the children; one girl was severely injured and bleeding, while the others had only light cuts.

The man told the police that he was "sick and tired of everything" and then drove his car into the children to kill them. "I was tired of everything, so I decided to kill the people by driving my car into multiple elementary school students," a police officer quoted the man.

orig_title: Liberal government re-elected in Canada following election
text:
Canada's Liberal Party won the Canadian federal election of 2025, as explained by statements from two major parties. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney was elected to a full term and formed a minority government. He replaced Justin Trudeau as prime minister in March and called an early election. The Liberals won 169 seats, three less than the majority in the House of Commons, more than the opposition party Conservative, which won 144 seats.

In his victory speech, Carney said: "As I warned monthly, America wants our land, our resources, our water, our nation. But these are no empty threats. President Trump is trying to break us so America can own us... This will never happen." Conservative Party of Canada leader Pierre Poilievre lost his own seats to Liberal candidate Bruce Fanjoy. New Democratic Party leader Jagmeet Singh also lost his seat.

In the election, 17% of seats changed party. Voter turnout was 67%, the highest in ten years. There were still further ballot recounts to confirm the results fully.

orig_title: Child defaces abstract painting by Mark Rothko worth tens of millions on display in Dutch museum
text:
A painting by late abstract artist Mark Rothko, titled "Grey, Orange on Maroon, No. 8," was damaged by a child during a "dangerous moment" in a Dutch museum on Monday. The 1960 painting, described by curator Saskia van Kampen-Prein as a "meditative and impressive color landscape," is valued at "tens of millions of dollars." 

The museum representative explained that after the child touched the painting, "superficial damage" occurred, as the child's clothing transferred the unremovable color, creating "small scratches" that were visible. The representative stated that the museum sought the advice of "conservative experts" from across the Netherlands and abroad to conduct research on the painting's restoration. The representative said that the painting would be returned to the exhibit after restoration. 

Sophie McAloone, a conservator at Fine Art Restoration Company, said that paintings like "No. 8" are particularly prone to damage due to factors such as the complexity of the materials used and the lack of a traditional protective coating. McAloone noted that the damage to the top layer of the paint could significantly affect the piece's appearance. 

Jonny Helm, a marketing manager, stated that Rothko's connections to colors, resins, and adhesives were "much more complex." He argued that it was "no first case" that a Rothko was damaged. "Black on Maroon," another work by Rothko, was vandalized by a person, Wlodzimierz Umaniec, in a London gallery in 2012. 

The museum identified the person responsible for damaging the painting but did not disclose who was financially responsible for the restoration or the associated costs. The museum also declined to share photos of the damage.

orig_title: Stunt pilot Rob Holland dies after crashing experimental aircraft
text:
Aerobatic pilot Rob Holland, 50, died in a crash of his experimental aircraft MXS at the Langley Air Force Base in Hampton, Virginia, USA, on Thursday. 

The news on Rob Holland's official Facebook and Instagram pages reads: "It is with the heaviest hearts that I must share that Rob Holland passed away today, April 24, 2025, in an accident at the Langley AFB, VA. The cause of the crash is currently unknown and is being investigated by the FAA, NTSB, and the DOD."

The head of the investigation into the National Transportation Safety Board, Dan Boggs, stated that there were no aerobatic maneuvers involved in the crash and that Holland was trying to make a "normal landing".

Before his death, Rob Holland was scheduled to perform at the Air Power Over Hampton Roads-Airshow on Saturday, April 26.

orig_title: Streaming platform Twitch bans rapper Kanye West seven minutes into first stream for performing "Nazi salute"
text: Kanye West's Twitch Channel Was Shut Down After He Made a Nazi Salute and Asked Followers to Wear Swastikas During a Live Stream. The channel was shut down just seven minutes after it went live, citing that West broke Twitch's community guidelines and terms of service. Despite the channel being shut down, the video spread to millions of views on other social media platforms like YouTube. The incident came a month after West posted a video where he discussed his friendship with known racist Nick Fuentes, who he called a "white supremacist." The two had dinner together at the home of former US President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago in 2022, sparking widespread criticism.

orig_title: Russian Lieutenant General Yaroslav Moskalik dies in car bombing assassination in Moscow
text: Russian Lieutenant General Yaroslav Moskalik was killed in a bomb explosion in Balaschikha, a town east of Moscow, on Friday, April 25, confirmed the Russian Investigation Committee. According to local media reports, Moskalik, while walking on the street outside his house, was detonated by a homemade, improvised device. Videos showing a car on fire in front of several buildings were posted on social media. A second, unseen victim was also killed. A Ukrainian special operations agent was suspected of carrying out the attack by Russian authorities. The alleged perpetrator was reportedly rewarded with $15,000 for the attack, which was planned for September 2024. The murder follows a string of similar deaths of high-profile individuals linked to the Russian regime, including military blogger Vladlen Tatarsky in April 2023 and Lieutenant General Igor Kirillov in December of the previous year. On the same day, US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff held talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin to discuss a possible end to the war.

orig_title: Los Angeles Police release body cam footage of armed standoff between officers and wife of Weezer bassist
text:
The Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD) released a camera footage on Friday of an incident on April 8, when Jillian Lauren, a writer and wife of Weezer bassist Scott Shriner, was shot, arrested and charged with attempted murder. 

During a police search in April, after a car was run over, a large number of police officers in the Eagle Rock area called off the police and Lauren was arrested with a 9mm pistol. Lauren pulled the pistol and the police demanded it, but she refused to give it up. She was suspected of being involved in the accident. 

Lauren allegedly opened fire on one of the accident's perpetrator and aimed the pistol at the police. The police replied with at least eight shots. Lauren was hit twice in the shoulder and retreated to her house. She claimed to be defending herself against the accident's perpetrator. Hours later, Lauren came out with someone identified as her babysitter. Both were arrested. Lauren received "non-life-threatening" injuries and was released from the police station after paying a $1 million fine. She will appear in court on April 30. A police spokesperson said that they will analyze the film, forensic evidence, and police protocol to determine if the police tactics, showing the weapon and applying lethal force, conform to the police policy.

orig_title: Indian government bans 16 Pakistani YouTube channels in India
text:
On Monday, April 28, the Indian government has banned the sighting of 16 YouTube channels in Pakistan, due to concerns over the content they have, which has been described as inflammatory and sensitive, particularly in relation to a recent attack on tourists in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir. The government has also issued a warning to the BBC.

According to a report, the decision was made based on a recommendation from the Union Home Ministry. The banned channels have a combined total of around 63 million subscribers, including major Pakistani news outlets such as Dawn, Sama TV, ARY News, Bol News, Raftar, Geo News, and Suno News. YouTube channels run by journalists Irshad Bhatti, Asma Shirazi, Umar Cheema, and Muneeb Farooq have also been banned. Other channels mentioned in the ban include Pakistan Reference, Sama Sports, Uzair Cricket, and Raji Nama.

Officials have so far not specified the exact content of the channels, but emphasized that the measures comply with the rules for digital content and national security concerns.

orig_title: Explosion in Iran's largest port, Shahid Rajaee, heard 50 km away, leaves dozens killed, thousands injured
text: A blast at the Shahid Rajaee Port in Bandar Abbas, Iran, killed at least 40 people and injured over 1,000, according to the Red Cross Society. The explosion, which was heard up to 31 miles away, destroyed windows in nearby office buildings, with photos showing scattered metal pieces and collapsed roofs. At least one roof was crushed. Reports of people trapped under collapsed walls. A fire before the explosion was described as a "giant fire" and a witness said it spread quickly before the explosion. A crisis management official said the disaster was caused by the explosion of several containers storing chemicals in the Shahid Rajaee Port area, likely containing hazardous materials. A private maritime risk company, Ambrey Intelligence, said the fire was caused by "inadequate handling of a load of solid fuel intended for use in Iranian ballistic rockets". The load of sodium perchlorate rocket fuel was delivered to the port in March 2025, the Financial Times reported. Ambrey said Iran's National Organization for Disaster Management had warned the port about the safety of the chemical storage before. The fire burned for a day after the accident and was described as a "thick column of thick, black smoke". Rescue efforts are underway, with helicopters deployed to fight the flames.

orig_title: Iran and United States schedule fourth round of talks
text: On Saturday, April 26, an Iranian delegation led by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met a US delegation led by US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff in Muscat, the capital of Oman, as part of the third round of negotiations for about six hours. Omani diplomats acted as mediators. The high-level talks were in line with the technical talks, which were originally scheduled for Thursday morning but were moved to Saturday. The Iranian delegation was led by Majid Takht-Ravanchi and Kazem Gharibabadi, while the US delegation was led by Michael Anton. After the talks, Abbas Araghchi said: "During the latest round of talks, we have answered the questions of the other side and the atmosphere was completely serious and focused on work. ... It was agreed that further checks would be carried out in the capitals before the next meeting to identify ways to close the gaps." Oman's Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr al-Busaidi subsequently commented that the talks signaled a shared aspiration to reach a unification agreement based on mutual respect and lasting bonds. A high-ranking official from the US administration described the talks as productive and positive, saying: "There is still much to be done, but progress was made to reach an agreement" and that both sides agreed to meet again in Europe soon. Before this round of talks, Abbas Araghchi had signed a book signing act for his book "The Power of Negotiation" at the Dar Luban Hall on April 29, Muscat International Book Fair. The exhibition includes Iran's pavilion, which was organized by Iran Book and Literature House together with the cultural representative office in Oman. The next round of talks, both high-level and technical, was provisionally scheduled for May 3 and would take place again in Muscat, Oman.

orig_title: Luigi Mangione pleads not guilty to federal charges involving murder of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson
text: On Friday, Luigi Mangione, the suspect in the murder case of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson, appeared in court in Lower Manhattan, where he pleaded guilty to the crime. Mangione's guilty plea came on the same day as federal prosecutors officially requested the death penalty for Thompson's murder. The charges were murder and stalking. The prosecution believed the murder was intended to "strengthen an ideological message". US Attorney General Pam Bondi, who had previously advocated for Mangione's execution, believed the murder was politically motivated. Mangione's defense team had described the execution as "barbaric". Some of Mangione's supporters gathered outside the courthouse, with some viewing him as a "people's hero" as the supporters of the US healthcare system were widely disappointed. Reports indicate that Mangione's defense fund has received over $1 million in donations.

orig_title: Lion mauls, kills teenage girl in Kenya
text: On Saturday, April 19, a female lioness killed a 14-year-old girl on a ranch south of Nairobi National Park in Nairobi, Kenya, according to the Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS). The attack took place in the girl's own home. Another youth present at the time reported that the lioness had stolen the girl before alerting others. Authorities confirmed that there was no evidence that the attack was provoked. It was assumed that the lioness was drawn to the area due to food scarcity and crossed the "insufficient" fence. KWS Rangers and search teams were quickly mobilized and followed a blood trail that led to the Mbagathi River, where the girl's body was found. She had injuries to her lower back. By Friday, the lioness had not yet been found. Authorities set traps and thoroughly searched the area to locate the lioness. Attacks by lions on humans are rare in Africa, especially without livestock involvement. KWS officials announced that discussions were held to strengthen "security measures" to prevent similar incidents in the future. In a separate incident, a 54-year-old man was killed by an elephant in Nyeri County, Kenya, according to KWS.

orig_title: United States: Baltimore federal grand jury indict man of international conspiracy in Cameroon, Central Africa
text:
A federal grand jury in Baltimore, USA, indicted a Marylander named "The Garri Master" on Friday on alleged conspiracy to provide material support for armed separatist groups in Cameroon, Africa, according to the US Department of Justice. The indictment alleged that the man called for Tatasw in response to alleged attacks on civilian population in Cameroon and provided financial support for the operations. The indictment alleged that he was involved in a conspiracy that included murder, kidnapping, and civilian casualties, which underscored the US commitment to international pursuit of justice that originated from the US.

Federal prosecutors claimed that Tatasw provided resources and made threatening communications to harm or kidnap civilians in Cameroon. 

Tatasw was arrested and feared a conviction in federal court and a significant prison sentence for his alleged contribution to the escalation of violence abroad.

The case highlighted the role of diaspora activists in the ongoing Anglophone conflict in Cameroon, where separatist groups rely on foreign support since the escalation of the conflict in 2017. Tatasw's arrest followed broader efforts by US and Cameroonian authorities to allow financial and logistical support to armed groups in the region from the diaspora.

orig_title: Police recover remains of man killed in first fatal shark attack in history of Israel
text:
Police on Wednesday said they had found the remains of a man, Barak Tzach, 40, who was attacked and killed by a shark at the Olga Beach in northern Israel on Monday. The victim was a father of four children. The shark attack was the first fatal shark attack in Israel since its founding in 1948 and the fourth overall; the first shark attack in the area was a fatal one in the 1940s.

Tzach's remains were found at the same location where the attack occurred, after a two-day search operation; the beach was immediately closed after the attack.

Witnesses at the Olga Beach, including some who were on vacation, saw the incident and filmed it, posting it on social media. "I was in the water, I saw blood and there were screams. It's frightening. We were here yesterday and saw the sharks in a circle."

The red-listed shark (Carcharhinus obscurus) and the sandbar shark (Carcharhinus leucas) are reported, but these areas have been frequented for decades, especially in winter - possibly due to the warm water released from the Orot Rabin power plant in Hadera. Tzach's wife believes that his intention was to film and document the sea, not to disturb the sharks.

orig_title: Iran and US plan meetings of technical experts after second round of negotiations
text:
On Saturday, April 19, the second round of talks between an Iranian delegation led by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and a US delegation led by US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff took place in Rome, Italy. The delegations sat in separate rooms for over four hours, while Oman-based mediators transmitted documents between the parties during the indirect negotiations.

Iran's Foreign Minister said: "It was a good discussion with the talks progressing," and confirmed that the next round of high-level talks with the US, planned for April 26 in Muscat, Oman's capital, would take place after technical discussions on an expert level on Wednesday, April 23, also in Oman.

Oman's Foreign Minister Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi released a statement on social media, praising Araghchi and Witkoff for their "high-level approach" and saying: "These talks are gaining speed and even what seemed impossible is now possible."

Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said: "The Italian government hopes to find a positive solution for the Middle East together," after meeting Araghchi in Rome before the second round of talks.

A senior official from the Donald Trump administration told CNN: "Today, in Rome, over four hours in our second round of talks, we made very good progress in our direct and indirect discussions."

orig_title: Man arrested after driving wrong way on Interstate 93 in New Hampshire
text:
A man from Lowell, Massachusetts, was arrested on Monday after driving the wrong way on a road in New Hampshire on Sunday night at 11 pm, heading in the wrong direction near Exit 34C in Franconia Notch.

According to the state police, the man was near Exit 39 and was heading towards the police. The first attempts to pass him were unsuccessful. The police soon noticed another vehicle, traveling south and directly in the path of the man's vehicle. The southern vehicle managed to get out of the way. A short time later, the man was pulled over into the side of the road, where he was apprehended by the police.

The man is charged with reckless endangerment, driving after being suspended or canceling the driver's license, and a third charge of drug trafficking and violating a police officer. The man is being held in custody and has been set for a later trial in the Littleton District Court, according to the state police.

orig_title: Researchers film colossal squid in its natural habitat for the first time
text:
Scientists at the University of Essex, England, reported on Wednesday, April 16, that they had captured the first-ever footage of a colossal squid, a member of the glass spider family (Cranchiidae), at great depths in the ocean. The observation of a 30-centimeter young squid was made on March 9 near the uninhabited South Sandwich Islands, a part of the British overseas territories in the South Atlantic. The researchers obtained the footage about 600 meters below the ocean surface.

The observation marked the 100th year since the official recognition and naming of the colossal squid. The remotely operated vehicle (ROV) SuBastian, which took the photos and videos, was provided by the Schmidt Ocean Institute's research vessel Falkor. It was part of a 35-day ocean statistics flaggship expedition, which was searching for new marine species.

According to the Schmidt Ocean Institute, the 35-day voyage on board the R/V Falkor was part of an international effort to discover new marine species. The expedition brought together researchers from several institutions and initiatives, including the Ocean Statistics Project and GoSouth, with Dr. Michelle Taylor from the University of Essex leading the scientific team. Dr. Taylor said, "It's incredible that we can utilize the potential of the taxonomic community through Falkor's telepresence while we're underwater."

Deep-sea researcher Kat Bolstad from the Auckland University of Technology, who did not participate in the expedition, helped with the identification of the species shown in the footage. "We finally have conclusive footage of this species, which we've been studying and dreaming about for years."

orig_title: Pope Francis dies at age 88
text: Pope Francis (born Jorge Mario Bergoglio) died at the age of 88 on April 21, 2025, at 7:35 am local time in Vatican City after a five-week hospital stay where he was battling an respiratory infection and double lung inflammation. The official cause of his death was a stroke that turned into an irreversible heart stop. The day before his death, he held an Easter Mass, Easter prayer, and called for an end to global conflicts, such as in Ukraine, Gaza, and Sudan. He also met with US Vice President JD Vance. He died at the Casa Santa Marta House, where a statement from Cardinal Kevin Farrell said: "Dear brothers and sisters, with deep sorrow I have to inform you that our Holy Father Francis has passed away. At 7:35 am in the morning, the Bishop of Rome, Francis, returned to the House of the Father. His entire life has been dedicated to the service of the Lord and the Church. He rejected the values of the Evangelium with faith-filled, courageous, and universal love, especially in the interest of the poor and marginalized. With infinite gratitude for his example as a true student of Lord Jesus Christ, we ask for permission to allow the spirit of Pope Francis to enter the infinite, merciful and loving life of the One and Three God." After his wish, Francis will be buried in the Basilica of St. Mary Magdalene in Rome.

orig_title: Baseball: Cincinnati Reds win against Baltimore Orioles
text:
The Cincinnati Reds beat the Baltimore Orioles 8-3 in the American Major League Baseball game at Oriole Park at Camden Yards in Baltimore, Maryland on Friday evening. The result was 8-3.

Three home runs by Elly De La Cruz and Matt McLain helped the Reds defeat the Orioles.

De La Cruz entered the game in the upper half of the third inning. With two outs and two runners on base, the Cincinnati Reds were trailing the Baltimore Orioles 1-0.

De La Cruz hit a ball off Orioles pitcher Cade Povich with the first pitch and hit the ball into the middle field. He reached the edge of the stands and went very high into the air. The umpires declared a home run.

Andrew Abbott pitched in the game (2-0, with an ERA of 1.64) and struck out 11 batters, allowing only one walk and three of the 21 runners who reached the field.

orig_title: Several tourists die in cable car crash in south of Naples, Italy
text:
On April 17, a cable car accident occurred in southern Italy on Mount Faito, south of Naples, resulting in the deaths of four tourists. One person was "very severely injured" and had to be airlifted to a hospital for treatment.

According to local media reports, the cable car was located near the summit of the mountain when one of its support cables snapped and broke. Another cable car was also located in the same stretch, although all passengers were successfully rescued during the accident.

The difficulties in rescue efforts were exacerbated by the poor weather conditions, including fog, wind, and rain, as passengers had to be evacuated one by one using the help of ropes.
The system was opened in 1952 and is an Aerial tramway system, starting from Castellammare di Stabbia and a 3km route including a 1km ascent to the summit of the mountain.

orig_title: Several suspects dead in South Africa after shootout results in the rescue of abducted US pastor
text:
Three suspects killed in shootout during rescue of US pastor Josh Sullivan in South Africa. A "high-intensity" shootout took place during the rescue of US pastor Josh Sullivan, who was abducted from his church in Gqeberha, East Cape, South Africa, last Wednesday. He was rescued again in the same geographic area where he was abducted last Wednesday. After his rescue, his condition was described as "wonderfully unharmed" by authorities.

The elite unit of the South African police, known as Hawks, was involved in the investigation. According to authorities, the rescue operation was a "confirmed lead" in which a coordinated team quickly moved to the identified address. When authorities approached the address believed to be Sullivan's home, the suspects tried to escape in their car and opened fire on the authorities. "The officers responded with tactical precision, which led to a high-intensity shootout in which three unknown suspects were killed," said the Hawks spokesperson, Avele Fumba. Sullivan was safely extracted from the vehicle, and a subsequent medical examination found that he was in "excellent condition" again.

Four armed men had abducted a religious preacher on Thursday, April 10, who led Sullivan's church, and had taken him on the way to him with a gun. They had escaped in their own car. It was assumed that the perpetrators had been watching Sullivan's family, as they were obviously familiar with Sullivan's name, explained witness Jeremy Hall. The Sullivan's car was found nearby, although Sullivan was nowhere to be found.

Sullivan describes himself as a "church planting missionary". He and his family moved to South Africa in 2018 from Tennessee. His wife and six children were among the witnesses of his abduction.

South Africa has seen a rise in gang activity and illegal arms trafficking in recent years, with a number of similar abductions and gun violence cases that have been attributed to poverty and inequality.

orig_title: Protester tasered and arrested at town hall hosted by US Republican congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene
text:
On Tuesday evening, a protester was arrested by police using a Taser. The incident occurred at a Town Hall event in Acworth, Georgia, held by Republican U.S. Congresswoman Marjorie Taylor Greene. Police were present at the event. Video footage showed participants in the crowd cheering as the protester was removed from the premises by police.

According to eyewitnesses, disturbances began only minutes after Greene entered the building. Some additional attendees were also removed from the area, with some being arrested.

Some see Greene as a controversial figure in U.S. politics. The congresswoman was urged by congressional superiors not to hold any Town Hall events. During the Town Hall event, participants shouted against Greene, although she did not address them. The congresswoman claimed that the police handled the situation appropriately, and also alleged that the Democratic Party was behind the disturbances at her Town Hall event, although these claims were unverified. She described the dissents as "fabricated".

orig_title: US Health Secretary vows to determine cause of autism by September
text:
US-Verteidigungsminister Robert F. Kennedy Jr. kündigte eine neue Initiative zur Ermittlung der Ursache für Autismus an, die bis September 2025 abgeschlossen sein soll. Die Ankündigung wurde während einer übertragenen Regierungskonferenz mit US-Präsident Donald Trump gemacht, bei der Kennedy ein "massives Forschungs- und Prüfungsprogramm" beschrieb, das von Hunderten Wissenschaftlern weltweit durchgeführt werden soll. Ziel war es, mögliche Umwelt-, Ernährungs- oder medizinische Ursachen für Autismus zu entdecken, einschließlich der umstrittenen und weit verbreiteten Theorie, dass Impfungen mit dem Entstehens des Entwicklungsstörungsbildes in Verbindung stehen.

Trump antwortete darauf, dass es "da sein muss, etwas Künstliches da draußen, das das tut. Wenn Sie eine Antwort darauf finden können, wo Sie damit aufhören, etwas essen oder vielleicht ein Schuss. Aber etwas tut das."

Kennedy, wenn er von Fox News befragt wurde, behauptete, dass das Programm eine umfassende Studie umfassen würde, "Wir werden Impfungen in Betracht ziehen, aber wir werden alles überprüfen. Alles ist auf dem Tisch, unsere Lebensmittelkette, unser Wasser, unsere Luft, verschiedene Parental-Methoden, alle Arten von Veränderungen, die zu diesem Ausbruch geführt haben könnten."

Das Konzept hat Kritik von führenden Autismus-Unterstützungsgruppen und Wissenschaftlern ausgelöst, die behaupten, dass die Frist unrealistisch ist und die Forschungsprämisse fehlerhaft ist. Kritiker werfen vor, dass Kennedys Berufung von David Geier - einem Anti-Impfungsaktivisten, der zuvor wegen der Ausübung von Medizin ohne Lizenz bestraft wurde - ein untröstliches Zeichen für die Richtung des Projekts ist. Darüber hinaus hat das Konzept ohne Eingabe von etablierten Autismusorganisationen wie der Autism Society of America stattgefunden, deren Präsident das Konzept als "schädlich, irreführend und unrealistisch" bezeichnet hat. Berichte deuten darauf hin, dass es keinen Budget oder einen transparenten Dokument über die Durchführung der Forschung zu den Ursachen von Autismus gab.

Die wissenschaftliche Konsens ablehnt die Theorie, dass Impfungen Autismus verursachen - eine Idee, die ursprünglich aus einer 1998 veröffentlichten Studie von Andrew Wakefield stammt, die später aufgrund von Fälschungen und ethischen Verstößen zurückgezogen wurde. Autismus ist ein komplexes neuroentwicklungsbezogenes Zustand, der von genetischen und Umweltfaktoren beeinflusst wird, wobei mögliche Verbindungen zu vorherigen Exponenzen, Muttergesundheit und Elterngrenze bestehen. Während Diagnosezahlen in den letzten Jahrzehnten gestiegen sind, wird berichtet, dass ein Teil des Anstiegs auf eine Erweiterung der Diagnosekriterien und eine verbesserte Aufmerksamkeit zurückzuführen ist, nicht nur auf eine Zunahme der Diagnose.

orig_title: Sandstorm in Iraq leaves thousands hospitalised
text:
On Monday, April 14, 2025, over 3,500 people in Iraq were hospitalized due to respiratory problems caused by a severe sandstorm, the worst of the year so far. The sandstorm cast a thick "orange haze" over the clouds, reducing visibility to just hundreds of meters, and in some cases even less. Authorities closed the airports in the provinces of Najaf and Basra.

Weather forecasts indicated that conditions would improve gradually starting from Tuesday, according to predictions by local weather services.

The United Nations has identified Iraq as one of the five countries most vulnerable to the greatest threats of climate change, which allegedly led to recurring sandstorms, intense heat periods, and water damage in the country.

The most recent severe sandstorm in Iraq occurred in 2022, which resulted in a fatality and treatment for over 5,000 people with respiratory problems.
